feature_name: Survivorship-free stock universe and point-in-time ST history
feature_description: stock_basic and namechange wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-005's dataset (2), plus the StockUniverse and NameHistory contracts that turn them into answers. The universe answers 'which securities were listed on day D' without survivorship: stock_basic returns list_status='L' when asked nothing, and a live probe on 2026-08-08 measured what that costs -- 5,539 listed rows against 5,878 for list_status='L,D' (339 delisted, 0 suspended), which on 2019-06-28 is 3,404 names against the 3,631 actually listed, 227 missing and every one of them delisted afterwards. A registry row is split into one panel row per lifecycle event, because a listing and a delisting cannot share an available_time: dating the row at the listing leaks a 2024 termination to a 2019 reader, and dating it at the termination hides the security from every earlier as_of. delist_date is exclusive, measured against Tushare's own daily bars on a random sample of 40 of the 339 delisted securities plus 15 named cases picked to break it (zero bars fall on or after it in any of them), so membership is listed_on <= day < delisted_on. ListingStatus is four-valued (not_yet_listed / listed / delisted / beyond_snapshot) and raises on bool(); is_listed() raises rather than answering False past the snapshot. NameHistory answers 'what was it called on day D' and 'was it ST' from namechange's two clocks, kept apart: ann_date is availability, start_date is effect, and 000001.SZ was announced 平安银行 on 2012-01-20 and became it on 2012-08-02. RiskWarning is five-valued and read from the name using the real historical prefix grammar, which the obvious startswith(('ST','*ST')) gets wrong on 237 of the corpus's records -- 235 share-reform forms plus the two pre-2020 ChiNext names that wore 退市风险警示 as a bare * with no ST behind it.
notes: V2-P1-005 (PRD Story S10; roadmap section 6 dataset 2; depends on V2-P1-004; depended on by V2-P1-009/010/012/017). Every number below is from a live probe of the real endpoints on 2026-08-08; none of it is asserted against the network -- the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) SURVIVORSHIP. stock_basic defaults to list_status='L' (the bare request, list_status='' and exchange='SSE' all return only listed rows), so the default query is the survivorship bug. list_status='L,D' returns 5,878 = 5,539 L + 339 D in one call ('LD' and 'L|D' both return zero rows, so the comma is the accepted separator and not lucky parsing). offset=300 leaves 39 rows, so 339 is the endpoint's whole delisted set rather than a page. The per-year census (1 in 1999, 3 in 2001, 46 in 2022, 45 in 2023, 52 in 2024) tracks the public record and the earliest entry is 1999-07-12, which is in fact the first A-share termination. That is evidence of completeness, not proof, and it is carried as data: KNOWN_UNIVERSE_LIMITATIONS names six measured boundaries (A-shares only -- zero B-share codes in either half; terminations only back to the first recorded one; suspension invisible; no announcement clock; the snapshot has no as_of; ts_code is not a permanent security identity -- 000024.SZ vs 001979.SZ, the non-standard T600018.SH, and five namechange codes the registry does not have including two withdrawn IPOs), and UniverseCompleteness reports them next to the counts a particular read actually saw. (2) THE DEFAULT FIELD SET HAS NO delist_date -- ts_code, symbol, name, area, industry, cnspell, market, list_date, act_name, act_ent_type -- so the descriptor sends an explicit fields list. (3) THE ROW SPLIT is forced rather than chosen: one available_time per row is either early enough to leak the delisting or late enough to reintroduce survivorship, so _stock_lifecycle_panel_rows emits one row per lifecycle event and the existing point-in-time filter does the rest. (4) delist_date IS EXCLUSIVE, measured: across a random sample of 40 of the 339 delisted securities plus 15 named cases picked to break it (absorption mergers 000024.SZ, code migrations T600018.SH, the PT era 000003.SZ, the share-reform B-share codes 600286.SH/600205.SH) ZERO bars fall on or after delist_date; list_date is inclusive because the first bar falls on it (checked on four codes short enough that daily's 6,000-row cap does not truncate their history). A REVIEW CORRECTION: the first version of this row also claimed the last bar is the PREVIOUS SESSION, from a sample of seven post-2014 names that had all traded through their 退市整理期. That is false and the sample was biased -- in the random 40 only 13 have their last bar on the previous session, 600286.SH stopped trading 260 sessions before its termination, 000024.SZ 15 sessions before, and T600018.SH has no daily bars at all. Only the exclusive bound is claimed now, and only the exclusive bound is what the contract needs; the gap is a suspension, which KNOWN_UNIVERSE_LIMITATIONS.suspension_invisible already names. All 52 of 2024's delistings and all 100 of its listings fall on SSE open days. (5) available_time IS THE EVENT'S OWN MIDNIGHT and the docstring claims only what it can defend: stock_basic carries no announcement column at all, both events are announced in advance (the 上市公告书, the 退市整理期) and by how much is not derivable here, so the bound stated is the checkable one -- a question asked at midnight on day D gets the membership day D's session actually had. The residual is named as KNOWN_UNIVERSE_LIMITATIONS.announcement_clock_absent rather than argued away, the same shape KNOWN_CALENDAR_LOOKAHEAD set. (6) THE REGISTRY'S DESCRIPTIVE COLUMNS ARE NOT STORED. name/industry/area/market/act_name have no history and no clock; the registry calls 000005.SZ 'ST星源(退)' today and stamping that on its 1990-12-10 listing row would be a 34-year look-ahead. The name on a day is namechange's answer. (7) NAMECHANGE'S TWO CLOCKS ARE NEVER MERGED. ann_date is availability and start_date is effect; across all 14,166 rows 6,150 coincide and zero have the announcement after the effect (measured, not depended on). name_on() answers from the effect, pending_at() from the announcement, announced_by() is the point-in-time filter -- so at 2012-03-01 the name is 深发展A and the rename to 平安银行 is simultaneously visible as announced-but-not-in-force. (8) end_date IS A WITNESS, NOT A COLUMN. It is None on 5,882 rows and that means 'in effect', not 'missing' (a review correction: the earlier 5,891 came from the paginated pull this same row declares unsound, which double-counts 380 duplicated records); it is derivable from the successor's start_date and, unlike the successor, is gated by no announcement, so storing it would put an unannounced future rename on the record currently in effect. The tests cross-check it instead, the treatment pretrade_date already gets. A recorded disagreement: for a delisted security the final record never closes -- 000003.SZ was terminated 2002-06-14 and namechange still answers 'PT金田A' for 2026 while the registry says 'PT金田A(退)'. That is not reconciled; stock_universe.py is the other half. (9) THE ST GRAMMAR, WRONG IN TWO PLACES AND CORRECTED IN ONE OF THEM BY REVIEW. The share-reform era put G/S in front of the ST marker, so risk_warning_of strips a leading S or G only when ST or *ST follows; the naive startswith(('ST','*ST')) marks 2,592 rows where the reform-aware rule marks 2,827 -- 235 genuinely special-treated names reading as ordinary, with zero false positives, which is why the gap survives review. The SECOND way it was wrong survived this task's own review of itself: before 2020 创业板 ran no ST regime and 退市风险警示 was a BARE * prefix with nothing behind it, so 300372.SZ ('*欣泰', 2016-07-12..2016-08-22) and 300028.SZ ('*金亚', 2018-06-27..2018-08-07) -- the corpus's only two names that start with * and are not *ST, both carrying change_reason='高风险警示' -- were answered RiskWarning.none. Both securities were terminated afterwards (欣泰退 2017-08-28, 金亚退 2020-08-03), so those were the two windows an ST filter most needed. The test is now on the marker * rather than the literal *ST, which takes the strict rule to 2,829 rows, and the state is RiskWarning.star_st rather than a sixth member because it is the same warning the main board spells *ST. The reverse mistake and its number were also misdescribed: reading a bare leading S/G as a warning marker in its own right would mismark 1,210 rows (S深发展A, G上港), while stripping the letter unconditionally and then looking for ST marks 1,708 rows with zero false positives but loses ST天龙, which becomes T天龙. change_reason is NOT used to derive the state, because a transition can land on another marked state (16 rows carry 撤销PT and 8 of them produce a name that is still marked -- ST吉轻工, ST振新, ST琼华侨, ST东海A, ST闽闽东, ST永久, ST凯地, ST红光; the first version of this row said nine). It is the independent witness instead, and the witness is what found the ChiNext gap -- the earlier 'zero rows have an ST-imposing reason on an ordinary name' was an unbounded claim whose scan omitted 高风险警示, so it could never meet its own counterexample. What is claimed now is bounded: across THIS 14,166-row corpus and ITS fifteen reason values, the eight imposing ones (ST, *ST, PT, 高风险警示, 从ST变为*ST, 撤消*ST并实行ST, 叠加ST, 叠加*ST) land on zero names the grammar calls ordinary -- a statement about a corpus, re-checkable against a re-pull. Delisting-period naming is classified rather than swept into 'none': 153 rows carry change_reason='退市整理期', 92 of their names end in 退 and the other 61 begin with 退市, and no row with another reason matches either shape. (10) PARTITIONING. stock_basic has no date filter, so one fetch spans 36 event years and panel_partition_year refuses it; filing it under the fetch year is not available either, because PanelStore.record_coverage refuses a date census reaching outside its partition's own year (V2-P1-003's fix). split_panel_batch_by_year therefore writes one partition per lifecycle year, which also makes the set of years a caller reads the observation window. namechange needs no split: its request window filters ann_date and its rows are dated there, because a rename's effective date is published IN the announcement -- the asymmetry with a delisting, which is not announced with its listing. The whole-market offset/limit pull was measured UNSOUND and is not used: two pages returned 14,166 rows with 380 exact duplicates, 13,786 distinct, and silently dropped a genuine record (000001.SZ / S深发展A) that the per-ts_code query returns; 37 announcement-year windows recover all 14,166 distinct rows. (11) NEITHER DATASET IS SERVED ON THE EVIDENCE PLANE. fetch() is verbatim passthrough under one available_time, and both response rows mix instants (delist_date beside list_date, end_date on the name in effect), so serves_evidence_plane=False refuses them by name rather than documenting a leak. (12) A live 2026 row (920165.BJ, announced 2026-08-11) has an availability instant after the fetch, which Timeline forbids; ingested_time is raised rather than available_time lowered, because lowering would make an unannounced rename readable, and both branches are pinned. Review correction: the raise now exists ONLY so such a row can be represented long enough to be discarded. _decode_panel_rows bounds its point-in-time filter at min(as_of, ingested_at) rather than as_of alone, so a row whose availability runs past the fetch instant is dropped and the raised clock never reaches a stored partition. The earlier bound had a plain escape route -- ProviderRequest accepts any as_of, and dating a batch at the end of the calendar year is a shape this repository's own fixtures use, which stored an ingested_time two days AFTER the clock that fetched it. Dropping is the honest answer because by its own clock the row was not knowable when the fetch ran, and it is the same statement the as_of filter already makes. (13) ONE PRE-EXISTING ASSERTION WAS UPDATED because this task made it false: test_tushare_metadata_declares_supported_datasets pinned ('daily','trade_cal') and now pins ('daily','trade_cal','stock_basic','namechange') -- still an exact literal. Layering unchanged: both contracts live in domain/ (pure datetime, bisect, dataclasses), openalpha_cn.panel imports no sibling subpackage, lint-imports 4 kept / 0 broken, runtime dependencies unchanged at 9, numpy/pandas still out per ADR-0003. Backend 836 passed + 1 skipped (was 709 + 1; 820 + 1 before this task's review fixes), coverage 93.02% (was 92.35%), frontend 52 passed unchanged. (14) THE REVIEW ALSO CLOSED THREE FAIL-OPENS AND ONE TAUTOLOGICAL TEST. write_stock_universe now vets every year before writing any year: interleaving them made the refusal itself destructive, leaving a store whose lifecycle years stop in the middle -- exactly the state load_stock_universe cannot distinguish from a quiet year. load_stock_universe gained require_years_through, an opt-in demand that the read cover every lifecycle year from years[0] through a stated year; without it a caller passing registered_years() asks for whatever the store happens to hold and can never notice that a year was never ingested, which on the real registry means 2024's 52 terminations reported as still listed. The demand is meaningful because a live probe found lifecycle events in EVERY year from 1990 to 2026 (6,217 rows over 37 years, the thinnest being 2013's eight), so a gap in a full-range read is an ingest gap rather than a quiet year. StockUniverse.listed_on now refuses a day before the first year in years_read, because a read that never saw those partitions cannot answer 'nobody was listed' for them; a universe built directly from SecurityLifecycle values has no window and keeps the honest empty answer. And the calendar overwrite guard's refusal is pinned by its whole message, remedy included: the earlier test asserted callable(_refuse_to_drop_stored_subjects), which stayed green when the entire remedy sentence was replaced with 'MUTATED REMEDY TEXT'. Eight mutants covering every one of these fixes were applied and all eight were killed by the suite.

feature_name: Adjustment factors with a fail-closed truncation guard
feature_description: adj_factor wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-006's dataset (3), the truncation guard that makes any capped Tushare response fail closed, and the AdjustmentHistory contract that turns the stored steps into adjusted prices and returns. The roadmap names this issue 'without it every return is wrong', and on a real ex-dividend day it is: 000001.SZ closed 11.30 on 2026-06-11 and 11.24 on 2026-06-12, so the unadjusted return is -0.53% while the adjusted one is +2.7423%, matching Tushare's own pct_chg of 2.7422%. The sign is not the same. TRUNCATION: the endpoint serves at most 6,000 rows and drops the OLDEST ones, so a bare adj_factor(ts_code=000001.SZ) returns 6,000 rows starting 2001-11-14 against a true 8,627-row history starting 1991-04-03 -- a decade of factors gone with no error code. _check_response_completeness refuses such a response on two independent witnesses (data.has_more, which must be exactly the boolean False, and a per-descriptor measured row cap) rather than storing a factor series that is a suffix of the truth. STORAGE: the factor is piecewise constant -- 000001.SZ's 8,627 rows take 43 distinct values, so it moves at 42 change points and the stored window is 44 rows, a 196x compression -- so the panel stores the steps plus each window's opening and closing observation, which is what makes a single year's partition self-sufficient. Those anchors are NOT a substitute for date coverage, which is why write_adjustment_factors takes a TradingCalendar and refuses, before compressing, any year missing a session the calendar reports open. CONVENTION: the published number is the BACKWARD (后复权) cumulative factor, 1.0 at the listing; forward (前复权) adjustment is that factor divided by a named base day's, and adjust_price refuses to run without one rather than guessing. adjusted_return takes no convention, because the two differ by a constant scale that cancels in a ratio.
notes: V2-P1-006 (PRD Story S12; roadmap section 6 dataset 3; depends on V2-P1-004/005; depended on by V2-P1-007/008/017). Every number below is from a live probe of the real endpoints on 2026-08-08; none of it is asserted against the network -- the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) THE TRUNCATION IS REAL AND SILENT. q(adj_factor, ts_code=000001.SZ) returns 6,000 rows beginning 2001-11-14; the same query restricted to 19910101..20011113 returns 2,627 more, beginning 1991-04-03 with adj_factor exactly 1.0, so the true history is 8,627 rows and the cap drops the OLDEST. Adding an explicit full range changes nothing. A whole-market window truncates the same way: 20240624..20240628 returned 6,000 rows covering only 06-27 and 06-28. (2) THE BRIEF FOR THIS TASK SAID THE API GIVES NO TRUNCATION SIGNAL -- 'no error code, no has_more, no total'. TWO OF THE THREE ARE WRONG. data.has_more is present on every response and is True on exactly the truncated ones; data.count exists but reads 0 always, so only 'no total' holds. (3) has_more IS NOT A 'MORE EXISTS' FLAG, it is the server's own len(rows)==limit heuristic, and that was measured decisively: the window 20011114..20260808 holds exactly 6,000 rows with nothing older and still reports True, while 20011115..20260808 returns 5,999 and reports False; limit=2627 on a window with exactly 2,627 rows reports True and limit=2628 reports False. It therefore OVER-reports and never under-reports, which is the fail-closed direction -- and it is why the measured row cap is kept beside it as an independent witness rather than replaced by it. Only the literal boolean False counts as complete; 'False' and '0' are truthy and 0 and '' are falsy, so neither coercion is a fact about the data (the rule _open_flag already applies to is_open). requires_truncation_flag makes an ABSENT has_more a failure too, and is stated per descriptor so that V2-P1-007/008 have to decide it; it is set on adj_factor and on stock_basic, the latter because that endpoint has no measurable cap and the flag is therefore its only witness. (4) THE CAP IS PER ENDPOINT, NOT GLOBAL, and this matters: adj_factor and daily cap at 6,000 (limit=8000 and limit=10000 do not raise it), namechange at 10,000, while trade_cal returned all 13,162 published SSE rows in ONE response with has_more=False -- so a single global constant of 6,000 would refuse a complete calendar. stock_basic returned its whole 5,878-row L,D registry with has_more=False, which places its cap ABOVE 5,878 without establishing where -- and the cap is unmeasurable from outside, because limit=5878 reports has_more=TRUE while limit=100000 reports false, so the flag turns True at whatever effective limit is in force and no probe can push past the real ceiling. '6000 minus 5878 = 122 rows of margin' would be exactly the guess this declines to make; if this endpoint shares namechange's 10,000 the true figure is 4,122. So stock_basic declares no cap and now carries requires_truncation_flag=True, because it was the one descriptor with NEITHER witness -- a response omitting has_more was accepted at any row count with nothing checking it. (5) WHERE THE GUARD MISSES, stated rather than glossed: it judges one response in isolation, so the residue is a server that truncates while reporting has_more=False at a row count under the declared cap. A LOWERED cap is NOT in the residue: raising limit above the measured value (6001/8000/10000) still returns exactly 6,000 rows with has_more=true, which shows the server computes the flag as len(rows)==min(limit, cap), so any truncation at any cap reports True and the flag witness covers a moved cap on its own. A calendar-derived expected ROW COUNT was considered as a third response witness and rejected on measurement: 000001.SZ has factor rows on 64 dates in 1991 that are not in the stored SZSE calendar at all -- trade_cal's SZSE series begins 1991-07-03 while the factor begins 1991-04-03, so those days are beyond the horizon rather than marked closed -- and all 64 are dates the SSE calendar marks open, so that expectation would manufacture false alarms. The calendar is used one layer up instead, where the direction can be chosen: see (12). (6) THE FACTOR IS NOT MONOTONE, contrary to the brief's 'monotone non-decreasing, pin it on real data' -- a test written to that spec would FAIL. Eight of 000001.SZ's own rows step down: five are genuine 1991-93 movements of up to 6.4% (2.608 -> 2.463 on 1991-11-11) and three are four-to-three-decimal rounding worth 0.0002%. Market-wide between 2023-12-29 and 2024-06-28, 28 of the 5,351 securities present on both dates have a LOWER factor on the later one. The contract makes no monotonicity claim and a test pins the eight decreases as data. The five that fell by more than 0.1% are filed SEPARATELY, as delisted_securities_carry_unstable_factors, because they are not market movements: 600069.SH (退银鸽(退), listed 19970430) has 5,421 daily bars ending 20200820 at 0.28 yuan and delist_date 20200827, yet adj_factor serves rows to 20250428 which change 17 times since 2020-01-01, OSCILLATING between two levels (6.415 -> 0.6604 on 20220624, back on 20220906, ..., 6.415 -> 0.6604 on 20240617 -- the step that produced the -89.7%), over four distinct values 0.6603/0.6604/6.4148/6.415. A cumulative factor cannot return to a level it left, so these are upstream defects; 600978.SH (delisted 20210322, last bar 20210222, factor rows to 20250814) has the same shape with 17 changes over 0.8016/5.041/5.0417, and all five (600069, 600978, 600247, 600677, 600485) are delisted SH main-board names. Any adjusted return spanning a delisting is untrustworthy. Filing that under 'the factor really can fall' would have told the reader it was a fact about corporate actions. (7) THE STORAGE DECISION IS PIECEWISE CONSTANT, and the reasons are measured: 8,627 rows taking 43 distinct values, so 42 change points and 44 stored rows (196x, not the 201x that quoting the distinct-value count as the row count gives), against ~4.8e7 rows for the whole market's daily form of a series that moves about once per security per year; the query is a bisect, the same shape NameHistory already uses. THE PARTITION-BOUNDARY HAZARD the brief flags is answered structurally -- load_bearing_observations keeps the window's FIRST observation, every change, AND the window's LAST observation. The last one is the easy one to drop and the one that matters: 000001.SZ's final 2024 change is 2024-10-10, so without it the partition would report covered_through as October and refuse every November and December question. Both anchors are real observations, not interpolated markers. Two adjacent years therefore concatenate with at most one redundant equal-valued row at the boundary and no invented one. (8) TWO HORIZONS, unlike NameHistory's one. A name persists until it is changed, so carrying the last one forward invents nothing; a factor changes on a schedule the held data cannot see (000001.SZ moved four times in the two years after 2024), so carrying the last factor forward asserts that no corporate action happened in a window the read never covered. factor_on refuses both ends and covered_from/covered_through state the window. (9) THE CONVENTION IS BACKWARD, and the brief called it 前复权累积因子, which is wrong: a forward-adjusted factor is 1.0 at the base day and below 1.0 before it, while this series is 1.0 at the listing (19910403) and 139.008 in 2026. 后复权 price = close * factor and needs no base day; 前复权 price = close * factor(day) / factor(base) and adjust_price RAISES without a base_day rather than defaulting to the newest day held, which would silently restate every adjusted price on the next refresh. Passing a base_day to the backward convention also raises, because a caller who supplies one has asked for the other scale. adjusted_return takes no convention at all, and a test proves the two scales give the same return on real prices. (10) INGEST SHAPE. A request is one trading day of the whole market (the same _trade_date_params daily uses): 5,387 rows on 2024-06-28 and 5,553 on 2026-08-07 against the 6,000 cap, so a cross section fits and one security's history does not. A partition is a calendar year = ~1.3e6 rows = ~244 fetches, and PanelStore.write_partition replaces a partition whole with no append, so the fetches have to become one batch first. merge_panel_batches is that primitive (the inverse of split_panel_batch_by_year, and the one V2-P1-007 will need for daily); write_adjustment_factors merges, checks the session census against a TradingCalendar, compresses, refuses a straddling year via panel_partition_year and refuses an overwrite that would drop a security via the shared _refuse_to_drop_stored_subjects. The subject guard and the session guard are the two halves of one failure and neither substitutes for the other: a missing security makes the answer shorter, a missing session makes it WRONG. A merged batch's source_uri becomes None when the inputs disagree, which is a real loss and is stated rather than papered over -- every row still carries its own subject and factor_date, and PartitionCoverage.batch_digest still re-proves the partition. (11) A PRE-EXISTING BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN PASSING. _panel_source_uri joined every distinct subject, so a real whole-market fetch built a ~60,000-character URI and ColumnarPanelBatch refused it OUTSIDE fetch_panel's decode try -- meaning no whole-market panel fetch could complete at all, stock_basic's included (reproduced against 2b06c4c with 400 synthetic registry rows). The join is now kept while it fits under the contract's own MAX_SOURCE_URI_LENGTH and replaced by '{n}-subjects' when it does not, so the two-exchange calendar URI is byte-identical to what it was. The producer's bound is BOUND to the contract's constant rather than restated as a second literal, and a test asserts the equality: while they were two separate 2048s, raising the producer's to 3,000 left the whole suite green and restored the original bug for every fetch whose joined URI lands in the gap (9-character codes over a 39-character frame make it 10n+38, so 201 subjects land on exactly 2,048 and 202 land past it). (12) READINESS waives required_dates ON THE RECORD, and this is the one place the storage decision is visible from outside: a compressed step function has rows only on load-bearing sessions, so a calendar-derived expectation would report a permanent date_gap on a partition that is complete by construction -- panel_readiness_requirement must NOT be pointed at this dataset. WHAT REPLACES IT IS A WRITE-TIME CHECK, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE STORED ROWS. The window anchors are not the replacement, and saying they were is the one claim in this row that was measured false: they bound one partition's ENDS, so a hole inside a partition -- or a partition that begins in March -- falls inside covered_from/covered_through the moment two years are read together and is answered by bisect from the previous step, with nothing raising. Reproduced end to end on a real PanelStore: a 2026 partition backfilled from 06-15 reports ready=True with no issues and answers factor_on(2026-06-12) with 134.5794 instead of 139.008, turning that day's return from +2.742251% into -0.530973% -- the unadjusted number, sign and all. Three shapes produce it on real 000001.SZ data: a 2020 partition starting in March beside a complete 2019 (36 wrong sessions, the true step being 2020-01-02), a single dropped cross-section fetch (1 wrong session), and 1996 fetched after that year's last step (50.0000% relative error, 6.984 against 13.968). So compression is preceded by _refuse_missing_factor_sessions, which requires every session the calendar reports open between the year's start and the day before the fetch. MISSING only -- extra days are tolerated, because the 64 1991 dates above are exactly the shape an equality check would wrongly refuse, and an extra observation cannot remove information. Named residues: a year written from a batch fetched on 1 January of that same year is unchecked, and partitions written before the gate existed are not re-examined on read. feature_name: Daily bars and valuations with a two-path return cross-check
feature_description: daily and daily_basic wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-007's dataset (4), plus the DailyBar/DailyValuation contracts, the return cross-validation that exercises them against V2-P1-006's adjustment factors, and the cross section that joins a session's bars onto the listed universe. The roadmap routes this issue onto the panel plane because kind='daily' evidence records are refused by evidence/builder.py. Tushare's pre_close is already restated for the morning's corporate action, so a session return has two correct forms (close/pre_close, and the adjusted ratio) and one that is wrong with the sign reversed on every ex-rights day; session_returns computes all three and refuses when the two correct ones disagree by more than one published tick. daily_basic republishes close, which makes the two fetches a session needs into a free cross-check, and write_daily_panel makes that agreement a precondition of storage. total_mv, circ_mv and turnover_rate reach the panel as P3 neutralisation and P4 leaderboard inputs. V2-P2-006 adds the third witness the stored pct_chg column exists for: session_returns also reconciles the row's own pct_chg against close/pre_close - 1, which is the only one of the two checks that reads close at all -- the pre_close comparison is between prev_close*f_prev/f and the published pre_close and never touches it. MAX_PUBLISHED_RETURN_DISAGREEMENT is one tick of a two-decimal percentage (1e-4 of return), the coarser of the two grids the endpoint publishes pct_chg on.
notes: V2-P1-007 (PRD Story S4; roadmap section 6 dataset 4; depends on V2-P1-004/005/006; depended on by V2-P1-008/017, P3 neutralisation, P4 leaderboards). Every number below is from a live probe of the real endpoints on 2026-08-08/09; none of it is asserted against the network -- the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) FETCH GRANULARITY IS ONE SESSION OF THE MARKET. daily(trade_date=20240628) returns 5,338 rows and daily_basic 5,338, against a measured 6,000-row per-response cap; 20260807 returns 5,535 for both, so the headroom is ~8%. A bare daily(ts_code=000001.SZ) and a bare daily_basic(ts_code=000001.SZ) each return exactly 6,000 rows with has_more=True, so a per-security history cannot be stored at all. Both descriptors therefore reuse _trade_date_params and V2-P1-006's merge_panel_batches, and the year is ~244 fetches per dataset. (2) pre_close IS ALREADY EX-RIGHTS ADJUSTED, which is the whole point. 000001.SZ closed at 11.30 on 2026-06-11 and its 2026-06-12 pre_close is 10.94, not 11.30. So close/pre_close-1 = +2.742230% and (close*f)/(prev_close*f_prev)-1 = +2.742251% agree, while close[t]/close[t-1]-1 = -0.530973% has the wrong sign. On the market-wide 2026-06-11/12 pair, 100 of 5,508 securities had a pre_close more than one fen from the previous close. session_returns() computes all three and REFUSES when the two correct paths disagree by more than one published tick of pre_close (0.01). The tolerance is stated in price space rather than return space because the same half-fen of rounding is 4.6e-4 of relative error on an 11-yuan stock and 3.3e-3 on a 1.50-yuan one. Measured across 16,246 real (previous session, session) pairs on three sessions, the largest disagreement was 0.0081 and the naive path was wrong by up to 118.30. (3) THE 49-NAME GAP IS TWO POPULATIONS, NOT ONE. On 2024-06-28 adj_factor served 5,387 rows and daily 5,338, with daily a strict subset. Of the 49: 26 were listed and halted (all 26 appear in that session's 28-row suspend_d) and 23 had already been delisted (delist_date <= 20240628) and still emit factor rows -- 600069.SH and 600247.SH among them, the names KNOWN_ADJUSTMENT_LIMITATIONS.delisted_securities_carry_unstable_factors already carries. priced_cross_section() keeps them apart without suspend_d (V2-P1-008) because it iterates universe.listed_on(day): the 23 never become candidates and the 26 land in PricedCrossSection.unpriced by name. (4) A PRICED SECURITY CAN BE ABSENT FROM THE REGISTRY. 300114.SZ has a real 2024-06-28 bar and stock_basic returns zero rows for it under 'L', 'D', 'P', 'L,D' and the bare request. It is the only such name on that session and there are none on 20250801 or 20260807. PricedCrossSection.unlisted_bars names these rather than keeping them (a code is_listed refuses to answer for) or dropping them (a market short by one, with no signal). (5) daily_basic IS A SUBSET OF daily, NEVER A SUPERSET, AND THE GAP IS ONE BOARD. 20150708: 1,489 / 1,467. 20180102: 3,282 / 3,252. 20200302: 3,843 / 3,783. 20220425: 4,836 / 4,780. 20240628 and 20260807: zero difference. Every missing code on every one of those sessions ends in .BJ. So close_disagreements() reports a valuation with no bar (never observed, a contradiction) and tolerates a bar with no valuation (ordinary), and write_daily_panel() refuses the first at write time. The close columns agreed on all 24,188 shared rows of five sessions. (6) NULLABILITY IS MEASURED, NOT REASONED. On 20240628, of 5,338 daily_basic rows: pe null on 1,102, pe_ttm 1,214, dv_ttm 1,840, dv_ratio 354, pb 29, ps/ps_ttm 3, volume_ratio 2 -- those eight are DAILY_BASIC_NULLABLE_COLUMNS. close, turnover_rate, turnover_rate_f, total_share, float_share, free_share, total_mv and circ_mv were populated on every row of five sessions across 2023..2026 and a null in one is refused at the provider boundary; a null total_mv would silently drop a name from a neutralisation regression. All 11 daily fields were non-null and all five price columns positive across 24,188 bars. (7) THE TRUNCATION FLAG IS DECLINED, WITH A REASON. requires_truncation_flag governs only an ABSENT has_more; a present one is checked for every dataset. adj_factor demands it because a truncated factor series is silently wrong (the step function answers the missing decade from an older level); a truncated daily response is short, not wrong. The residue is pinned rather than argued away: a response that both omits the flag and comes in under 6,000 rows is accepted. (8) THE SESSION CENSUS IS V2-P1-006's HOMOMORPH AND DIFFERS IN WHAT IT PAYS FOR. adjustment_requirement waives required_dates (compression destroys the census), so its write-time census is the only check and cannot re-examine an older partition. A price partition is uncompressed, so daily_requirement does NOT waive required_dates and every read re-checks the same calendar-derived expectation. Both censuses share _session_census() and both bound the expectation at the year's own start and the day before the fetch. panel_readiness_requirement is deliberately not reused: it clamps at as_of's calendar date, one session too generous for a dataset that publishes at 16:30, and _sessions_published_through reads the same DAILY_AVAILABILITY_TIME the provider dates available_time at. (9) THE ROW-WISE PLANE IS REROUTED, NOT REMOVED. The roadmap notes that kind='daily' records are refused by evidence/builder.py:88-90. That refusal is correct and stays: an EvidenceSnapshot is a normalised citation and a price bar has no _Facts model or EvidenceFamily. daily keeps serves_evidence_plane=True, unlike stock_basic/namechange, because a bar has a single honest available_time; what moves it onto the panel plane is ADR-0002's ~1.35e7 rows per field, and scale is a reason to add an output shape rather than to make the existing one refuse. (10) MUTATION-TESTED. Twenty mutations of these guards were applied one at a time with __pycache__ cleared before each run; all twenty were killed.

feature_name: Trading halts and published price limits
feature_description: suspend_d and stk_limit wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-008's dataset (5), plus the halt contract that answers what did not trade and the published-band contract that answers how far what did trade could move. suspend_d is three states rather than a suspension list: an R row is a resumption and an S row carrying a suspend_timing window is an intraday halt, and both mean the security traded, so only an untimed S explains an absent bar. That is the answer to the limitation V2-P1-007 recorded as a_partial_cross_section_is_invisible_without_suspend_d, on the read side through explain_unpriced and at write time through _refuse_unexplained_thin_sessions. stk_limit is the band the exchange published, and AShareExecutionPolicy previously derived one from the board and an is_st flag; the two disagree on 159 of 5,338 names on one ordinary session, so MarketBar gained optional up_limit/down_limit fields that the policy prefers when they are there, with the derived path untouched for every caller that does not supply them.
notes: V2-P1-008 (PRD Stories S47/S55; roadmap section 6 dataset 5; depends on V2-P1-004/005/006/007; depended on by V2-P1-012/017 and the P4 leaderboards). Every number below is from a live probe of the real endpoints on 2026-08-09; none of it is asserted against the network -- the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) suspend_d IS THREE STATES, NOT A SUSPENSION LIST. suspend_d(trade_date=20240628) serves 28 rows: 26 S and 2 R (000615.SZ, 603050.SH), and both R names have a daily bar that session. Every R row on every session probed had a bar (27/27 on 20150709, 5/5 on 20150708, 17/17, 6/6, 5/5, 2/2, 1/1, 1/1). Separately, an S row can carry a suspend_timing window: 20150708 served 1,343 S rows of which 31 carry one, and ALL 31 have a bar while NONE of the other 1,312 do -- the same exact split on 20150709, 20160104, 20180208, 20200302 and 20220425. So halted() is the untimed S set only. That split does NOT hold before 2015 (12 of 18 untimed S names had a bar on 20050104, 15 of 143 on 20080102, 1 of 41 on 20100104, with suspend_timing null throughout), which is carried as KNOWN_SUSPENSION_LIMITATIONS.intraday_halts_are_unmarked_before_2015 rather than assumed away. suspend_type's value domain is exhaustive, not sampled: 537,671 rows spanning 2007-01..2026-12, pulled in windows narrow enough that none was truncated, carry S or R and nothing else. (2) THE 1,529-ROW EXCESS OVER daily IS THREE POPULATIONS AND MOSTLY NOT EQUITY. stk_limit(20240628) serves 6,867 rows against daily's 5,338. The extra 1,529 are 1,418 funds (ETFs and LOFs -- 159*.SZ, 51*.SH, 501*.SH, 16*.SZ, 56*.SH -- all present in fund_basic), 85 B shares (44 900*.SH and 41 200*/201*.SZ, in neither stock_basic nor fund_basic) and the session's 26 halted A shares. adj_factor's 49-name excess on the same session shares only those 26; its other 23 are delisted names stk_limit does not carry. daily is a subset of stk_limit only recently: 60 bars had no band on 20200302, 56 on 20220425, 44 on 20160104, 23 on 20150708, all but 001914.SZ being .BJ codes. stk_limit also has a horizon -- 0 rows on 20050104 and 20060104, 1,408 on 20070104. (3) THE DERIVED BAND IS WRONG ON 159 OF 5,338 NAMES, FOR FOUR INDEPENDENT REASONS. Joining stk_limit onto daily.pre_close for every priced name on 20240628: (a) the Beijing board rounds INWARD -- all 249 .BJ names match floor(pre*1.30) and ceil(pre*0.70) while ROUND_HALF_UP matches only 118 and 143, so 131 differ by one fen (920924.BJ: 7.32*1.30 = 9.516, published 9.51); the same 100%/~50% split holds on 20220425 (87 names), 20250801 (269) and 20260807 (333). (b) ST on ChiNext or STAR keeps the board's 20%: 128 names were ST by the name_history grammar and 104 (all main board) have a 5% band while 25 (24 ChiNext, 1 STAR) have 20%, where _rejection_reason's is_st branch computes a band four times too narrow. (c) A new listing has NO band for five sessions, published as a sentinel up_limit with down_limit=0.01, and the encoding has changed twice -- 100000.0 (SSE 2020, 2022), 1000000.0 (SZSE 2022), 99999.999 (SSE 2024, 2026), 999999.999 (SZSE 2024, 2026). (d) 600182.SH 'S佳通', a share-reform name the ST grammar correctly calls ordinary, carries a 5% band. Nothing about the derived rule is silently changed: MarketBar's two new fields default to None and _price_band falls back to the identical arithmetic. (4) THE SENTINEL IS CLASSIFIED BY RATIO, NOT BY VALUE. A whitelist of the four observed encodings would misread a fifth. LIMIT_FREE_RATIO=2.0 sits between the widest real published band ever measured (1.44x pre_close -- 300740.SZ and 603709.SH on their 20180208 first day, +44%/-36%) and the narrowest sentinel (384x, 688052.SH on 20220425). Both consumers are also correct without the classification: no real bar satisfies high >= 99999.999 or low <= 0.01. (5) THE CAPS ARE MEASURED PER ENDPOINT AND ONE OF THEM IS NEARLY GONE. stk_limit serves at most 7,800 rows per response and suspend_d at most 5,000 (20260701..20260807 returns exactly 7,800 with has_more=True, 20150601..20150831 exactly 5,000, and limit=8000/10000/12000 raise neither). The whole-market stk_limit cross section was 6,867 rows on 20240628, 7,216 on 20250801 and 7,733 on 20260807 -- +349 then +517 -- so it sits 67 rows under its cap against daily's 465 of 6,000. stk_limit also DEMANDS the truncation flag, the first price dataset to do so, because unlike a dropped bar a dropped band is not an absence: the execution policy substitutes its derived rule, which is the wrong number above. suspend_d declines it, because every consumer uses a halt to excuse a missing bar, so a truncated response raises more alarms rather than fewer. (6) THE THIN-SESSION FLOOR IS THREE QUARTERS TIGHTER. V2-P1-007's MIN_SESSION_ROW_SHARE had to sit at 0.5 because 2015-07-09 legitimately served 1,363 bars against that year's median of 2,359 (0.578). A full-year census of 2015 -- 244 sessions, one daily and one suspend_d request each -- shows that counting whole-day halts moves the year's minimum to 2,593 of a median 2,796 (0.927), with the binding session moving from July to January where the shortfall is within-year listing growth rather than a halt. MIN_EXPLAINED_SESSION_SHARE is therefore 0.85 and catches a session that lost a seventh of the market unexplained. Three years were censused in full and 2015 binds: 2008 min explained 0.959 (bars alone 0.914), 2015 0.927 (0.578), 2018 0.984 (0.941). 2018's bar figure reproduces the one MIN_SESSION_ROW_SHARE's docstring already published, which is what makes the other two checkable rather than asserted, and 2008 is in the set precisely because it predates the intraday marker, so it is the year where halted() over-counts most. The guard is OPT-IN -- write_daily_panel's halts parameter defaults to None -- which is a real fail-open and is stated as one: making it mandatory would change the signature for every existing caller, and V2-P1-015's panel build, which fetches all three datasets in one loop, is where the default should be removed. The 0.5 floor still runs unconditionally, so nothing is weaker than before. (7) MUTATION-TESTED. Twenty mutations of these guards were applied one at a time with __pycache__ cleared before each run; all twenty were killed.

feature_name: Index composition and published weights with visible staleness
feature_description: index_weight wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-009's dataset (6), plus the IndexMembership contract that turns a monthly publication into two separate answers. The endpoint publishes once a calendar month, on that month's last open session, so every question about any other day is answered by carrying a snapshot forward -- and the two things carried forward are not equally trustworthy. Membership is what the publisher said it is and usually survives the fill; a weight is a month-end capitalisation share that starts drifting with prices the next session. constituents_on returns an IndexComposition carrying no weight at all, weights_on returns an IndexWeights carrying as_published_on and days_since_publication, and there is no accessor anywhere that hands back a bare float for a day. The weight-sum tolerance is derived from each publication's own decimal precision rather than calibrated on a recent session, and the registry join reports the constituents stock_basic cannot confirm instead of refusing the publication over them.
notes: V2-P1-009 (PRD Story S11; roadmap section 6 dataset 6; depends on V2-P1-004/005; depended on by V2-P1-010, P3 neutralisation, P4 leaderboards and P5 benchmarks). Every number below is from a live probe of the real endpoint on 2026-08-09 covering the whole published history of the three indices -- 000300.SH from 2005-04-29, 000905.SH from 2007-01-31, 000852.SH from 2014-10-31, 633 publications and 336,298 constituent rows -- and none of it is asserted against the network; the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) MONTHLY, NOT DAILY, AND EXHAUSTIVELY SO. The 633 publications fall on 633 distinct calendar months: no month inside an index's life carries none, no month carries two, and all 633 dates are the last open SSE session of their month on the stored trade_cal series. 000300.SH published on exactly 12 dates in 2023 (20230131..20231229) and on 9 in 2005, its launch year. That is what build_index_membership's month rule encodes, and it is what pays for index_weight_requirement waiving required_dates: the rule needs no calendar, runs on every read rather than only at write time, and sees a hole that straddles two partitions. (2) THE STALENESS IS THE POINT, AND IT IS NOT adj_factor'S STEP FUNCTION. A factor really is constant between two ex-rights days; an index weight really is not constant between two publications, so the same storage shape carries a completely different guarantee. Composition and weights are therefore different types with different warnings, and the asymmetry is measured rather than asserted: 166 of the 630 publication-to-publication transitions changed the membership (the scheduled June and December reviews replace 50 names in 000905.SH and 100 in 000852.SH, with single-name substitutions in every other month), and 38 constituent terminations fall strictly inside a forward-fill window -- 600001.SH 邯郸钢铁 is in the 2009-11-30 publication, was terminated 2009-12-29, and the next publication is 2009-12-31, so 2009-12-29 and 2009-12-30 both name a security that had gone. So even the composition answer carries as_published_on, and this issue does not claim a forward-filled membership is a fact about the day. THE COMPOSITION'S LARGEST FAILURE IS NOT THOSE 38, AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS ROW MISSED IT. The publisher's June and December reviews take effect after the close of that month's SECOND FRIDAY; index_weight does not carry the new list until the month's last session, so the review is in force for 9 to 14 sessions before it is published and constituents_on answers those sessions from a composition that had already been replaced -- silently, with no horizon raised and a days_since_publication that reports only the snapshot's age. Measured: 000300.SH's 2026-05-29 and 2026-06-30 publications differ by 19 names, 000905.SH's by 50 and 000852.SH's by 100; 2026-06-15..2026-06-29 is 10 sessions, so every 000300.SH question in that window names 19 securities that had gone and omits 19 that had arrived. Over all 76 June and December reviews from 2013-12 to 2026-06 that is 6,358 + 15,250 + 28,292 = 49,900 (name x session) answers naming a removed security and 49,900 more omitting an added one -- a lower bound, since the reviews fell in January and July before 2013 and are not counted. It is disclosed as scheduled_review_takes_effect_before_it_is_published and it is also askable: IndexComposition and IndexWeights carry undated_rebalance, the names that changed at the NEXT publication, which this dataset cannot place anywhere inside the gap. That field is built from the module's own rows and needs neither the publisher's schedule nor a trading calendar, so it also covers the unscheduled single-name substitutions and the pre-2013 January/July era; it over-reports (on 2026-06-01 it already names the 19) rather than under-reporting, which is the direction a dependency gate should be wrong in. (3) THE SUM TOLERANCE IS DERIVED, NOT CALIBRATED. The brief for this task quoted 100.002 / 99.997 / 100.002 from one 2024 session; across the corpus the absolute deviation from 100 has a median of 0.005, a 90th percentile of 0.03, a 99th of 0.11 and a maximum of 0.21 (000852.SH 2014-10-31), so a 0.003 tolerance drawn from that session would refuse more than half the published history. The bound used is count * 0.5 * 10**-decimals, the arithmetic worst case for a correctly rounded column, which refuses none of the 633 and fits most tightly at 0.092 of its value (000905.SH 2009-01-23). It is not vacuous: one constituent dropped from a 300-name publication moves the sum by 0.433 against a 0.15 bound. The precision is read per publication because the endpoint changed it twice -- three decimals in 2005..2010 and 2016..2026, two in 2013..2014, with 2011, 2012 and 2015 each carrying publications of both kinds -- and that choice is stated honestly as unproven by the corpus: every real publication sits inside the three-decimal bound too, so a fixed rule would admit the same set today and would refuse a return to the coarser era. (4) THE REGISTRY JOIN HAS TWO REAL COUNTEREXAMPLES, AND IT REPORTS THEM. 990018.SH is in eighteen 000300.SH publications from 2005-04-29 to 2006-09-29 at weights 0.681..1.391 and is in neither the L nor the D half of stock_basic's 5,878-row registry. It has since been identified rather than left unexplained: namechange(990018.SH) resolves it to 上港集箱 / G上港, the entity 上港集团 absorbed by share exchange in 2006, with stock_basic dating the surviving listing 600018.SH 上港集团 to 2006-10-26 -- and the publications show the handover, 990018.SH leaving 000300.SH and 600018.SH arriving in the same 2006-09-29 to 2006-10-31 transition. Tushare renumbers a pre-merger entity out of the survivor's code and stock_basic keeps only the survivor, the same mechanism V2-P1-007 met in namechange. 600270.SH 外运发展 is in 000905.SH's 2018-12-28 publication at weight 0.253 while its registry delist_date is 2018-12-28, which V2-P1-005 treats as exclusive. Those are the only two constituent identities out of 336,298 constituent-rows the registry cannot confirm, and constituent_listing_report separates unknown_to_registry, not_listed and beyond_snapshot rather than refusing the publication -- discarding a real month of a real index over one upstream inconsistency would be the worse answer. Zero constituents have a list_date after their publication. (5) THE CONSTITUENT COUNT IS DATA, NOT A CONSTANT. 000300.SH published 298 names on 2009-12-31: 600001.SH and 600357.SH were both terminated on 2009-12-29 and the month-end publication dropped them with no replacement, the 2010-01-29 review restoring the count. It is the only off-nominal publication in the 633 (000905.SH is 500 on all 235 of its own, 000852.SH is 1000 on all 142), and a rule asserting 300/500/1000 would refuse a real partition on the one day it mattered. (6) THE CAP IS 7,000 AND NO limit RAISES IT. index_weight(000852.SH, 20230101..20231231) should hold 12,000 rows and returns exactly 7,000 with has_more=True; limit=8000, 10000, 12000 and 20000 all return the same 7,000. The first version of this row said limit was ignored in both directions and that was wrong -- re-measured for the task-32 review, limit=4000 returns 4,000, limit=5000 returns 5,000, limit=6999 returns 6,999 and the string '5000' returns 5,000, each with has_more=True. limit narrows and never widens, so 7,000 is the server's own ceiling. Nothing sends limit (_index_weight_params), so the correction changes a stated measurement rather than any behaviour. The cap drops the oldest rows and can split a publication: index_weight(000300.SH, 20100101..20231231) returns 7,000 rows over 24 dates whose oldest, 2022-01-28, carries 100 of its 300 names. The flag is therefore demanded -- a partial publication is a different index rather than a short one -- even though the sum tolerance is an independent second witness for that exact shape, because a truncation landing on a publication boundary drops whole months and leaves every survivor summing perfectly. For the three indices this issue measures the headroom is the widest in the table (one publication is at most 1,000 rows) and is the only one not on the market's clock: what would have to grow is an index's constituent count, which its own definition fixes. That is a fact about those three and not about the descriptor, which takes any index_code -- a whole-market index is a cross section like any other, and the single month 20260701..20260731 is 5,126 rows for 000985.CSI 中证全指 and 5,175 for 000902.CSI 中证流通, 73% of the cap and rising with every listing, against 2,000 for 932000.CSI and 800 for 000906.SH. (7) THE INDEX IS THE SUBJECT, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE OVERWRITE GUARD WORK. PanelStore's key is (dataset, year) with no index dimension, so a per-index backfill loop would leave a year holding whichever index it wrote last -- V2-P1-004's exchange failure exactly. write_index_weights reuses _refuse_to_drop_stored_subjects, which compares stored subjects against the batch's, so it only works because the subject column holds the index. Putting the constituent there would trip the guard too, today, and only by the coincidence that these three indices are disjoint. It would NOT then misfire on every ordinary rebalance -- that supporting claim was in the first version of this row and is false: _refuse_to_drop_stored_subjects compares a whole partition's subject set against a whole batch's, and a year's batch carries every name that year published, so rewriting 2023 for all three indices drops zero subjects under either choice. What the constituent subject would lose is the case the guard exists for: 000906.SH 中证800 is 000300.SH plus 000905.SH, so a batch for it covers both of their constituent sets and would replace their partition with nothing appearing to go missing. The two remaining reasons stand: the three indices being disjoint on their shared publication days is a coincidence rather than a property, and the index is what index_weight_requirement names in required_subjects and what load_index_membership filters on. Under either choice the guard is blind to a lost MONTH -- a per-month write loop carries all three indices every time and replaces the year with one month -- which write_index_weights now says out loud; the read is what refuses that, on the month rule or on covered_from == covered_through. The endpoint also returns ZERO rows for a comma-joined index_code, so one index per request is the endpoint's constraint rather than a preference. (8) MUTATION-TESTED. Thirty-four mutations of these guards were applied one at a time with __pycache__ cleared before each run at landing; all thirty-four were killed. The task-32 review then applied 51 of its own and six survived, four of them properties this module names in a docstring and never tested: _require_weight, _stored_weight, _require_stored_text and _require_text rewritten from an exact type check to isinstance (only a float or str SUBCLASS distinguishes the two, and neither was exercised); _require_weight's upper bound widened from 100 to 1000, which the parametrised case then failed for the wrong rule because its match= pattern was just weight; and load_index_membership's subject filter replaced by None. All six now have tests. Twelve mutations were applied for this pass -- those six plus six covering undated_rebalance (the publication-day short circuit, the empty-transition None, the pass-through in IndexWeights.composition, an off-by-one on the following publication, and the two population sites) -- one at a time with __pycache__ cleared before each run; twelve killed.

feature_name: Point-in-time industry classification with a named taxonomy backfill
feature_description: index_classify and index_member_all wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-010's dataset (7), plus the IndustryTree and SecurityIndustryHistory contracts that turn them into an answer to 'which industry was this security in on day D'. The membership rows carry an explicit closed interval, so nothing is forward-filled and a coverage hole is refused rather than papered over. What they do not carry is when the answer became knowable: the whole 1984..2026 history is expressed in the SW2021 taxonomy, which came into force 2021-12-13, so every pre-2021 answer is a backfill, and over the window the two Tushare endpoints can both speak to they disagree about the L1 on 1,038,252 of 9,566,861 (name x session) pairs. IndustryAnswer therefore never returns a bare industry code -- it carries the taxonomy, the taxonomy's effective date and is_backfilled -- and the provider splits a closed assignment into an opening row and a closing row and floors both at the taxonomy's effective date, so a read before 2021-12-13 blocks with not_yet_knowable while a read inside the SW2021 era sees the corpus as it then stood. The registry join reports the listed securities with no industry rather than dropping them silently.
notes: V2-P1-010 (PRD Story S11; roadmap section 6 dataset 7; depends on V2-P1-004/005; depended on by V2-P3-004 neutralisation and P4 leaderboards). Every number below is from a live probe of both real endpoints on 2026-08-09 -- the whole SW2021 and SW2014 trees (511 and 359 nodes) and the whole membership corpus (7,893 rows over 5,889 securities, assembled from 31 l1_code slices x 2 is_new states and cross-checked against offset paging) -- and none of it is asserted against the network; the rows are inlined as fixtures. (1) is_new='N' EXISTS, AND THE DEFAULT REQUEST HIDES IT. The task brief left this open and the answer is yes: 2,004 superseded assignments with a populated out_date, over 1,645 securities. They are reachable ONLY by sending is_new='N' explicitly. A bare request returns 3,000 rows with has_more=True and offset=3000 returns the remaining 2,889; all 5,889 are is_new='Y' with an empty out_date, one row per security, and 5,889 is exactly what the 31 l1_code slices sum to with 5,889 distinct ts_code and no duplicate. is_new='' behaves like the bare request and is_new='Y,N' and is_new='A' return zero rows, so no request shape returns both halves. A fetch that omits the parameter therefore stores a current snapshot indistinguishable from a complete history -- no truncation flag, no short count -- which is why _index_member_all_params refuses to default it and why the request subject is the pair (l1_code, is_new). (2) THE WHOLE CORPUS IS BACKFILLED, AND THE REVISION IS ERASED. Every one of the 7,893 rows is labelled with an SW2021 node: the 31 distinct l1_code values used are exactly SW2021's 31, and the SW2014-only L1 801020.SI 采掘 appears on none. The earliest in_date is 1984-05-09 (000639.SZ), six years before the Shanghai exchange opened, and 12 securities start before 1990-12-19. The vintage dates are derived rather than looked up, from the per-index index_member endpoint this issue does NOT store: 912 constituent rows enter on 2014-02-21 (SW2014), and 535 leave on 2021-12-10 against 393 entering 2021-12-13 with 801020.SI 采掘 losing 66 of its 97 members on exactly 2021-12-13 (SW2021). index_member_all shows neither: exactly 1 of its 7,893 rows has in_date=20211213 and exactly 1 has out_date=20211210, both 301071.SZ 力量钻石, an ordinary single-name move. So the taxonomy revision is not merely relabelled here, it is undetectable from these rows, and the largest transitions visible are the annual constituent reviews instead (613 assignments start 2021-07-30, 255 on 2022-07-29, 124 on 2017-06-29). (3) THE DISTANCE FROM THE OTHER ENDPOINT IS MEASURED UNDER A STATED RULE. Over the 7,571 SSE sessions from 1990-12-19 to 2021-12-10, index_member_all answers 12,675,906 (name x session) pairs. Tushare's per-index index_member names exactly one L1 for 9,566,861 of them; it is silent on 2,561,228 and names two L1s at once on 547,817, and neither of those counts as agreement or as disagreement. Of the 9,566,861 comparable pairs 1,038,252 disagree -- 10.85% of them, 8.19% of all the answers, over 1,039 distinct securities -- and the largest flows are 轻工制造 -> 纺织服饰 at 37,591 name-sessions, 基础化工 -> 汽车 at 27,783 and 电力设备 -> 机械设备 at 21,693. That is a disagreement between two endpoints and NOT a measurement against the classification in force: index_member is backfilled too, giving the SW2021-created L1 环保 149 constituent rows of which 100 start before 2021-12-13 (earliest 1999-12-30), 石油石化 47 of 54 and 美容护理 28 of 34. The structural claim in (2) needs no witness and is the load-bearing one. The task-33 review found the earlier figures here (1,461,237 / 11.5% / three named flows) irreproducible; these are what a stated rule gives. Disclosed as every_pre_2021_answer_is_a_backfill and the_taxonomy_revision_itself_is_erased. (4) THE CLOCK CLOSES IT, AND THE ROW IS SPLIT RATHER THAN HELD. available_time is the later of the row's own event and the taxonomy's effective date, and a response row becomes one or two panel rows -- an opening row dated at in_date and, for the 2,004 closed intervals, a closing row dated at out_date -- exactly as stock_basic's registry row is split into a listing and a delisting. The taxonomy floor is what makes a pre-2021 read block with not_yet_knowable rather than answer. The split is what makes any other read possible at all: V2-P1-010 first shipped a single row held back to its out_date, which is fail-closed but was described as a 4.02% row-level residue and is not one -- the readiness gate compares a PARTITION's max_available_time, so one 2024 close held its whole in_date year past every earlier as_of. Measured on the stored 7,893-row corpus at as_of 2023-06-30: 29 of the 38 requestable years blocked outright and the 9 that read held 118 securities between them, no usable cross section at any historical as_of before 2026-07-31. Split, the same corpus reads 37 of 38 years and 5,270 securities there, and 617 rows whose out_date is at or after 2021-12-13 still keep their termination invisible until it happens. The cost the split adds is the one direction that is fail-OPEN -- a read that skips the year an interval closed in reassembles it as never ending -- and it is closed by a rule rather than a note: load_industry_histories compares the years asked for against the years the store holds and bounds the histories at the year before the first stored partition it skipped, after which assignment_on and is_classified_on refuse. Disclosed as a_partial_year_read_cannot_see_an_interval_close and no_cross_section_before_the_taxonomy_is_readable_at_all. (5) THE INTERVAL IS CLOSED AT BOTH ENDS AND A GAP IS REFUSED. out_date is the last day the assignment held: 1,955 of the 2,004 transitions have the successor's in_date on the very next SSE session after out_date, zero securities have two assignments covering one day, and every one of the 5,889 has exactly one open assignment. Every out_date is an SSE session; 21 in_date values over 14 distinct days are not, 11 of those days preceding 1990-12-19 where the calendar does not reach and three not -- the Sundays 2022-01-09 and 2022-07-17 (7 Beijing-board rows) and the 端午 holiday 2026-06-19 (301583.SZ, 001248.SZ) -- so nothing here assumes an endpoint is a session. The other 49 transitions are real holes and assignment_on raises rather than carrying the older label across them: 000639.SZ ST西王 is 社会服务 through 2002-08-29 and unclassified for 4,103 sessions until 2019-07-24, 000716.SZ 黑芝麻 for 3,428, 600365.SH ST通葡 for 3,299, and the shortest is 002674.SZ 兴业科技 at 45. Which 49 they are needs a calendar: IndustryReclassification.is_not_calendar_adjacent flags 442 of the 2,004 and 393 of those merely cross a weekend or a holiday (237 three-day deltas, 48 ten-day), so is_across_a_gap is exact only when reclassifications(sessions=...) is given one. is_classified_on answers the same question as a value, because an unclassified name is ordinary rather than an error. (6) THE FIRST in_date IS NOT A LISTING DATE. For 4,325 of the 5,875 securities the registry also carries, the first in_date PRECEDES the stock_basic list_date (600844.SH classified from 1993-10-08, listed 1994-03-11); 1,307 coincide exactly and 243 fall after, the extreme being 600841.SH 动力新科, listed 1994-03-11 with no assignment until 2022-07-29, 6,903 sessions later. So it is neither a listing date nor an event this dataset explains. (7) COVERAGE IS 99.98% TODAY AND 97% IN 2015. Of the 5,539 securities stock_basic reports listed on 2026-08-07, 5,538 have a current assignment; the one exception is 920038.BJ 森合高科, listed 2026-08-05, four days before the probe -- a classification lag, not a hole. Point-in-time coverage is materially worse because the 49 holes sit inside listed lives: 5,358 of 5,363 (99.91%) on 2024-06-28, 3,814 of 3,876 (98.40%) on 2020-06-30, 2,694 of 2,776 (97.05%) on 2015-06-30, 1,784 of 1,869 (95.45%) on 2010-06-30 and 913 of 973 (93.83%) on 2000-06-30. In the other direction 14 of the corpus's 5,889 codes are absent from the 5,878-row registry, including the two withdrawn IPOs 000991.SZ 通海高科 and 002525.SZ 胜景山河 that KNOWN_UNIVERSE_LIMITATIONS already names and T00018.SH, which is the registry's T600018.SH under a third spelling. industry_coverage_report separates classified, unclassified and unknown_to_registry and its classified_ratio is None rather than 0.0 or 1.0 for an empty universe, so a threshold check has to answer that case instead of reading a plausible number off it. There is deliberately no beyond_snapshot bucket, unlike ConstituentListingReport's: this report starts from universe.listed_on(day), which refuses a day past the snapshot outright, so the horizon is a refusal of the question rather than a verdict about some of its codes and such a field could never hold anything. (8) THE TREE IS A REPORT, NEVER A PRECONDITION. index_classify(src=SW2021) returns all 511 nodes in one response (31 L1 / 134 L2 / 346 L3) and SW2014 returns 359 (28 / 104 / 227); the bare request, src='' and any level without a src all answer SW2014, which is NOT the vintage index_member_all speaks, so _index_classify_params refuses an unstated vintage rather than defaulting it. src='SW', 'CI' and 'SW2014L1' return zero rows rather than an error. 25 membership rows name l3_code=850412.SI 特钢, which is absent from the SW2021 tree's 346 and resolves through index_classify(index_code=850412.SI) as an SW2014 L3 with parent_code 230100 and a null is_pub -- while those same rows' l1_code and l2_code are SW2021's. In the other direction 3 SW2021 L2 nodes and 9 L3 nodes are named by no membership row. So IndustryTree.ancestry refuses an unknown node and nothing in SecurityIndustryHistory consults the tree; requiring the join would discard 25 real rows, which is the answer constituent_listing_report reached for the same shape. is_pub is nullable and the null is data: all 227 SW2014 L3 rows carry it while SW2021's carry '1' or '0' (10 of 134 L2 and 87 of 346 L3 are '0'). (9) THE CAP IS 3,000, THE LOWEST IN THE TABLE, AND limit ONLY NARROWS. A bare index_member_all request returns exactly 3,000 rows with has_more=True and limit=3001, 5000 and 10000 all return the same 3,000, while limit=100 returns 100 -- so 3,000 is the server's own ceiling, as index_weight's 7,000 is. The task brief said limit was ineffective in both directions and that is wrong. offset DOES work here, unlike the paging namechange was measured to break on: offset=3000 returns 2,889 with has_more=False and offset=5000 returns 889, and the two default pages sum to exactly the 5,889 the slices give with no duplicate. It is still not used, because a descriptor's guarantee is about one response and a paging loop's is about the caller. Slicing by l1_code x is_new keeps every one of the 62 requests far under the cap: the largest is 801890.SI 机械设备 at 625 current plus 229 superseded. The superseded half is the one to watch and it grows in steps rather than continuously -- 439 rows at the end of 2015, 801 at the end of 2020, 2,004 today, with 587 added by the 2021 revision alone. index_classify's cap is unmeasurable from outside exactly as stock_basic's is: the 511-row tree returns has_more=False, limit=100000 also returns 511 with has_more=False, and limit=511 returns 511 with has_more=True, so the flag turns True at whatever effective limit is in force. Both descriptors therefore demand the flag, taking the table to six. (10) THE SECURITY IS THE SUBJECT, AND THE WRITE GUARD HAS A BLIND SPOT IT NAMES. index_member_all has no date filter, so one fetch spans 1984..2026 and the merged batch is split into one partition per membership-event year -- the year an assignment opened or the year it closed, since those are two rows -- as stock_basic is split by lifecycle year. The subject column holds the security, so _refuse_to_drop_stored_subjects blocks a per-l1_code backfill loop, which would otherwise leave each year holding whichever slice ran last. What it cannot see is a loop over the MEMBERSHIP STATE: an is_new='Y'-only pass carries every security and produces a complete-looking corpus with no history at all, which no stored-data check can distinguish from a market where nobody was ever reclassified. That is stated in write_industry_memberships and closed on the request side instead, by the refusal in (1). The tree is filed under its vintage's own effective year -- 2014 and 2021 -- so the two vintages never contend for a partition and need no subject guard. (11) MUTATION-TESTED. Thirty-three mutations of these guards were applied one at a time with __pycache__ cleared before each run; all thirty-three were killed. They covered the three availability bounds separately (dropping the taxonomy floor, dropping the out_date bound, replacing either max with min) plus revision_time raised to the fetch instant; is_backfilled's boundary widened to <=, forced to False, and its day count zeroed; all three endpoints of covers(); the gap refusal and is_classified_on; the single-open, overlap and undated-taxonomy rules in build_security_industry_history; the parent-chain, vintage-mixing and rooted-L1 rules in build_industry_tree; classified_ratio's None branch and the coverage report's unclassified bucket; both request refusals on each endpoint (defaulting is_new to current, accepting an unknown state, defaulting src to the endpoint's own SW2014, accepting an undated src); the is_pub null branch and the out_date null branch; the 3,000 cap raised to 6,000; both truncation-flag demands; the membership writer's subject guard; and the read-side taxonomy switched to SW2014. Two of the thirty-three initially reported as skipped because the harness's anchor text was wrong rather than because they survived, and one reported a kill that was a duplicate-keyword syntax error; all three were re-written against the real source and killed by test_a_tree_request_without_a_vintage_is_refused_rather_than_defaulted, test_the_membership_projection_stores_the_codes_and_drops_the_names and test_both_industry_descriptors_demand_the_truncation_flag. One mutation genuinely survived the first pass and is now closed: loosening the overlap rule from <= to < accepted two assignments sharing their boundary day, which the corpus has none of only because industry_through is inclusive -- an upstream that switched to an exclusive end date would produce it on all 2,004 transitions. test_two_assignments_that_share_their_boundary_day_are_refused now kills it. The task-33 review then added sixteen more against the fixes above, again one at a time with __pycache__ cleared: fifteen were killed and one survives as an equivalent mutant. The killed ones cover the calendar-day predicate at > 3 and > 400 (the two the review found surviving, now killed by a real Friday-to-Monday transition), is_across_a_gap ignoring the calendar it was given, the session count taken inclusive of the out_date, a missing calendar reported as zero rather than None, level_one_count counting L2 and nodes_at ignoring its level (both previously untestable against a one-node-per-level fixture), the row split emitting only its opening half, the opening half keeping its out_date, the clock dropping the taxonomy floor, the split treating a blank out_date as an end date, the fold preferring the open half over the close, the fold accepting two different closes, and both halves of the answerable-through bound. The survivor is widening _optional_industry_date_text to accept '' again: the split normalises a blank out_date before the parser sees it, so no input can reach that branch and the mutant is equivalent.

feature_name: Financial statements with an ambiguity that is carried rather than resolved
feature_description: income, balancesheet, cashflow and fina_indicator wired onto the descriptor table as V2-P1-011's dataset (8), plus the StatementHistory/ReportFiling contracts that answer 'what did this security's filing say, as of day D'. The endpoints share the key (ts_code, end_date, ann_date) and that key does not identify a row: measured over a 53-security sample paged to exhaustion on 2026-08-09, 633 of income's 3,201 keys carry more than one row, 1,244 of balancesheet's 3,170, 718 of cashflow's 2,849 and 2,671 of fina_indicator's 3,270 (81.7%). Both rows of a corrected pair carry the SAME ann_date, so no clock can order them, and fina_indicator has no update_flag column at all. build_statement_history collapses the duplicates whose stored values are equal -- which is not a choice of version but the observation that there is only one answer -- and ReportFiling.value_of raises AmbiguousReportError, per field, on what is left. 'Equal' means equal INSIDE THE STORED PROJECTION and not upstream: 2,194 of fina_indicator's 2,671 duplicate keys and 1,166 of balancesheet's 1,244 agree across all 108 and all 152 served fields, while the collapse reads only the 10/7/5/11 columns the descriptor requests and therefore folds more (2,223 and 1,205 rows). Re-measured over a 76-security sample on 2026-08-09 with every response field fetched, 133 of the 5,658 keys that collapse in the projection carry rows the endpoint served differently -- 0 income / 60 balancesheet / 27 cashflow / 46 fina_indicator, half of balancesheet's real disagreement -- in fix_assets (45), cip (25), accounts_pay, contract_liab, others, assets_yoy, eqt_yoy and undistr_porfit (000002.SZ's 2025 annual gives it as None and as -44,418,597,816.52). That is the named limitation the_merge_rule_is_agreement_in_the_projection. Nothing ranks update_flag: on the differing pairs the 1 row is the richer one 156/31/284 times and the 0 row 10/3/23 times, and on 3 of income's duplicate keys both rows carry the same flag. The disagreement reaches headline numbers -- income.ebit at opposite signs, revenue at 4.6%, n_income_attr_p at 3.1%, balancesheet.total_share at 2.5%, fina_indicator.bps at a factor of ten -- so picking either version silently is a factor-level error rather than a rounding one. A read that skips a stored announcement year is bounded rather than silently narrow: load_statement_histories compares the years asked for against store.registered_years and sets StatementHistory.answerable_through to the year before the first stored partition it skipped, so 920403.BJ's 2024-01-05 restatement of its 2022 annual cannot be missed in silence.
notes: V2-P1-011 (PRD Story S6/S9; roadmap section 6 dataset 8 and section 7; depends on V2-P1-004; depended on by V2-P1-017 label contracts, V2-P2-002 revision injection and P3 factors). Every number is from a live probe of all four real endpoints on 2026-08-09 -- 53 securities spread across stock_basic's 5,539 listed codes plus six long-history names, each paged to exhaustion. Three roadmap/brief claims were refuted and are corrected in code: (1) f_ann_date >= ann_date held with 'zero violations' over a 65-row window but is violated 116 times in this sample (49 income / 16 balancesheet / 51 cashflow rows), and Timeline refuses a revision_time before available_time, so _announcement_timeline RAISED on real rows until it was changed to max(ann_date, f_ann_date); (2) income's 14 duplicate pairs for 000001.SZ were reported as having 0 byte-identical-apart-from-the-flag members, when 11 of the 14 are exactly that; (3) the per-response cap is 100 for balancesheet and fina_indicator but is NOT 100 for income and cashflow, which returned 127 and 90 rows with has_more=False and whose caps are unmeasurable from outside. The whole-market fetch shape is one (security, year) window per request: ts_code is mandatory (there is no cross-section) and a comma-joined list returns zero rows with code=0 on income, balancesheet AND cashflow alike (4/6/5 rows for one code against 0/0/0 for the pair, re-measured 2026-08-09) while fina_indicator is the one endpoint that answers with both securities' rows, while the largest measured window is 15 rows against the 100 cap. fina_indicator names its report-period year as a second subject because its start_date/end_date filter end_date rather than ann_date, so a window derived from as_of could never return an annual report. Year-window assembly was cross-checked against offset paging: 162 vs 162 rows for 000001.SZ balancesheet and 117 vs 117 for 600519.SH income with zero rows on either side only, and the one fina_indicator row a 1990..2026 sweep missed is end_date=19891231, which is why the corpus starts at 1989. 24 of 24 mutants of the collapse rule, the refusal, the point-in-time reads, the clock, the request shape and the ingest guards were killed, and the review pass added 10 more -- ordering latest_filing_on by announcement rather than period, comparing only the second version in value_of and disagreeing_fields, comparing only the first version in _collapse, a 1e-5 relative tolerance in _collapse, counting one disagreeing field per filing in financial_ambiguity_report, dropping the sort in build_statement_history, and dropping, loosening or bypassing the answerable_through and finite-value guards -- all 10 killed. The refusal cost is measured end to end rather than modelled: the whole corpus was driven through TushareProvider.fetch_panel, write_financial_statements into a real PanelStore and back out through load_statement_histories, and every (filing, projected column) pair was then actually read -- 1,288 refusals out of 104,415 reads (1.23% FOR THIS PROJECTION -- a wider one would refuse more), concentrated as ebit 258/288 on income, free_cashflow 450/450 on cashflow, fcff 441/507 on fina_indicator and total_share 34/43 on balancesheet. Over the same partitions the clock-derived PartitionCoverage.revised_row_count reads 55/59/23/0, which are exactly the rows where f_ann_date genuinely post-dates ann_date and none of the same-day corrections; the update_flag label census reads 2,397/1,439 for income, 2,907/1,509 for balancesheet, 2,120/1,447 for cashflow and is empty for fina_indicator. Assembling the corpus took 847/859/731/1,028 (security, year) requests for 53 securities, so a whole-market backfill of all four endpoints is on the order of 3.6e5 requests.

feature_name: Panel health report that separates this fetch's defects from the datasets' inherent limits
