feature_description: Aggregate every dataset's health instrument into one structured report at a stated as_of: evaluate_readiness's twelve codes carried through unchanged, a freshness bound derived per publication cadence (the calendar's own longest closure for the daily datasets, its widest month-end gap for index_weight, the 31 October to 30 April statutory disclosure interval for the statement datasets, and no event-clock bound at all for the event-driven ones), the four cross-dataset checks no single dataset can make (declared subject containment, daily vs daily_basic close agreement, unpriced names a halt does not explain, and the two return paths), plus revision and duplicate-version counts. The eight KNOWN_* registries fold into 55 entries that ride alongside the findings rather than among them -- the ten-dataset acceptance store carries the 45 that touch it -- and a finding a known limitation could explain names it.
notes: V2-P1-012 (PRD Stories S13/S69; roadmap acceptance 'an injected defect can be reported'; depends on V2-P1-003..011; depended on by V2-P1-013's fail-closed gate, 015's CLI and 016's REST/SDK face). This issue aggregates and adds nothing to any dataset module. Eleven defects are injected into a ten-dataset store built at run time and each is asserted to be named: partition_missing, partition_file_missing, partition_file_unreadable, date_gap, stale, coverage_stale, subject_set_disagreement, close_disagreement, return_path_disagreement, unexplained_unpriced and ambiguous_filing -- and the healthy panel is asserted to produce zero findings, because a report that fires on a healthy panel is one every reader switches off. Four judgements are recorded rather than assumed. The freshness bounds live here and not on a ReadinessRequirement because a bound that blocks a read and a bound that prints a line cost different things; three of the four are derived from the supplied calendar or cited from the disclosure rules, and the event-driven datasets get no event-clock bound at all, with fetch_age reported in its place. On any real exchange calendar the daily bound is the Spring Festival closure plus a day, i.e. 12 to 13 days for the whole year, so stale is not the check that catches a panel that stopped -- date_gap is, and it can only fire on the three price-shaped datasets that carry a required_dates; the other twelve waive it structurally and their date holes are visible on readiness.checks_waived and nowhere else. Severity is HEALTH_CODE_SEVERITY, a total function of the code rather than an argument at each emission site, and is pinned entry by entry: revision and duplication are notices because V2-P1-011 measured that 81.7% of fina_indicator's keys carry more than one row -- a report that called that a defect would fire on every healthy financial partition -- while every disagreement between two datasets is a warning, including an unexplained unpriced name at any share of the session, because the write-time guard already refuses what a measure relative to neighbouring sessions can see. is_clean is 'no blocking and no warning' and is pinned in both directions: a panel carrying only notices is clean with a non-empty findings, and a panel carrying a close_disagreement is not. And a dataset whose coverage record no longer describes what is on disk is withheld from the composition check and from the revision counts rather than compared -- a guarantee of the store's own write path, since nothing re-reads a partition to corroborate its record, so a Parquet file swapped underneath the catalog by anything other than the store is not caught here.

feature_name: Fail-closed dependency gate that refuses instead of answering empty
feature_description: The fail-closed dependency gate V2-P1-013 asks for: given the datasets, years and sessions a downstream is about to read, either a clearance or an explicit refusal with reasons -- never an empty result a caller reads as 'there was nothing there'. Blocking is GATE_CODE_BLOCKS, a verdict for every one of the twenty PANEL_HEALTH_CODES, so a code added upstream fails a test here instead of being waved through. It blocks exactly the severities is_clean counts, all twelve blocking and all five warning codes and none of the three notices, and the two tables are stated separately and asserted to agree rather than one being derived from the other. WHY WARNINGS BLOCK: an adj_factor partition missing its ex-rights row is ready with issues == [] -- adjustment_requirement waives required_dates, so there is no session census for the hole to show in -- and the only code that can see it is return_path_disagreement, a warning: 000001.SZ's published pre_close of 10.94 against the 11.30 the surviving factors imply, a gap of 0.36 against a tolerance of 0.010017. A gate blocking on 'blocking' alone would clear that panel and let -0.530973% through against a true +2.742251%, sign reversed. WHY NOTICES DO NOT: V2-P1-011 measured 81.7% of fina_indicator's keys carrying more than one row, so a gate refusing duplication would refuse every real financial panel and be switched off; each notice is already refused where it is finer to do so, in financial_ambiguity_report. CHECKS_WAIVED: twelve of the fifteen declared datasets waive required_dates structurally (measured, not estimated), so neither blocking on a waiver nor clearing on one is right. Exactly one dataset is both on the daily cadence and waives it -- adj_factor, measured over all fifteen and now pinned by an assertion -- and for that one the gate asks whether a session-scoped cross-check (close_agreement, unpriced_explained, return_paths) actually ran over it; if none did it refuses with unverified_daily_coverage rather than clearing on registration, files, fields and freshness, which is the exact set the Task 29 panel passed while holed. THE CLEARANCE CARRIES ITS OWN WIDTH: those three checks run on DependencyRequest.sessions and nothing else, so a check having run corroborates the named sessions and says nothing about the rest of the year -- with the ex-rights adj_factor row removed, naming 2026-01-15 or 2026-01-16 clears with is_clean and no notice and the ungated adjusted_return still answers -0.530973%, and close_disagreement and unexplained_unpriced seeded on an unnamed session clear the same way. The read side cannot close that residue (panel_ingest records it as such) and blocking every request whose years reach past its sessions would refuse the ordinary one-session request, so cleared returns ClearedDataset records -- dataset, years, the sessions a session-scoped cross-check actually opened, and the caveat codes still open outside them -- instead of bare names. CADENCE: the roadmap's 'daily' scopes what counts as failure (freshness_policy derives the bound per cadence) and not whose failure counts -- blocking only daily datasets would clear a cross-section request with stock_basic missing, which is V2-P1-008's 92.5%-unpriced shape. THE VERDICT IS NOT A COLLECTION: DependencyClearance refuses bool(), len() and iteration outright, including when cleared, and cleared raises on a blocked one, with cleared_or_none as the named merged shape.
notes: V2-P1-013 (PRD Story S14, Implementation Decision 5; roadmap acceptance 'integration: assert blocking, not an empty success'; depends on V2-P1-012; depended on by V2-P1-015's CLI, V2-P1-016's REST/SDK face and P4's list-level gate V2-P4-023). This issue consumes the health report and modifies no dataset module and no part of panel_doctor. Five judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) Blocking is a total table over the closed code set rather than a branch, for HEALTH_CODE_SEVERITY's reason one layer up: a single entry flipped to False lets a sick panel through while every injection test not using that code keeps passing, so it has to be a diff against a literal a test pins entry by entry. The gate's table and the doctor's severity table are asserted to agree but neither is derived from the other, so a demotion upstream has to be made twice. (2) All five warning codes block, and Task 29's Critical is the argument: a missing adj_factor step is invisible to all twelve readiness codes and visible only to return_path_disagreement. check_unavailable blocks for the mirror reason -- 'I could not look' must never read as 'I looked and it was fine'. (3) The three notices do not block, because V2-P1-011 measured them to be ordinary on this corpus and each is already refused at a finer granularity; they ride on the clearance instead, and a test pins that a blocked clearance's notices do not silently acquire the finding that blocked it. (4) checks_waived is answered by neither horn: blocking on a waiver refuses twelve of fifteen datasets permanently and clearing on one is how Task 29 happened, so the gate asks whether anything in the request's scope read a session of the dataset whose sessions were never required. The residue is named rather than hidden and pinned in both directions: a hole in adj_factor on a session the factor did not step across changes no answer and clears, because factor_on carrying the previous step forward is what a step function means. (5) The clearance refuses bool()/len()/iteration on a cleared clearance too, because an accessor that answers when healthy and raises when sick passes every test written against a healthy panel and fails only in production -- the landmine CalendarDayStatus.__bool__ already refuses to be. panel_health_report's date_timezone is deliberately not re-exposed: every partition records the timezone its dates were derived in, and a gate-level override would judge a partition against a session boundary it was not written to. Layering: panel_gate is a top-level module for panel_ingest's and panel_doctor's reason -- openalpha_cn.panel imports no sibling subpackage, the edges run panel_gate -> panel_doctor -> panel and never back, and panel's import closure is unchanged; its dependency set is pinned to exactly {domain, panel, panel_doctor}, with panel_ingest deliberately absent so the gate cannot build a ReadinessRequirement that differs from the one each dataset's own reader uses. Verification: 44 mutations of panel_gate.py were applied one at a time with __pycache__ cleared between runs, and all 44 were killed; three earlier survivors were closed by adding a for-loop iteration test (list() consults __len__ for a length hint, so it cannot see a broken __iter__), a blocked-clearance notices assertion, and tests for the years_by_dataset and freshness_overrides pass-through. numpy/pandas stay out per ADR-0003, the runtime dependency set is unchanged at 9, and no fixture is committed -- the ten-dataset store, including 000001.SZ's real ex-rights session, is built at run time. REVIEW FIXES (task 36): (a) The load-bearing claim that a session-scoped cross-check having run made 'the hole that would have mattered reachable' was false and was reproduced through the supported writers: with 000001.SZ's ex-rights adj_factor row removed the gate blocks on the ex-rights session and the one after it and clears on every later one, so naming 2026-01-15 cleared with report.is_clean, notices == [], and the ungated adjusted_return over 2026-01-12..2026-01-13 still answering -0.530973%; close_disagreement and unexplained_unpriced seeded on an unnamed session cleared identically. Blocking whenever the request's years reach past its sessions was rejected -- it refuses the ordinary narrow request, and bounding the implied session set needs panel_ingest._sessions_published_through, which this module's pinned import set forbids -- so the fix is that the verdict states its width: cleared returns ClearedDataset records carrying years, the sessions a session-scoped cross-check actually opened (for every dataset those checks touch, not only adj_factor) and the caveat codes still open outside them, with corroborates() answering per session and unverified_daily_coverage riding on the permission it qualifies rather than being resolved by a check that looked at one day. (b) blocks_for and blocked_datasets now match GateBlock.datasets rather than GateBlock.dataset: filed under datasets[0], a close_disagreement answered blocks_for('daily_basic') == () and a subject_set_disagreement answered blocks_for('adj_factor') == (), which is 'nothing wrong there' told to a caller polling dataset by dataset. (c) The fifteen-dataset cadence measurement is now an assertion driven through panel_health_report (15 datasets, 12 waiving required_dates, {adj_factor} daily and waiving) rather than a docstring, so a second dataset in that shape arrives as a red test instead of being blocked forever or corroborated by accident through unpriced_explained's dataset tuple. (d) empty_requirement is reachable through panel_health_report after all -- a price requirement built inside a year that has begun but published no session states required_dates=(), which happens every January -- and now has an integration test. (e) unverified_daily_coverage has a category (unanswerable) so V2-P1-016's grouped facet needs no special case. (f) A years_by_dataset or freshness_overrides key naming a dataset outside the request now raises instead of being silently dropped, and the no-dataset guard no longer prints an always-empty list. (g) date_timezone's exclusion is measured rather than assumed: one store at as_of 2026-01-16 09:00 UTC reports date_gap and is_clean=False in Asia/Shanghai and no code at all in UTC. Twenty-seven further mutations of panel_gate.py were applied one at a time with __pycache__ cleared before each run and all twenty-seven were killed; they cover both accessors matching the filing label again, the category table forgetting the gate's codes and either kind of block carrying a constant category, the corroborated sessions being recorded when nothing read the dataset / never recorded / always empty / dropped on the way in and require_datasets passing none of them, the caveat attached to every dataset and to none, corroborates answering yes for everything, cleared_for and cleared_with_caveat losing each of their guards or answering with whatever came first, caveat_codes answering empty, the corroboration predicate losing its cadence half / its waiver half / inverting the waiver, a cross-check that did not run or that is not session-scoped corroborating anyway, both override guards removed separately and the guard itself neutered, and the no-dataset guard. One survived the first pass -- a block carrying a constant category -- and is closed by asserting both the four distinct categories the seventeen blocking codes produce and the per-code agreement with GATE_CODE_CATEGORIES. Two more had anchors ruff had reformatted and were re-written against the real source rather than reported as survivors. Backend 1707 passed + 1 skipped (was 1689 + 1), coverage 95.26% (was 95.24%), panel_gate.py fully covered.

feature_name: Panel fixture generator driven by a measured shape table
feature_description: A run-time panel fixture generator whose first-class deliverable is PANEL_SHAPES: a closed table of twenty-two forms the live A-share data demonstrably has, each carrying the measurement it came from and a detector that reads the generated artifact and answers whether the form is actually there. The three review passes over V2-P1-010..V2-P1-012 ran fresh mutants and every survivor had one cause -- a fixture that lacked a form the real data has -- so shape coverage is made a property of the generator, asserted in one place, rather than a property of each fixture author's imagination. The guard against the obvious way that could be faked is four whole-table statements: asking for a shape produces it, the shapeless panel has none of them, no detector answers from the request (each detector is re-run against the shapeless artifact relabelled as carrying every shape), and one column hand-edited through ColumnarPanelBatch flips the answer. Since V2-P2-000 each shape also declares, in PanelShape.provokes, the panel_doctor codes a panel carrying it and nothing else reports -- empty for the sound forms, and asserted in both directions against a real panel_health_report, so a shape claiming nothing that starts complaining fails and so does a shape whose declared code stops arriving. write_generated_panel drives the batches through the real panel_ingest writers into a tmp_path PanelStore, so every write-time guard runs against the shapes; nothing is checked in, which is what scripts/verify_publication.py's blocked suffixes require. The six fixture-shape gaps the reviews found are rebuilt from the generator alone and each of the six mutants dies against it, so the coverage survives a later migration off the hand-written builders. The shape table's citations are checked as a table too: every measurement must name a module that resolves under src/openalpha_cn/, and the two constants whose magnitude (rather than existence) is load-bearing -- the session close step and the limit-free sentinel band -- are asserted against the tolerance and the encoding they were chosen from, so neither can be shrunk back into a surviving mutant silently.
notes: V2-P1-014. Test infrastructure, so it lives under tests/ rather than src/: in src/ it would ship in the wheel, enter --cov=openalpha_cn, and have to answer to openalpha_cn.panel's zero-sibling-edge rule, which it spans by construction. At the tests/ root rather than in one subtree because two subtrees use it. Twenty-two shapes over fourteen of the fifteen declared datasets. The earlier claim recorded here -- that namechange and index_member_all are handed back as the domain carriers NameRecord and IndustryAssignment because their panel encoding is produced by providers/tushare.py's own row splitting rather than by a plain projection -- was half wrong and is corrected by V2-P2-000; see OA-PANEL-021. Existing fixture constructors are deliberately not migrated: rewriting them would move a large number of live assertions. Measured at 754ba9e: all six of the fixture-shape gaps the reviews recorded were already closed by the three review-fix commits, so the six mutants die against the pre-existing suite too; what is new is that they also die against a panel built only from shapes. REVIEW FIXES (task 37 review). (a) The generator is now inside the type gate: [tool.mypy]'s packages=["openalpha_cn"] does not reach tests/, so the completion command is uv run mypy src scripts tests/panel_fixtures.py -- 0 errors under the same strict settings src/ answers to, warn_unused_ignores included, which is what makes the eight # type: ignore[arg-type] evidence rather than decoration. pyproject.toml is unchanged and the rest of tests/ is deliberately not pulled in. (b) SESSION_STEP's magnitude was the only thing keeping the sixth mutant dead and nothing asserted it: _has_moving_closes only asks whether the closes differ at all, so shrinking 0.5 to 0.005 left all 21 tests green and revived the mutant. The gap-6 test now requires the generated step to clear pre_close_tolerance at the panel's widest close and to be at least the measured 0.06. (c) The limit-free band is pinned to (99999.999, 0.01), an encoding SSE actually publishes: is_bounded is a ratio test against LIMIT_FREE_RATIO's 2.0, which 200.0 against a ten-yuan close also satisfies while sitting in the empty region between the widest real band (1.4409x) and the narrowest sentinel (115.61x). (d) HEALTHY_SHAPES is 13 of the 19 rather than 11: calendar.multi_session_recess and financials.earlier_period_announced_later are both storable and finding-free, and the docstring's exclusion reasons now cover all six that are left out. (e) Three measurements were re-grounded on a live probe of 2026-08-10. industry.coverage_hole cited 002674.SZ's 45-session hole, which is in the ledger and in tests/unit/domain/test_industry_classification.py but not in the module named beside it; it now quotes that module's own 000639.SZ / 000716.SZ / 600365.SH census. financials.three_versions_of_one_key was a derivation from an excess-row count that a second sample falsifies (54 securities, 3,673 rows over 3,048 keys, 625 excess spread over exactly 625 two-row keys and no three-row key at all); it now cites 002514.SZ's 2022 annual announced 2023-03-15, whose total_revenue reads 684026684.14, 684026684.14, 667399250.52 -- first two agreeing, third moving -- with 000981.SZ and 002682.SZ as the other two witnesses, 4 of 15,801 keys over 277 securities. calendar.multi_session_recess cited an industry hand-over delta distribution for a calendar form; it now cites trading_calendar.py's own 605 closed weekdays and the 2015 Victory Day pair, 2015-09-07's pretrade_date being 2015-09-02. (f) A new whole-table assertion resolves every cited module path under src/openalpha_cn/, which is what would have caught (e)'s first case.

feature_name: CLI face for building, examining and gating the panel plane
feature_description: Three commands wiring V2-P1-007..013 onto the command line: panel build fetches and stores one year through the real panel_ingest writers, panel doctor reports panel_health_report structurally and for humans, and data-check runs the fail-closed dependency gate. The deliverable is the exit code as much as the output: PanelExit is a four-entry table (ok / unhealthy / bad_request / provider_failure) that deliberately leaves 2 to click's own UsageError, so 'the gate refused you' and 'you typed the command wrong' are never the same observation in CI. data-check exits non-zero whenever the clearance is blocked, which is the whole point -- a command that ran the gate, was refused and still exited 0 is V2-P1-013's empty success reappearing one layer up. panel doctor exits non-zero exactly when the report is not is_clean, so blocking and warning findings count and notices never do: ambiguous_filing fires on 8.15% / 1.29% / 15.80% / 13.70% of the four statement endpoints' real filings, and a command that failed on those would be the first thing a pipeline appended || true to. The two commands can therefore disagree about one panel and both be right, because the gate's own refusal unverified_daily_coverage is not a health code; that divergence is pinned rather than papered over. A clearance is consumed only through is_blocked / cleared_or_none -- never bool(), len() or iteration, all three of which raise even on a cleared clearance -- and the JSON carries each cleared dataset's years, corroborated sessions and caveats, because a bare dataset name is exactly as wide as its reader assumes. panel build's targets are a closed table in dependency order in which one target is one unit of work a writer accepts: 'price' is daily + daily_basic + suspend_d fetched in one pass over the sessions, since write_daily_panel takes the pair together and its halts argument has no default, so --dataset daily is refused by name with the coupling as the reason. The session loop is bounded exactly where _session_census bounds its expectation, and the credential never passes through the CLI at all: TushareProvider resolves TUSHARE_TOKEN itself and a ProviderFailure's message -- which can carry the token it was sent with -- is never printed or logged, only its closed-Literal category.
notes: V2-P1-015 (PRD Story S84; roadmap acceptance 'integration: CLI'; depends on V2-P1-013; depended on by V2-P1-016's REST/SDK face, which serialises the same PanelHealthReport -- health_report_payload is written as a standalone function for that reason). doctor was already taken by the provider-credential check, so the panel's health report is namespaced under `openalpha panel doctor` rather than shadowing or renaming it; data-check stays top-level where the roadmap names it. Five build targets, not twelve: namechange, index_weight, the two industry datasets and the four statement endpoints each need a different fetch plan (one announcement year, one index-month, one l1_code slice, ~5,500 (security, period-year) windows per market year) and are refused by name instead of being offered without a test behind them. Every CLI test drives the real Typer app through CliRunner and none touches the network: panel build goes through the real TushareProvider with a scripted transport injected at cli._panel_transport, so the provider's decoding, point-in-time filter and projection and every panel_ingest write-time guard run for real, and the read-side panels come from tests/panel_fixtures.py's generator. Fourteen mutants -- including 'exit 0 when blocked', 'count notices too', 'echo the failure message', 'flatten cleared to bare names', 'always waive halts' and 'follow the flags rather than the dependency order' -- were killed by this suite. V2-P1-016 moved health_report_payload and clearance_payload verbatim out of cli.py into the new openalpha_cn/panel_view.py, which is what 'written as a standalone function for that reason' was a promise about: the CLI's two commands, the three HTTP endpoints and the three SDK methods now render one definition rather than three that agree today. cli._panel_store delegates to panel_view.panel_store for the same reason -- three faces disagreeing about where runtime_dir/panel lives would make every equivalence between them a coincidence. No CLI behaviour changed; clearance_payload gained one additive key, blocks_by_category.

feature_name: Data-readiness REST and SDK face with one rendering behind both
feature_description: The panel plane's three read-side answers over HTTP and in-process, with one rendering behind both faces: GET /api/v1/panel/readiness (DatasetReadiness per named dataset), /health (the whole PanelHealthReport) and /gate (the fail-closed DependencyClearance), paired one-for-one with OpenAlphaSDK.panel_readiness / panel_health / panel_clearance. The deliverable is the status code as much as the body: PANEL_HTTP_STATUS is a five-entry table where blocked is 409 and not 2xx, because an endpoint that ran the gate, was refused and still answered 200 would be no gate at all -- the empty success V2-P1-013 exists to make unavailable, reappearing one layer up. The refusal still carries every block, notice, unverified check and the whole health report it rests on, because a caller told 409 and nothing else cannot act on it. A notice never reaches the non-2xx half: V2-P1-011 measured ambiguous_filing firing on 8.15% / 1.29% / 15.80% / 13.70% of the four statement endpoints' real filings, so a face that refused those would refuse every honest financial panel. health and readiness always answer 200 when the request could be put, because they are reports and grant nothing -- the verdict is is_clean / all_ready in the body -- and the gate is the only endpoint whose 200 is a permission. Equivalence is asserted the way V2-P0B-010 and Task 16 assert theirs: the same input driven once through the SDK and once through TestClient, compared as the same answer.
notes: V2-P1-016 (PRD Story S83, Implementation Decision 23; roadmap acceptance 'REST + SDK equivalence'; depends on V2-P1-003 and consumes V2-P1-012/013/015; depended on by P4's leaderboard face). Five judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) 409 for a blocked gate: RFC 9110's conflict-with-current-state, distinct from 422 for a request that cannot be put at all (a dataset with no declared cadence, a request naming no dataset, a naive as_of), which is cli.PanelExit's unhealthy/bad_request split under this app's existing codes. (2) health and readiness answer 200 about a sick panel: they grant nothing, so their status code claims nothing, and pinning that asymmetry is what test_the_health_endpoint_and_the_gate_disagree_about_one_panel_and_both_are_right is for -- a clean panel that refuses a request naming no session is two right answers, not a bug. (3) exchange and calendar have no default on either face, mirroring DependencyRequest's rule that every field deciding how hard the panel is examined is mandatory; calendar=false switches off every session-scoped cross-check and the gate then refuses a daily-cadence dataset nothing corroborated, which is a decision rather than a default. (4) blocks_by_category groups off GateBlock.category and is total over HEALTH_CATEGORIES: unverified_daily_coverage has no HEALTH_CODE_CATEGORY entry because it is not a fault of the panel, so a grouping through that table would raise on exactly the code this gate exists to issue. (5) The --no-halts waiver is deliberately not reported: halts feeds _refuse_unexplained_thin_sessions and nothing else, so the two builds store identical partitions and identical catalog records, and a field claiming to distinguish them would be invented. That residue is pinned as an equality across all three endpoints (test_a_panel_built_with_the_halt_guard_waived_is_indistinguishable_from_one_that_was_not, using tests/panel_fixtures.py's new write_generated_panel(halts=False)) so that recording the waiver at write time fails a test rather than going unnoticed. Two of the generated shapes can produce a blocking and a warning finding since V2-P2-000 (see OA-PANEL-021), and this suite is deliberately not rewritten onto them: both of those are defects the writers accept, and the panel defect this suite asserts on is the other kind, dug by hand -- the daily partition's Parquet file is unlinked while the catalog still registers it, which is not a shape and never will be. Eighteen mutants were run against this suite and all eighteen were killed, including 'answer 200 when blocked', 'answer 409 when the health report is not clean', 'report a missing calendar as a bad request', 'drop the sessions the request named', 'read cleared instead of cleared_or_none', 'group blocks through HEALTH_CODE_CATEGORY and drop the unmapped code', 'build counts_by_severity from the findings present', 'let with_calendar default to True on either face', 'load the calendar anyway when the caller said this run has none' and 'let the CLI's panel store stop agreeing with the other two faces'. Three of the eighteen survived a first pass and each named a real gap rather than a wrong mutant: the SDK's no-default rule had no test (added), the fixture generator's halts flag was only asserted through an equality that a generator ignoring it would also satisfy (the argument handed to write_daily_panel is now observed: None for the waived build, a non-empty corpus for the guarded one), and the third was an equivalent mutant that had to be rewritten. The acceptance review of this issue found the suite blind to a class of defect an equivalence structurally cannot see: an equivalence compares two faces asked the same question, so a parameter neither face forwards, and a payload key neither side reads, are invisible to it. Of 25 further mutants the reviewer wrote, 5 of 5 status-code/control-flow mutants died, 10 of 16 rendering mutants died and 0 of 4 request-parameter mutants died -- with panel_view.py at 100% line coverage throughout and 19 of the 54 payload keys it renders appearing nowhere in tests/ at all, which is the clearest evidence in this repository that line coverage constrains this class of gap not at all. The worst survivor was the SDK ignoring its caller's exchange and judging every request against a hard-coded SZSE, which the whole suite passed because both sides of every equivalence were handed the same EXCHANGE. All ten survivors are now killed, by assertions of magnitude rather than existence: counts_by_severity is pinned at {blocking: 3, warning: 3, notice: 0} on the hand-dug sick panel and reconciled against len(findings); all three SDK methods are driven with exchange=SSE against a store holding only SZSE's calendar and must raise PanelUnreadableError; index_weight is driven with an index the panel holds, one it does not and none at all -- three different answers through both faces -- which kills a face dropping index_codes on either side; and one 409 block, one readiness issue and the duration fields are asserted field by field, including severity, category, both sides of a four-dataset cross-check, the ten sessions a date_gap names, and 345600 / 75600 / -30024000 seconds rather than 'a float', which kills a renderer returning timedelta.days. Three further gaps the same review named are closed here. (a) The status table was missing the two least guessable cells -- /panel/health and /panel/readiness answer 409 for a calendar that is not stored -- and was missing the internal_error row cli.PanelExit has, so a reader concluded every non-2xx a panel endpoint issues means something about the panel or the request; a corrupt catalog is now driven to 500 through all three endpoints. (b) PANEL_HTTP_STATUS called cli.PanelExit its sibling without recording that exactly one row does not correspond: panel doctor exits 1 on a panel /panel/health answers 200 about, so an alert rule reading only that endpoint's status code never fires -- now stated in both documents and pinned by a test. (c) 409 carried two incompatible body schemas with nothing to tell them apart; every panel refusal now answers {'detail': {'reason', 'message'}} where reason names the row of this table that enveloped it, the two bodies share no key at all, and app.py looks the status up by error.reason so a fault added to panel_view.py with no row is a KeyError at the boundary rather than a mis-enveloped refusal. message is the fault's disclosable text, which never names this service's filesystem layout -- _without_store_path removes both spellings of the store root from a cause that interpolated it, while str(error) keeps it for the CLI and the SDK, which are inside the process that owns it. Alongside these, cli._panel_request now delegates to panel_view.panel_request instead of near-duplicating it (the drift this module exists to prevent, on the request side rather than the rendering side), exchange is checked for build_trading_calendar's own well-formedness rule whatever with_calendar says and its inertness under calendar=false is pinned as an equality, /panel/readiness's silent discard of a session is documented and pinned the same way, and the four top-level panel_* modules' allowlists are now discovered from the directory rather than named one by one, so a fifth one arrives red instead of unguarded. Sixteen of seventeen mutants written for these fixes were killed; the seventeenth ('forward a session from the readiness endpoint') was equivalent, because dataset_readiness deliberately never reads DependencyRequest.sessions, and its non-equivalent replacement ('refuse a session there') is killed.

feature_name: Fail-closed write ordering, both schema stamps gated, and a witness for every dataset
feature_description: The P1 stage review's fail-closed predicate group: three places where a panel-plane predicate said it refused and did not. (1) write_partition renamed the new Parquet into place and then upserted the catalog, with no transaction joining them, so interrupting the second step left the new bytes on disk beside two stale catalog rows -- and because readiness compares those two rows to each other and never re-reads the file, they agreed and the verdict was ready with issues == []. The order is now COPY -> catalog upsert -> rename, with the rename inside the same lock, which turns that interruption into a complete no-op and turns the one remaining window (a rename(2) after a committed row) into a disagreement readiness can see: partition_file_missing on a first write, coverage_stale on a re-write. The idempotency no-op additionally reconciles the catalog's row count against the Parquet footer, so a retry cannot cement that window by answering already written. (2) Two schema stamps existed and two docstrings claimed both were gated: panel-catalog was, panel-batch was not. A coverage record stamped panel-batch/v99 was recorded without complaint and assess_readiness returned ready; both the write and the read boundary now check it against PANEL_BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSIONS_READABLE. The catalog stamp itself had one unguarded entry left, write_partition's read-only idempotency probe, which let a v99 catalog take a silent success on one branch and a replaced partition file on the other. (3) trade_cal carried neither truncation witness -- no measured cap and no required has_more -- on a compensating argument that measurement disproved on both of its clauses, leaving the single source of truth for every date-completeness check on this plane unguarded; it now demands the flag, which a live probe shows is present on every response and does flip when the endpoint truncates.
notes: P1 stage acceptance follow-up to 676cba3 (R4 Critical, R8/R9/R10/R11 Important); companion to OA-PANEL-001/002/003 and the tushare descriptor table. Each fix is stated against the reproduction that produced it. R4: making catalog.duckdb unwritable -- a stand-in for a read-only mount, a full disk, a kill between the two steps and the cross-process writer race this store deliberately does not solve -- produced readiness=ready issues=[], coverage row_count=2 and a query returning the three new rows; after the reorder the same fault changes nothing at all. Recomputing the partition's content hash on the read path was considered and rejected: it is O(rows) re-serialisation on every gate check, so the guarantee is stated narrowly instead -- this store keeps its own two catalog rows honest with each other, and a file changed behind its back remains partition_file_unreadable's eight-byte job and V2-P1-012's deep pass. Four docstrings the review falsified are corrected rather than left standing: store.py's refusing to touch it and its called by every public method that opens the catalog, catalog.py's a coverage record must still describe what is on disk (both sides of that comparison are catalog rows), and test_panel_catalog.py's unconditionally. R8: catalog.py's not_yet_knowable max over max_available_time survived a max -> min mutation against all 1976 tests, because the only test asserting that code used a single coverage record, on which max and min are identical; a cross-year test where only the newest year holds hindsight now kills it. The same change discloses, by name and with a test, that not_yet_knowable is a partition-level judgement over a whole calendar year, so no as_of inside a partition's year can read it through the supported path -- a hard constraint on P3 factor computation and P4 walk-forward, left for P2 to decide rather than changed here. R9: the panel-batch stamp's gate is a refusal rather than a readiness code, for the reason the catalog stamp's is -- an unknown stamp means the record's other columns have no known meaning, and a verdict computed from them is a guess dressed as an answer; the readable set is duplicated in panel/catalog.py because panel imports no sibling subpackage, with a drift pin in tests/unit/domain/test_panel_batch.py. R10: the suite was order-dependent -- naming tests/unit/test_import_layering.py before tests/integration/storage/test_migrations.py failed V2-P0B-007's two structured-logging acceptances in 0.9 seconds, and CI was green only because the default collection order happened to be the other one. Root cause: importlinter.cli.lint_imports calls logging.config.dictConfig, whose default disable_existing_loggers=True sets .disabled on every pre-existing logger, including openalpha_cn.storage.migrations; the calls are wrapped and the flags restored, with a test that the raw CLI still causes it and a source-level check that no call bypasses the wrapper. Unreachable today at <=366 rows a year, and fixed anyway because trade_cal was the only dataset in the table with no witness and no compensating control. Two assertions in test_tushare_adj_factor.py changed to admit the eleventh flag-demanding dataset, deliberately, per that module's own instruction that a later task should change the test rather than read its redness as a verdict. feature_name: Strongly typed label contract from prediction day to tradability
feature_description: V2-P1-017 writes the roadmap's chain -- prediction day -> tradable session -> return window -> limit/halt handling -- as types rather than as a notebook convention. SignalFrame.horizon stops being a free 1-64 character string and is constrained to <1..999><d|w|m|y> (domain/horizon.py); the constraint is a Field(pattern=...) and not a normaliser, so every value this repository already writes (5d, 10d, 3m) serialises byte-for-byte as before and no stored signal_id moves. Only the session unit is countable: the number of sessions in a month is not fixed (a Spring Festival month is far shorter, and trade_cal is amended mid-year), so ResearchHorizon.sessions refuses rather than multiplying by a constant nobody measured. LabelWindow is built from the published calendar -- next_trading_day for the entry (the session AFTER the prediction day, because a session's own cross section is knowable only at 16:30 Asia/Shanghai) and shift(horizon.sessions) for the exit -- so both ends are open sessions and the interval spans exactly the horizon by construction. window_return computes the return on both correct paths measured in V2-P1-007: the chained close/pre_close product, which reads no factor, and the telescoped (close*f)/(close*f) ratio, which reads no pre_close, with session_returns cross-checking every link against the tolerance calibrated on 37,602 real rows. The naive close_exit/close_entry - 1 is carried beside them and never used: on 000001.SZ's 2026-06-12 ex-dividend session it is -0.530973% against a true +2.742230%, with the sign reversed. Eight refusal codes cover the acceptance criterion's boundary cases -- a one-price limit lock on either end (a mere touch does not refuse), a whole-day halt, a timed halt still running at the closing call auction (halt_spans_the_close: 39 of the 59 timed S rows served across 68 whole-market sessions run through the close, 13:00-15:00 being the common spelling, so daily.close is an earlier print no order could have filled at), an unpublished band, an absent bar reported separately from the halt that might explain it, and the three non-listed registry verdicts including a delisting inside the window. build_label_window refuses a timezone whose UTC offset at the signal's own instant is west of -7h, which is exactly the boundary at which dating the signal a day early can put an already-published close on the entry session, and label_outcome takes a HaltCorpus -- suspend_d plus the span it was read over -- so a window reaching outside a year-keyed read raises instead of reporting that nothing happened. backtest.validation.observation_from_label is the one constructor that can answer for an OutcomeObservation's two free floats: it hands OutcomeValidator the two 后复权 closes, so end_price/start_price - 1 IS the label rather than resembling it.
notes: V2-P1-017 (PRD Stories S27/S28; roadmap acceptance 'contract + limit/halt boundary cases'; depends on V2-P1-004 trade_cal, 006 adj_factor and 008 suspend_d + stk_limit; depended on by P3's factors and P4's leaderboards, for which a label is the supervised signal). Four judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) SignalFrame.horizon is constrained in place instead of retyped: signal_id is sha256 over the model's canonical JSON, so replacing the field or rewriting an accepted value would move the identity of every stored signal, while restricting the domain moves none -- test_constraining_the_horizon_field_did_not_restate_any_accepted_value pins that, and docs/api/schemas/signal-frame-v1.json now publishes the pattern. (2) The naive path in OutcomeValidator.validate is NOT rewritten. end_price/start_price - 1 is correct when both prices are on one adjustment scale and wrong when they are raw closes, and the observation cannot tell which it was given; observation_from_label supplies prices that make the expression exact, and the free-float constructor stays because the replay corpus and every existing caller build one directly. (3) realized_return staying 0.0 unless final_action is 'watch' is left alone: it is the POSITION's return, where OutcomeLabel.realized_return is the SECURITY's, and a factor is fitted against the second while a decision is scored against the first. (4) The window-level agreement bound is reported, not enforced -- it is the product of the per-session bounds session_returns has already enforced, so a second guard there would be a branch no input can take. KNOWN_LABEL_LIMITATIONS carries seven boundaries, each traceable to a measurement made elsewhere: a pre-open signal enters one session late, a calendar horizon cannot size a window, halted over-counts before 2015 because suspend_timing is null throughout the early history, an unpublished band refuses every window ending before 2007-01-04, only the two ends are tested for tradability, a delisting inside the window is refused rather than priced -- a survivorship hole measured at 339 terminated names against 5,539 listed, 229 of them since 2020 and 52 in 2024, i.e. 100% of the terminal windows absent -- and a timed halt that ended before the close is assumed to have been tradeable at it. It has no runtime exit on purpose: panel_doctor.known_limitations keys its answers by dataset and a label is a contract rather than a partition, so nothing but tests/unit/domain/test_labels.py holds these to the code.

feature_name: Halt reconciliation, write-time rebuildability, and one definition of a data fact
feature_description: The P1 stage review's positive-counterexample chain on suspend_d: three places where the panel plane accepted, cleared or misclassified something a live corpus proves. (1) build_suspension_day refused a security carrying both an R row and an S row on one session as 'two sources that were never reconciled', and a census of every session of 2015..2026 -- 334,362 rows, no response truncated -- disproves the attribution: one suspend_d request for one session serves both rows, on 73 of 334,289 (security, session) pairs, all 73 exactly one R and one S, clustered on resumption days and on the recent years (1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 11, 13, 13, 8, 9, 17 for 2015..2026). _reconcile_states now lets the S row decide and its suspend_timing choose between halted and interrupted, which is the ordinary rule rather than a new one: 26 of the 73 are .BJ codes daily carries nowhere in that year, and on the 47 it does carry the S row's own timing predicts the bar 45 times, with both misses falling the safe way. halted against interrupted -- two S rows, one untimed and one timed -- has no finer row to prefer and stays a refusal; the census never served it. (2) write_suspensions merged, checked the year and the subject set and stored, never building a SuspensionDay, so a partition its own reader refuses landed on disk and was reported READY (2,293 rows) by panel doctor and CLEARED by data-check while every load_suspensions of it raised -- V2-P1-013's 'a failed dataset explicitly blocks downstream' failing one layer up. _refuse_unrebuildable_suspensions runs the reader's own reconstruction before the write, and panel_doctor._rebuild_check rebuilds every year-scoped partition readiness already called ready, reporting domain_rebuild_refused -- a warning, so GATE_BLOCKING_SEVERITIES stops the gate clearing it -- for the partitions already on disk that the write guard can no longer prevent. (3) cli._PANEL_WRITE_REFUSALS named four exception types where panel_doctor._LOAD_FAILURES named nine, so a SuspensionError out of a real build exited 5 ('a defect in the command, not a verdict about the panel') with its message withheld against a credential it cannot carry. The two lists are now one set, pinned whole by a test, and the refusal exits 1 with the ticker and the session visible.
notes: P1 stage acceptance follow-up to 676cba3 (R1/R2/R3 Critical). Extends OA-PANEL-008 (suspend_d + stk_limit), OA-PANEL-013 (the dependency gate) and OA-PANEL-015 (the CLI's exit codes); companion to OA-PANEL-017's fail-closed predicate group. The R1 semantics are measured rather than assumed -- the 'resumed then halted intraday' reading the review proposed is right for 65 of the 73 pairs and wrong for the 8 whose S row is untimed, 7 of which have no bar -- and the residue is disclosed as KNOWN_SUSPENSION_LIMITATIONS.a_resumption_and_a_halt_can_share_one_session rather than asserted away. R7 of the same review is a no-op at this commit: check_unavailable was already promoted from notice to warning by ade483d, and test_the_strongest_cross_check_failing_to_load_is_a_warning_and_not_a_notice pins it end to end, which nothing did before.

feature_name: Operability: a cap with a way past it, one horizon per panel, and a probe that probes
feature_description: The P1 stage review's operability group: three ways the panel plane worked in a test and not on a schedule. (1) stk_limit's whole-market cross section sat 66 rows under its measured 7,800-row per-response cap and grew +2.231 rows per session over the thirteen session steps 2026-07-22..2026-08-10 (7,705 -> 7,734), i.e. 29.6 sessions -- about six weeks -- after which _check_response_completeness would refuse every fetch of the current year, permanently and correctly, with no escape route any face of this repository exposed (ProviderRequest.subjects is never passed by cli._session_batches, and could not have worked anyway: stock_basic carries 5,878 codes against the cross section's 7,733, and the 2,194 missing are the funds and B shares). The descriptor now declares a measured page_size of 4,000 and TushareProvider._request_rows re-runs the same request as limit/offset pages when, and only when, the one-shot response was refused as truncated -- reactive, so the request count and the wall clock are unchanged until the cap actually binds. Three live measurements make it sound: pages do not overlap, the last page reports has_more=False, and the concatenation is element-for-element identical to the un-paged response, which is why a paged partition carries the same ColumnarPanelBatch.content_digest and the same panel/store.py::_content_hash a one-shot partition would. (2) panel build read its clock once per invocation and the five targets are five invocations, so a build crossing local midnight produced a panel no as_of could assess cleanly -- 144 sessions for daily/daily_basic/adj_factor against 145 for stk_limit on this repository's first live build. --as-of pins the horizon across invocations and is now reported by every build; the same instant is handed to TushareProvider so the writers' own session census (which reads batch.fetched_at) cannot disagree with the loop bound; and _refuse_split_horizon refuses, before the first session is fetched, a build whose horizon disagrees with a session-scoped partition it is not going to replace, naming the exact --as-of that resolves it. (3) doctor --probe sent no request at all for nine of Tushare's fifteen datasets -- four are panel-only, so fetch() refused them by design, and five were handed the empty subject tuple their own params_builder refuses -- and reported both as the same word, configuration, that a missing credential produces, always exiting 0. probe_subjects and probe_plane give every dataset a minimal request its own builder accepts on the plane it is served on, and an authentication outcome now fails the command; doctor --json no longer returns before its own exit check. Alongside: a wrong Tushare token answers code=40101 and was classified upstream/retryable, a quota breach answers code=40203 and the declared rate_limit category had never once been produced, and ProviderFailure.retryable had no consumer anywhere -- a transient socket error 27 seconds into a 45-minute build voided it as invalid_response. _post now translates transport errors into upstream/retryable where they happen and retries four times with jittered exponential backoff, waiting the quota's own window for a rate limit, and the session loop prints a progress line every ten sessions against a build that used to print nothing for 49 minutes.
entrypoint: openalpha panel build;openalpha panel build --as-of;openalpha doctor --probe;TushareProvider.fetch_panel;TushareProvider.probe_subjects;TushareProvider.probe_plane
notes: P1 stage acceptance follow-up to 1ac3b9a (R5/R6 Critical, R12/R13 Important). Extends OA-PANEL-008 (stk_limit's cap), OA-PANEL-015 (the panel CLI) and OA-OPS-* (doctor). Every number in the description is a live measurement made for this issue on 2026-08-10/11 with a real token, and three of them overturned a statement this repository had written down. The cap headroom was disclosed as clearing 'inside one year' from annual growth figures; session-by-session it is 29.6 sessions, and KNOWN_SUSPENSION_LIMITATIONS now carries the per-session rate rather than the annual one. Two docstrings named ProviderRequest.subjects as stk_limit's escape route; the registry cannot enumerate that endpoint's subjects (5,878 against 7,733, the 2,194 missing being funds) so sharding by it would have dropped them silently -- offset paging was chosen instead and measured to be order-preserving, which is what keeps both partition hashes unchanged. And Implementation Decision 33 was cited in review as requiring a fail-closed probe before every panel build; its text says only that doctor makes one minimal request per candidate dataset and that P1's dataset list is decided by that report, so no probe was wired into panel build -- 15 network round trips before each of ~720 is a cost D33 does not ask for. Two pre-existing assertions were changed and both are recorded rather than absorbed: test_tushare_adj_factor.py::test_a_fetch_that_runs_before_the_session_closes now asserts the row is dropped instead of the fetch raising, because its stated premise ('the endpoint serves no rows for a session that has not closed') is false -- suspend_d served two rows for 2026-08-11 at 05:29 that day, so doctor --probe reported invalid_response for a working endpoint every morning; _daily_close_timeline now raises ingested_time exactly as _calendar_static_timeline has since V2-P1-005, and the row is still discarded by the min(as_of, ingested_at) filter. And test_cli.py::test_main_entrypoint_logs_provider_probe_failure asserted returncode 0 for a probe reporting authentication, which is the defect R12 booked. Resumable builds were considered and not done: the unit of work is a whole partition (PanelStore has no append) and _session_census requires every open session from 1 January, so a resume cache is a second on-disk format with its own staleness and integrity questions; the cheaper half of the same benefit -- not losing a 45-minute build to one transient socket error -- is what the bounded retry buys. Runtime dependencies unchanged at 9: the backoff is twenty lines of arithmetic rather than tenacity.

feature_name: One clock the caller cannot move, and a build that spans the years it names
feature_description: The P1 re-verification's two Important findings, both of them about a flag meaning more than it said. (1) V2-P1-018 gave panel build an --as-of and wired the resolved instant in as TushareProvider's clock. That pinned the right thing -- ingested_time is a stored column, so an unpinned rebuild rewrites the partition every time -- and, silently, the wrong one: _decode_panel_rows keeps a row only if it was knowable both at the request's as_of and at the instant the fetch ran, and both halves then read the same caller-supplied value, so min(as_of, ingested_at) became min(as_of, as_of). Reproduced offline through the real CLI: wall clock at 12:00 Asia/Shanghai, --as-of two days ahead, exit 0 and a stored adj_factor partition whose max_available_time is 16:30 that same day -- four and a half hours of look-ahead written to disk by the flag whose job was alignment. The provider now takes two instants: stamped_at, which a caller may pin and which fetched_at and ingested_time come from, and clock, the wall clock, which is the only ceiling the point-in-time filter reads. Both properties hold together -- the unpublished session is dropped and the year refused, and a rebuild at the same --as-of still changes neither content_hash, nor written_at, nor the Parquet file's mtime. (2) The P1 gate is `panel build --start 2015 --end 2026` completing and resuming, and --year was a single int: Click keeps the last value and discards the rest in silence, so --year 2025 --year 2026 built 2026 and never mentioned 2025. --year is now repeatable and de-duplicated, --start/--end is a closed range, the two forms refuse each other rather than merging, years run oldest first, and a refusal names the years that finished and the exact --start/--end/--resume that carries on. --resume is year-granular and reads only stored evidence -- a target is skipped for a year when every session-scoped dataset it writes already reaches the last session this build would fetch, which the write-time censuses have already made a whole-year statement about. Live: trade_cal across the gate's own 2015-2026 in 26.6s (12 partitions, 366 rows in each leap year and 365 otherwise), then adj_factor 2015-2016 built and re-run with --resume for zero requests. Intra-year resumption is deliberately not implemented and the roadmap gate now says so: a PanelStore partition is written whole and _session_census requires every open session from 1 January, so a half-fetched year would need a second on-disk format whose worst failure is a partition that looks complete and is not. Two minor repairs ride along: PanelStore.query/profile_query answered the catalog-row-without-a-file window with a bare duckdb.IOException carrying an absolute path, which cli._panel_command classifies as internal_error -- the same misclassification SuspensionError was added to _PANEL_WRITE_REFUSALS to close -- and it is now a PanelStorageError naming the state readiness already calls partition_file_missing; and _refuse_overlapping_pages now states which paging failure it cannot witness (a row inserted between two offset pages shifts the tail past the offset and is never served, producing no duplicate).
entrypoint: openalpha panel build --as-of;openalpha panel build --start;openalpha panel build --end;openalpha panel build --resume;TushareProvider;PanelStore.query
notes: P1 re-verification follow-up to 90beba8, which introduced the first finding while fixing the split horizon. Extends OA-PANEL-019 (--as-of and the panel CLI's operability) and OA-PANEL-015 (the panel CLI). The path chosen for the clock was the reviewer's option (b), two instants rather than refusing a future --as-of: refusing it would have broken _pinning_remedy, which legitimately names an instant on the following day at 12:00 Asia/Shanghai and can therefore run ahead of a wall clock earlier than noon, and it would have left the documented bound restored only in effect rather than in fact. The asymmetry between the two instants is the guarantee and runs one way: a pin can make this provider understate how recently it observed a row, and can never make a row knowable that was not. On the gate: --start/--end and year-granular resumption are delivered and measured live over the gate's own range for trade_cal; intra-year resumption is not, so the roadmap's P1 gate line now carries what is met and what is not rather than being read as passed.

feature_name: Generated panels that are unhealthy on purpose, and the datasets P2 injects into
feature_description: The half of the fixture generator P2's nine injection issues need and V2-P1-014 did not have. Two things were missing and both were invisible because everything was green. First, none of the nineteen shapes could produce a blocking or a warning finding: every one of them wrote a panel the real panel_ingest writers accept and panel_doctor is silent about, which is what makes them fixtures, so the entire 'must report unhealthy' half of panel_doctor and panel_gate was reachable only by unlinking a Parquet file or asking about a year that was never built -- neither of which is a defect of the data, which is what the nine injection issues are about. Two shapes now reach the two severities that count: daily.uncorroborated_factor_step restates a pre_close the adj_factor series does not corroborate, which is V2-P1-006's Critical (adjusted_return answering -0.530973% against a true +2.742251%, the sign wrong and not just the magnitude) and produces one return_path_disagreement warning; financials.announced_after_the_as_of files a report announced three days after the read and produces one not_yet_knowable blocking plus the check_unavailable warning that follows from an unreadable income partition. The second satisfies roadmap section 11's constraint rather than working around it: the same partition at the same as_of is ready without that row and blocked with it, so the refusal is attributable to the injected row and not to not_yet_knowable's partition granularity. Second, the generator declared fifteen datasets and wrote nine; namechange, index_member_all, balancesheet and fina_indicator are now written too, which matters because a dataset with no partition cannot be blocked, cannot be stale and cannot hold a row that is not yet knowable -- V2-P2-003 and V2-P2-004's whole subject matter was unreachable from the generator. write_generated_panel gained a dataset selection so a test that reads one dataset stops paying for eleven, and GeneratedPanel now carries its own frame (year, as_of, exchange) instead of leaving every caller to import three module constants.
notes: V2-P2-000 (the hard prerequisite the P2 scope survey named; extends OA-PANEL-014, which stays the row for the shape table itself). Four judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) The reason namechange and index_member_all were left unstored -- that their panel encoding comes from providers/tushare.py's row splitting, so writing it here would state one contract twice -- was never true of namechange: panel_ingest.write_name_history's own docstring says that dataset stays one row per record while stock_basic splits, because a rename's effective date is published in its own announcement, and name_histories_from_panel_rows is a one-row-per-record decoder. index_member_all really does split, an opening row dated at industry_from and a closing row dated at industry_through; the answer to 'stated twice' there is not to store nothing but that domain/industry_classification.py already owns the decoder (industry_histories_from_panel_rows and _fold_split_rows), so the round trip is assertable -- carriers to rows to store to carriers, with the row count asserted too, since a generator emitting one row per assignment would read back correctly while making a 2026-01-09 hand-over visible to a reader standing on 2026-01-02. (2) index_classify is the one declared dataset still absent, and the reason is the frame rather than the encoding: write_industry_tree files a vintage's whole tree under the vintage's own effective year (2021 for SW2021) and industry_trees_from_panel_rows refuses a stored taxonomy_date that disagrees with INDUSTRY_TAXONOMY_EFFECTIVE_FROM, so it cannot be moved into this generator's single 2026 partition year and a panel carrying it would have to hand every caller a per-dataset year map. That is an interface change to GeneratedPanel and it should arrive with the first shape that needs a second partition year; no P2 injection does, because V2-P2-004 injects a membership change and the tree only resolves a code to a name and a parent. (3) A future row is stored by moving the batch's own fetch instant, not by weakening anything: ColumnarPanelBatch refuses a row whose available_time is after its own as_of (domain/panel_batch.py::_check_visible_at_as_of), so the injection has to be a batch genuinely fetched later than the read -- which is what any corpus built on Tuesday and queried as of the Friday before is -- and the read's as_of never moves. (4) The dataset selection refuses an incoherent request rather than answering it: daily and daily_basic are written by one call to write_daily_panel and cannot be selected apart, and selecting daily with the halt guard on but without suspend_d is refused because _refuse_unexplained_thin_sessions reads the halts back out of the store, so the omission would not skip the guard but run it against an empty corpus where every session has zero halts. HEALTHY_SHAPES in tests/integration/panel/test_panel_shape_coverage.py is now derived from PanelShape.provokes rather than hand-listed, because the hand-list carried a reason -- 'the two industry shapes and the two name_history shapes carry no stored dataset at all' -- that stopped being true the moment those datasets gained partitions, and nothing failed; the derivation is pinned against a literal so membership is still a visible diff. One consequence outside the generator: test_panel_doctor_human_output_omits_the_limitation_line_for_a_dataset_with_none now reads READY namechange rather than BLOCKED, which is the stronger form of the same assertion -- a blocked dataset could have been silent about limitations because the report never got as far as looking them up.

feature_name: Read-side look-ahead injection, paired against the same partition without the row
feature_description: The read-side half of the point-in-time guarantee, injected and paired for three datasets: V2-P2-001 (a filing announced after the read), V2-P2-003 (an index publication dated after the read) and V2-P2-004 (an industry assignment that takes effect after the read). The write side already refused a late row -- tests/contract/panel/test_columnar_batch_parity.py injects a one-microsecond late row at five positions of a 64-row batch and both contracts reject it, and four provider contracts assert no_data with a reason separating not-knowable from not-there -- but PanelStore.query()'s scan carries no available_time predicate, so the only point-in-time gate a reader passes through is evaluate_readiness' partition-level not_yet_knowable, and no test had ever driven a future row into a partition and then asked a loader for it. Every assertion here is a pair over one partition at one as_of: the partition with the injected rows refuses, and the same partition with exactly those rows pruned answers. The pruned half is built by rebuilding the generated batch through ColumnarPanelBatch with the unknowable rows dropped and driving it through the same real panel_ingest writer, so nothing else about the partition moved -- which is what turns the roadmap section 11 attribution claim (the refusal came from the row, not from the year the partition covers) from an argument into an assertion. A third test per issue pins the boundary: the read opens at the injected row's own availability instant and is blocked one microsecond earlier, the read-side counterpart of the <= boundary the batch contract pins on the write side. Each issue also asserts what the domain object answers once the row is knowable, because refusing is only half of a point-in-time guarantee: filing_for hands back 100.0 before the restatement's ann_date and 777.0 from it, constituents_on answers a January question from the January publication while the injected February publication is a real rebalance (one name added, one removed), and assignment_on refuses the day the new industry interval covers rather than carrying the superseded label across it. Two generator shapes were added for the two datasets that had none: index.publication_after_the_as_of and industry.reclassification_after_the_as_of, taking PANEL_SHAPES from twenty-two to twenty-four and the shapes that make a generated panel unhealthy from two to four.
notes: V2-P2-001 / V2-P2-003 / V2-P2-004 (extends OA-PANEL-021, which stays the row for the generator's unhealthy-panel half). Three judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) No row-level available_time predicate was added to PanelStore.query(), which panel/catalog.py lines 135-139 leave to P2 by name. available_time is stored (it is one of the four clock columns every partition carries) so the filter is reachable, and it is still the wrong trade: a filtered read hands back a short partition, and every consumer above this plane reads shortness as missing data rather than as withheld data. build_index_membership refuses a gap in the month sequence; load_industry_histories' answerable_through exists precisely because a read that stops short of an interval's closing row reassembles an interval that never ends and answers with an industry the security had already left; build_stock_universe refuses a delisting whose listing was filtered away. Turning a fail-closed refusal into a plausible-looking short answer is the one trade this plane is built not to make, and evaluate_readiness is pure over catalog metadata with no access to rows, so the partition verdict would have to exist alongside the filter in any case. What P2 owes the partition gate is proof that its refusals are attributable, which is what this row delivers. (2) The injectable unit differs per dataset and is declared rather than derived: one row for income and index_member_all, two for index_weight, because build_index_publication refuses a constituent set whose weights do not sum to 100, so a publication is a set of rows by construction. (3) The industry injection closes the old interval on the panel's last session and opens the new one on 2026-02-02, seventeen days later, so exactly one stored row of the partition is after the as_of and the 17-day delta stays clear of both existing industry shapes' detectors (session_adjacent_handover counts only hand-overs of ten days or fewer; coverage_hole counts sessions strictly between the two ends, of which there are none past the window). Mutation-checked in both directions against the new file: deleting the not_yet_knowable clause, drifting its > to >=, recording min(available_time) instead of max on the coverage row, and comparing partition years instead of instants each kill six of the thirteen tests; blocking every partition that has coverage at all kills nine, which is the half that proves the pruned read really is allowed through. Test-only plus two generator shapes: no src/openalpha_cn behaviour changed, the runtime dependency set is unchanged at 9, and nothing is checked in that scripts/verify_publication.py blocks.

feature_name: Overlapping label windows annotated, and the one contradiction refused
feature_description: V2-P2-005 asks for explicit refusal or annotation of overlapping labels and PRD story S28 asks for purging and embargo over them. Which of the two verbs applies is decided by measurement rather than by preference: a window at horizon h spans h + 1 sessions, so two prediction days one session apart share h of them -- five of six at 5d and nine of ten at 10d, the two horizons this repository stores -- and a contract that refused overlap would refuse every training set that could be built here. overlapping_windows therefore reports every pair of one security's samples whose windows share a session, as a LabelOverlap carrying the two windows, the shared sessions and the fraction of the shorter window they are. It refuses exactly one shape, and that shape is not an overlap: two samples of one security on one prediction day, which is either two horizons entered as one feature row or one horizon whose sessions moved because the calendar under it did. Neither is repairable by dropping samples from one side of a split, which is all a purge can do, so it raises LabelError where an overlap is reported -- HaltCorpus.require_coverage's distinction (a malformed question raises, a property of the market is reported) applied one level up. LabelSample is the (security, window) pair a set is assembled out of, matching label_outcome's own two arguments. Purging and embargo are declared unimplemented rather than approximated.
notes: V2-P2-005 (PRD Stories S28/S93; roadmap 'overlapping label detection, requiring explicit refusal or annotation'; extends OA-BT-012, which stays the row for the label contract itself). Three judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) THE LAYER IS THE DOMAIN, OVER A SET OF SAMPLES. label_outcome is single-security and single-window, has no CLI, REST or SDK face, and its only src importer (backtest/validation.py) takes two of its types and never calls it -- so before this there was nowhere for an overlap injection to be aimed. The three candidate homes were the window layer, an OutcomeLabel-sequence layer, and backtest/validation.py. The window layer is the right one because overlap is a property of windows and needs no prices, no registry and no halts to compute; an OutcomeLabel sequence would make the question depend on whether each label happened to be refused, and validation.py validates one decision against one observation and has no set. (2) THE SCOPE SURVEY'S PROPOSED CONTRACT -- 'overlapping windows must be refused' -- IS THE RIGHT LAYER WITH THE WRONG VERB, and the measurement is what decides it: at a 5d horizon consecutive daily prediction days share 5 of 6 sessions, so refusal would refuse the ordinary case. A run of k consecutive prediction days at 5d yields 5k - 15 overlapping pairs for k >= 5; test_a_run_of_eight_daily_samples_at_five_days_yields_the_twenty_five_pairs_it_should runs that formula at k = 8 against the published calendar, and asserts the per-gap counts (7, 6, 5, 4, 3 pairs at session gaps 1..5) rather than only the total, so a rule that overlapped everything and a rule that overlapped nothing both fail. (3) PURGING AND EMBARGO ARE NOT DELIVERED AND ARE STATED AS SUCH. KNOWN_LABEL_LIMITATIONS.overlap_is_annotated_and_neither_purging_nor_embargo_is_implemented carries the reason: both need a train/test split to be defined against, and this repository has no splitter, no fold and no fitted model for a purge to run between. It also names what this cannot see at all -- two windows sharing no session can still both be driven by one announcement, and a feature computed over a trailing window can reach across the gap an embargo would open -- because naming those needs a feature contract, which is P3's. The test pins that the sentence and the module agree by asserting labels has no purge and no embargo symbol, so an implementation arriving later has to remove the sentence that says it has not.

feature_name: One tradability predicate, two contracts, driven from one stored panel
feature_description: backtest/execution.py and domain/labels.py both answer 'could this session have been traded at its close' and were built from different inputs and never compared. AShareExecutionPolicy reads a MarketBar whose suspended is a bool the caller supplies; label_outcome reads suspend_d's three-valued TradingState plus its suspend_timing window, stk_limit's band through limit_touch, and the registry. V2-P2-007 delivers the agreement rather than a merger: test_execution_label_parity.py stores one generated panel carrying four shapes and drives every (security, session) pair of it through both paths, asserting the label's session-level refusal set and the policy's buy verdict as one mapping over 71 pairs. The one thing that had to be built is suspended_at_the_close, the single supported collapse of a three-valued halt corpus into MarketBar's one bool: the obvious spelling (state is TradingState.halted) is fail-open on the majority shape, because a security halted 13:00-15:00 traded, so it is interrupted rather than halted, while its daily.close is the last print before the halt. KNOWN_EXECUTION_LIMITATIONS names the three places the agreement stops, each with a test named after it.
notes: V2-P2-007 (PRD Story S55; roadmap 'halt-day and limit-day return handling'; extends OA-PANEL-008 and OA-BT-012, which stay the rows for the two contracts themselves). (1) THE ROADMAP'S STATED CAUSE IS OUT OF DATE AND THE REAL GAP IS DIFFERENT. 'suspended/is_st are always False in the existing tests' was refuted by V2-P1-008: tests/unit/backtest/test_execution_published_limits.py sets is_st=True on a real ST ChiNext row (300029.SZ on 2024-06-28, published band 1.54/2.30, the board's 20% and not ST's 5%) and suspended=True on an ordering assertion. What remains uncovered is that the two implementations are unrelated: AShareExecutionPolicy imports PriceLimit and nothing else from domain/price_limits, and no test had ever computed a return across a halted or locked session through it. (2) NOT MERGED, FOR TWO REASONS. The two have different arities -- one order against one bar, against one window of sessions -- and this policy's verdicts are pinned by tests/unit/backtest/test_execution.py against the derived band, which execution.py's own docstring says must not be silently re-decided from a new dataset. A red-team gate that rewrote the thing it measures would measure nothing. (3) THE COLLAPSE INTO ONE BOOL IS THE DELIVERABLE. TradingState.__bool__ raises precisely so the collapse cannot happen by accident, so it has to happen somewhere; suspended_at_the_close is that somewhere, for published_limit_fields' reason. 39 of the 59 timed S rows served across 68 whole-market sessions run through the close and 30 of 2015-07-08's 31 are the 13:00-15:00 spelling, so the naive collapse is wrong on two thirds of the shape it is asked about; test_the_naive_collapse_of_the_halt_corpus_fills_at_a_close_no_order_could_reach drives the same stored rows through both spellings and shows the fill. (4) THREE DISAGREEMENTS, DISCLOSED AND EXERCISED. The registry verdict is not an input at all (MarketBar has no field that could carry one, so a terminated name executes like any other bar while the label refuses three times over); an absent band is derived rather than refused (up_limit=None means 'not supplied', never 'the exchange published none', and the derivation is wrong on 159 of 5,338 names on 2024-06-28); and a one-price session refuses one side here and both ends there (selling into a limit-up lock is the trade that had a counterparty, so the policy fills it while the label refuses the session outright, which makes the label strictly the more conservative). test_every_declared_limitation_is_exercised_by_a_test_in_this_file requires each code to appear at least twice in the module's own source, so a limitation whose test was deleted goes red instead of reading like one that still holds. (5) ONE GENERATOR SHAPE. price_limits.one_price_limit_up publishes an upper band at the session's own close for securities[3] on sessions[1] -- the band is the lever rather than the bar, because restating the close would restate the next session's pre_close and every return chained through it -- and takes PANEL_SHAPES from twenty-four to twenty-five. Without it the generated panel had no locked session at all and the whole one-price half of both contracts was reachable only from hand-written carriers.

feature_name: P2 injection register: one parametrised table, both directions, and the CI gate it is
feature_description: V2-P2-001..008 each inject something a point-in-time contract must refuse, and until V2-P2-009 they were eight arguments in seven files with no harness -- the closest thing being tests/integration/test_research_cycle.py's single hand-written vector, driven through a bare try/except ValueError/else matching the substring 'not visible'. INJECTION_VECTORS is eight rows over seven issues, each carrying what it injects, the exception type and regex its refusal must match, the regex the un-injected read's answer must match, and the two callables that perform its own halves. Two parametrised tests drive the whole tuple in both directions, so a row cannot be added without being executed.
