Four audits sit on top: every declared pattern is cross-matched against every other vector's real refusal text so a loose pattern is red on the first run; every P2 issue must be a vector or a DisclosedExclusion; each exclusion's named test is AST-verified to exist; and this module's own AST is parsed to require that both direction tests are parametrised over INJECTION_VECTORS itself. The gate is no new job and no new marker: addopts deselects exactly one marker, this module declares none, and the python job runs uv run pytest on four matrix cells of every push and pull request.
notes: V2-P2-009 (roadmap T8/D34, 'parametrised injection table + CI regression gate', replacing test_research_cycle.py's single hand-written vector; collects V2-P2-001..008). Four judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) THE TABLE IS THE CALL, NOT A CATALOGUE BESIDE ONE. Task 38's lesson is that a table and an implementation drift apart with nothing failing, and the inversion that closes it is to make inject and clear required fields of the row: there is no dispatch to forget, so a row added without an implementation is a row whose inject does not refuse and whose parametrised test goes red. Verified by adding a bogus ninth row: it fails both direction tests and the pattern-disjointness audit. (2) NARROWNESS IS MECHANICAL. test_no_vectors_refusal_matches_another_vectors_refusal runs all eight injections, collects the real refusal text, and asserts the full 8x8 match matrix is the identity -- so a pattern loose enough to match a neighbour's refusal (the way a register rots) is red immediately, which is this repository's pytest.raises(match=...) rule made into an assertion instead of a review note. (3) THE CI GATE IS THE ABSENCE OF A MARKER. A dedicated marker would make the register MORE skippable, not less: a marker is a name a future -m can exclude, and the one deselection this repository has is what keeps the default suite offline. test_the_register_is_a_regression_gate_the_default_run_cannot_skip asserts the three facts that make it a gate -- markers == ['e2e'], addopts ends with -m "not e2e", this module declares no module-level pytestmark, and the python job's step runs uv run pytest --cov=openalpha_cn. (4) V2-P2-008 IS A DISCLOSED EXCLUSION RATHER THAN A ROW. Its finding is that nothing refuses: a stock_basic partition fetched with list_status='L' is self-consistent on every cross section and require_datasets clears it identically to a complete registry, so an injection whose expected refusal does not exist has no place in a table whose harness asserts one. Padding it in would have meant a second harness whose only job was to make the count right. The exclusion names the test that does cover it and that name is AST-verified, so a rename or a deletion is red rather than a promise that still reads kept. The replaced vector is asserted absent from test_research_cycle.py by name, because the roadmap asks for replacement and not coexistence. Test-only: no src/openalpha_cn behaviour changed for this row, the runtime dependency set is unchanged at 9, and nothing is checked in that scripts/verify_publication.py blocks.

feature_name: P2 red-team gates on a live panel: the injection register's e2e half
feature_description: Every one of V2-P2-009's eight injection vectors runs over a generated panel, because a generator can be told to produce a restatement, a doubled index publication or a halt running into the close and live rows cannot. That leaves one question unasked: do the same gates bite on the panel a user builds? tests/e2e/test_pit_injection_online.py asks it. It builds a real panel from Tushare, reads a real partition back off disk as the batch that wrote it (StoredPartition), puts a defect into it through write_panel_batch -- the same call panel build makes, so the catalog's coverage census is recomputed rather than patched -- and then asks panel doctor, data-check, GET /api/v1/panel/gate over a real socket and OpenAlphaSDK.panel_clearance. Three injections: a row whose available_time is three days past the read (the not_yet_knowable mechanism shared by V2-P2-001/003/004), five percentage points onto one daily row's pct_chg (V2-P2-006's third witness), and a correction of a stored halt's window published after the original (V2-P2-002's shape on the plane panel build can build). Each is a pair over one partition at one as_of -- the injected write and the same write with exactly that row pruned or restored -- so the refusal is attributable to the row rather than to the year.
notes: P2 e2e acceptance. Four judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) THE INJECTION GOES THROUGH THE WRITER, NOT AROUND IT. not_yet_knowable is decided from PartitionCoverage.max_available_time, which panel_ingest.panel_coverage computes from the batch; a Parquet file edited behind the catalog's back would carry a future row readiness cannot see, so the injection would test nothing. StoredPartition reads the partition back using the coverage record's own field census for column order and kind, rebuilds a ColumnarPanelBatch (which re-runs the subject, clock and shape checks and recomputes the digest) and writes it with write_panel_batch. test_restoring_a_rewritten_partition_reproduces_the_catalog_row_the_build_wrote is the falsifiability check: the restored partition must carry the build's own partition_content_hash, row count, availability ceiling, field, date and subject censuses, so a lossy round trip fails there rather than three tests later. (2) THE PCT_CHG INJECTION IS INVISIBLE TO THE CATALOG BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS THE POINT. It moves no clock, no subject, no date and no row count, so readiness stays ready and the test asserts that; _refuse_close_disagreement compares two pre_close values and close_disagreements compares two closes from two datasets, and neither reads the row's own statement of its own return. Only session_returns' third witness does, and the assertion is that exactly one new finding appears, naming the security, the session, pct_chg and the injected value. (3) THE CORRECTION'S HONEST ANSWER IS A REFUSAL, NOT THE EARLIER VALUE. PanelStore.query() carries no row-level available_time predicate -- test_lookahead_injection.py records the judgement that adding one would turn a fail-closed refusal into a plausible-looking short answer -- so the earlier question is refused for the whole partition and the later one is refused because two rows now disagree about how much of a session a halt covered. That is a different contract from StatementHistory.filing_for's, which does answer from the earlier version, on a plane panel build has no target for; the difference is asserted rather than smoothed over. The correction restates suspend_timing rather than suspend_type because an R row beside an S row is reconciled now, not refused -- 73 of 334,289 (security, session) pairs over 2015..2026 carry exactly that pair from one request. (4) THE SUITE IS STILL OFFLINE BY MEASUREMENT. The new module declares pytestmark = pytest.mark.e2e, which addopts deselects, and tests/unit/test_offline_suite.py checks that structurally for every module under tests/e2e/. Also in this change: tests/e2e/conftest.py's labelled fixture read the registry at the price plane's clock, and stock_basic's 2026 partition legitimately reaches the midnight of a security listing the day after the panel's last bar, so three label tests errored with not_yet_knowable; knowable_from takes the maximum over the partitions a read actually touches and stays a property of the artifact rather than of the wall clock. Test-only: no src/openalpha_cn behaviour changed, the runtime dependency set is unchanged at 9, and nothing is checked in that scripts/verify_publication.py blocks.

feature_name: Three surviving-mutant bindings: a boundary operator, a cleared pattern and a detector's scope
feature_description: P2's acceptance ran 33 cross-batch mutants and four survived. Three are closed here, each by the assertion the existing test was one case short of. (1) session_returns' published-return guard is the repository's only tolerance whose boundary operator no test pinned: the existing test places the gap at 0.9x and 1.1x of MAX_PUBLISHED_RETURN_DISAGREEMENT, so widening > to >= left 2181 tests green. A flat session (close == pre_close, so published_return is exactly 0.0) whose pct_chg says exactly one published tick (0.01 / 100.0 is bit-for-bit 1e-4) puts the gap exactly on the bound and requires it accepted, with the next representable gap refused. (2) INJECTION_VECTORS' cleared regex had no narrowness audit at all -- the 8x8 identity matrix covered refusal only, so relaxing any row's cleared to '.*' left the suite green, which is the read that answers nothing that cleared was introduced to exclude. The same matrix now runs over cleared, plus the statement the matrix cannot make alone: no cleared pattern may match the empty answer. (3) PANEL_SHAPES' detectors were pinned on their own shape, on the shapeless panel and on a mislabelled panel, but never against each other, so widening _has_disclosure_after_the_as_of from income to any dataset -- which would collapse V2-P2-001, 003 and 004 into one injection -- was a green change. The full 25x25 matrix is now pinned, with the five containments that really hold declared in CROSS_TRIGGERS. The same task narrows the shape-provocation test to each shape's own declared datasets, which is what PanelShape.datasets and write_generated_panel(datasets=...) were built for and neither caller used.
notes: P2 acceptance review, mutants M12/M24/M34 plus the shape-panel slope. Each binding was verified by re-applying the mutant that motivated it and watching it go red. M12: '>' -> '>=' in session_returns now fails test_a_gap_of_exactly_one_tick_is_accepted_and_the_next_representable_gap_is_not with 'a gap of 0.0001, past the 0.0001'. M24: any cleared regex relaxed to '.*' now fails the cleared matrix on every off-diagonal cell of that row. M34: _has_disclosure_after_the_as_of widened to sweep every batch now fails the 25x25 matrix with income's detector answering for index.publication_after_the_as_of and industry.reclassification_after_the_as_of. THE FIVE DECLARED CROSS-TRIGGERS ARE NOT LEAKS AND ARE NOT WAIVERS. Four are containment of one shape's form inside another's panel: a multi-session recess closes two mid-window weekdays, a factor step restates the pre_close it is corroborated by, three versions of one key contain two, and four statement endpoints contain two. The fifth is the shapeless panel's own withheld bar: with moving closes, the halted name's next stored pre_close is a session no row carries, which reads as an uncorroborated restatement in the bytes -- and a detector that could tell the difference would be reading the generator's intent rather than the artifact, which PanelShape.detect's docstring forbids. panel_doctor does not report it because the return-path check is session-scoped to the requested day. THE NARROWING IS SELF-GUARDING. panel_health_report gates every cross-dataset check on its inputs being in scope, so a dataset left out can only remove findings, never invent one; the provocation test asserts equality, so a shape that under-declares its datasets loses its own code and goes red. Verified by dropping adj_factor from daily.uncorroborated_factor_step's declared datasets: test_a_shape_provokes_exactly_the_health_codes_it_declares fails with [] == ['return_path_disagreement']. Measured 55.35s -> 10.48s over the 25 parametrisations, 2.21s -> 0.42s per shape.

feature_name: Every KNOWN_* limitation registry bound to the suite by structure
feature_description: V2-P2-007 invented a structural binding for limitation registries -- each KNOWN_EXECUTION_LIMITATIONS code must be the suffix of a test declared in the same module, checked off that module's AST -- and installed it on one of the eleven registries. The P2 acceptance measured what the other ten were worth by renaming KNOWN_UNIVERSE_LIMITATIONS.a_listed_only_registry_is_invisible_to_every_downstream_check, the entry V2-P2-008's finding rests on and the one the injection register's disclosed exclusion cites by name: the whole suite stayed green, because the code occurred twice in the repository and both occurrences were docstrings. A per-entry same-named test does not scale to 128 entries and would not be the right shape if it did -- most entries disclose what an upstream does not serve, so there is no branch to drive, and 58 of KNOWN_PANEL_LIMITATIONS' 59 codes are folded copies of another registry's. The binding installed instead is a floor under all of them: every declared code must appear as a string literal in executable test code, where executable means outside a docstring in a test_*.py file, checked by AST. In practice each registry now carries a set literal of all of its codes compared for equality -- the form KNOWN_ADJUSTMENT_LIMITATIONS has had since V2-P1-005 -- which closes 32 codes across six modules that no assertion had named.
notes: P2 acceptance review, mutant M15. THE JUDGEMENT IS THAT 007's FORM DOES NOT GENERALISE AND A WEAKER ONE DOES. 007's binding is one test per entry named after the entry; it is right at three entries and wrong at 128, for three reasons. The volume is the least of them: most entries are disclosures about what an upstream does not serve, so a test named after one would assert about a sentence rather than about code, which is the drift wearing the badge of the fix. KNOWN_PANEL_LIMITATIONS is derived, so 58 of its 59 codes would need their tests written twice. And the AST check enforces the name, not the body -- it cannot tell a proof from a pass statement. The floor installed instead is strictly about naming and says so: it does not require the reference to prove the limitation, only that the registry and the suite agree on what it is called. What it buys is every registry rather than three entries of one, and it covers registries that do not exist yet, because the registry table is checked against an AST scan of src/ rather than trusted. Four attack directions were run and all four go red: renaming an entry (fails both the meta-audit and the module's own set literal), deleting one (the set literal, which is why equality and not membership), adding one with no test (the meta-audit, naming the registry and the code), and adding a whole new KNOWN_* registry (the source-tree scan). A fifth failure mode is guarded by test_prose_does_not_satisfy_the_binding_and_this_is_how_that_is_known: a sentinel phrase this module names only in its own docstrings, spliced from two halves so it is never itself an executable literal, must land on the prose side of the split and never on the executable one -- without which a broken docstring filter would make the audit pass vacuously. KNOWN_CALENDAR_LOOKAHEAD is the eleventh registry and is listed as codeless rather than omitted: its entries carry no code because they are three reproductions of one defect (panel_doctor._limitations() folds all three into the_published_schedule_can_be_amended_after_it_becomes_answerable), so its key is calendar_date and test_trading_calendar.py already pins all three as an exact dict.

feature_name: Every test a source docstring cites, resolved against the tests that exist
feature_description: Source docstrings in this repository name the test that measures each guarantee, and nothing checked that those names resolved. tests/unit/test_source_cited_tests.py scans every module under src/openalpha_cn for a tests/<path>.py citation, optionally followed by ::<name>, rejoins the one line break the prose style produces (immediately after the ::), and resolves the path against the tree and the name against that file's own AST -- functions, async functions and classes, because a citation may name a helper or a fixture rather than a test. The failure lists each unresolved citation with the source file it was written in, because a moved test and a renamed test need different repairs. It is the citation-shaped sibling of OA-OPS-030's KNOWN_* binding: a structural check over a correspondence that was previously maintained by whoever remembered.
notes: FOUND BY THE FACTOR CONTRACT REVIEW, WHICH READ THE CITATIONS ONE AT A TIME. This repository documents a guarantee by naming the test that measures it, which makes the citations a table -- and the repository's own lesson about tables is that only a run of them catches drift (panel_factors._refuse_table_drift, test_the_contract_and_the_store_agree_on_every_rejected_dataset, test_the_registry_table_is_every_known_registry_in_the_source_tree all exist because a hand-maintained correspondence went stale while everything stayed green). Two citations had already gone stale: domain/factor.py named test_factor_engine.py for a test that lives in test_factor_report_periods.py, and panel_neutralization.py named test_every_determinant_of_this_neutralisation_is_either_in_the_identity_or_exempted_by_name for a test whose real name has no _of_this_neutralisation in it. THE ONE WRAPPED FORM ACCEPTED IS A BREAK STRAIGHT AFTER THE ::, AND THAT IS A RULE RATHER THAN A LIMITATION: a break inside the identifier cannot be told from a citation of a shorter name followed by a sentence, and three of the four citations this audit first refused were wrapped that way -- one of the three ALSO naming the wrong file, which a rule that guessed at the join would have hidden. A bare tests/<path>.py with no :: is checked as a file only, because a whole-module reference is a weaker and different claim. The extractor has its own tests, without which the audit could pass by finding nothing: it asserts a floor on the number of citations found, that the wrapped form is among them, and that a mid-identifier wrap does NOT resolve.

feature_name: The Parquet footer reconciled against the catalog on every readiness assessment
feature_description: P2's product acceptance appended one row to a real stock_basic 2024 Parquet file, behind the store, with available_time in 2035. Every fact readiness had still agreed -- the partition is registered, the file is present, it carries PAR1 at both ends, and the catalog's content_hash matches the coverage record's -- so panel doctor reported READY ... rows=152 over a 153-row file, data-check answered CLEARED with exit 0, and load_stock_universe(as_of=2026-08-11).listed_on(2024-07-02) came back with the injected security in it. panel/store.py and panel/catalog.py both stated the boundary honestly and both overclaimed its size: a swap to a different-but-valid Parquet file was said to be 'out of reach of any O(1) check'. It is not. Parquet carries the row count in the footer, DuckDB answers count(*) from metadata (0.3 ms on a 2,000,000-row partition, independent of size), and write_partition's no-op branch already read it. PartitionState now carries file_row_count on the read path too and evaluate_readiness blocks with partition_row_count_mismatch when it disagrees with the coverage record or cannot be read at all -- so every row inserted or removed behind the store is refused. The residue is stated rather than implied: an edit that changes values in place moves neither the magic, nor the count, nor the catalog, and is visible only to a check that reads the column.
notes: P2 product acceptance, blind spot A. Three judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) THE COST WAS RE-DECIDED, NOT INHERITED. Task 26 declined to recompute _content_hash on the read path because that is O(rows) re-serialisation on every gate check, and that judgement stands. It does not extend to the footer: the count is metadata, the read is O(1) in partition size (0.26 ms on a 796,497-row partition), and the same store already paid it on the write path for the same reason. The end-to-end cost is one footer read per requested year, measured on the widest assessment this repository makes: stock_basic over 37 lifecycle years went from 123 ms to 134 ms per assess_readiness call. (2) THE COMPARISON IS AGAINST THE COVERAGE RECORD, not panel_partitions.row_count, and it is sound because the check runs after coverage_stale has passed -- record_coverage refuses a record whose row_count disagrees with the registered partition's, so at that point the two catalog numbers are provably equal and one PartitionState field carries both. (3) THE CATEGORY IS inconsistent AND NOT missing. A tampered file may hold more rows than the record describes as easily as fewer, and filing it under missing would tell a reader that data is absent when the truth is that two records of one partition disagree.

feature_name: The event clock, which readiness never compares against as_of
feature_description: evaluate_readiness compares exactly one instant against as_of -- max_available_time, which answers 'could anyone have known this yet' -- and says nothing about last_event_time, which answers 'has this happened yet'. The two come apart because ColumnarPanelBatch does not require a row's event to precede its availability, and trade_cal is why: the exchange publishes next year's sessions this year. P2's product acceptance measured what that costs everywhere else. One stock_basic row listing on 2026-12-31 and knowable from 2026-01-02 passed the batch contract, passed the writer, was reported READY by panel doctor and CLEARED by data-check with exit 0, and then made load_stock_universe raise StockUniverseError: 999002.SZ lists on 2026-12-31, after the 2026-08-11 registry snapshot. panel_doctor now emits event_after_as_of (warning, so the gate blocks) for a dataset holding an event later than the read, exempting the published_in_advance cadence.
notes: P2 product acceptance, blind spot B. Three judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) THE EXEMPTION IS BY CADENCE, NOT BY DATASET NAME. A blanket 'event_time > as_of blocks' rule would refuse the trading calendar on every panel this repository builds: measured on a real panel, trade_cal 2026 reaches 2026-12-30, five months past the read, while every one of the other eight partitions stops the day before it. published_in_advance is the declaration that already means exactly this, and trade_cal is its only member, so a second such dataset earns the exemption by declaring its cadence rather than by being added to a list. (2) IT IS A DOCTOR CODE AND NOT A READINESS CODE. evaluate_readiness is pure over catalog metadata and cannot see cadence, which lives in panel_doctor; putting the rule where the vocabulary is avoids a new ReadinessRequirement field on nineteen construction sites. warning is the severity domain_rebuild_refused already carries for the same shape -- the read this report clears is the read that raises. (3) IT IS WITHHELD WHEN not_yet_knowable ALREADY FIRED. Both codes are about a row the reader should not be given, read off two clocks; on the three generated shapes that inject a row dated after the read both clocks move together, and _rebuild_check's rule against double-counting one defect in two vocabularies applies unchanged. What is left is the case nothing else catches: a row that WAS knowable, describing an event that has not happened.

feature_name: The calendar's own disclosed look-ahead, made conditional on the panel's horizon
feature_description: TradingCalendar.known_lookahead() says in its docstring that it exists 'so V2-P1-013's gate can see them', and had no caller in src/ at all -- only tests. So the repository's one known real look-ahead reached a reader as static prose: on a real 2015 trade_cal partition (365 rows, covering 2015-09-03 with 132 days of look-ahead) panel doctor --json answered is_clean: true, findings: [], and the three dates appeared in limitations in a sentence that reads identically whether the panel covers them or not. panel_health_report now runs a calendar_lookahead cross-check: with a calendar it reports calendar_lookahead_in_horizon naming the covered dates, their announcement dates and the width of each look-ahead window; without one it records that the check did not run.
notes: P2 product acceptance, blind spot C. Two judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) THE SEVERITY IS notice AND THE ARGUMENT IS NOT THAT IT IS HARMLESS. Three things decide it. It is an inherent limitation of trade_cal, already carried in KNOWN_PANEL_LIMITATIONS, rather than a defect of this fetch -- and is_clean is the verdict on the fetch, which is Task 35's separation. It has no remedy: every blocking and warning code names an action (re-fetch, rebuild, name a session, narrow the request) and this one cannot, because removing the defect needs a revision history the endpoint does not serve. And a warning would refuse, permanently and with no way forward, every panel whose calendar reaches 2015-09-03, 2015-09-04 or 2020-01-31 -- 'a gate that refuses everything gets switched off' is the argument panel_doctor already accepted twice, for the three measured notices and for unverified_daily_coverage's caveat form. What the notice buys over the prose is that it is conditional, names which dates, and rides on DependencyClearance.notices so a cleared caller holds it. (2) IT IS A CROSS-CHECK AND NOT A PER-DATASET FINDING. Three datasets' required_dates are derived from this calendar (daily, daily_basic, stk_limit), so the contamination is not trade_cal's alone and does not depend on trade_cal being among the datasets the request named; and a run with no calendar has to be visibly unrun rather than silently clean, which is what cross_checks is for.

feature_name: The un-gated read named, disclosed on every report, and bound to an allowlist
feature_description: PanelStore.query() is public, takes no as_of, consults no readiness verdict and carries no row-level available_time predicate: measured on a real stock_basic 2024 partition it returns 152 rows, of which 92 were not knowable at 2024-07-01. The point-in-time gate is read_if_ready(), which is opt-in rather than structural. P2's technical acceptance named this the most dangerous seam left for P3, because the factor engine faces a 120x cost for rebuilding the panel per as_of and the natural response is to call query() and filter by available_time itself -- moving the guarantee out of the storage plane with nothing auditing it. Three things now do: query()'s docstring states the gap and the measurement in its first paragraph; KNOWN_STORAGE_LIMITATIONS carries it as a disclosure every panel_health_report shows its reader; and tests/unit/panel/test_query_callers.py pins the src/ files allowed to make the call, so a new caller fails a test rather than arriving silently.
notes: P2 product acceptance, blind spot D. Three judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) NO ROW-LEVEL FILTER WAS ADDED, and the earlier argument still holds: a filtered read hands back a short partition and every consumer above this plane reads shortness as missing data rather than as withheld data -- build_index_membership refuses a gap in the month sequence, load_industry_histories refuses an interval whose closing row was filtered away, build_stock_universe refuses a delisting whose listing was. See tests/integration/panel/test_lookahead_injection.py's 'What is deliberately not here'. (2) NO REQUIRED unchecked=True ARGUMENT. It puts the warning at every call site, which is the right instinct, but it is a breaking change to a published 1.0.0 API for a method with exactly one caller in src/, and a keyword a caller types once stops being read the second time. (3) THE ALLOWLIST IS AN ALLOWLIST AND NOT A BAN. A future reader with a real need may take the un-gated path; what it may not do is take it silently. The AST match is on the call's shape (query with a columns keyword, which PanelStore.query makes keyword-only and mandatory) rather than on the receiver's type, because EvidenceStore.query is a different method on a different plane; a splatted call is the named residue.

feature_name: Every declared dataset has a build target, in two phases
feature_description: The eight datasets providers/tushare.py declared, panel_ingest could write and panel build could not fetch. Before this, PANEL_BUILD_TARGETS held five entries against fifteen descriptors and twelve write_* functions, so `panel build --dataset income` answered "is not one of this command's build targets" and `panel doctor --dataset income` therefore reported partition_missing for ever -- the state P2's 002/003/004 gates and P3's 009-013 factor families were specified against, and the state three independent acceptance passes each reported. The table is now thirteen targets covering all fifteen datasets, each with the request shape its endpoint was measured to have: namechange one announcement year per request; index_weight one index for one calendar month, 3 x 12 = 36 per year, with a month that lies between two publications refused at write time because build_index_membership would otherwise only refuse it on every later read; income/balancesheet/cashflow one (security, announcement year) window, and since ts_code is mandatory and a comma-joined list answers zero rows with code=0 on three of the four, that is 5,881 requests per dataset per year taken from the stored stock_basic registry (or from --subject); index_classify one taxonomy vintage, both measured ones, filed under 2014 and 2021 because the response carries no date column at all; index_member_all 31 x 2 = 62 (l1_code, is_new) slices read off the stored SW2021 tree rather than a literal, refusing a sweep whose superseded half came back empty -- the one shape write_industry_memberships names as invisible to its own subject guard, since a current-only corpus carries every security and no history. PANEL_BUILD_SPAN_TARGETS is the second build phase and it exists because of fina_indicator: that endpoint's window filters end_date while its rows are filed at ann_date, so an announcement year is assembled from at least two report-period years (the annual of A-1 plus the interims of A) and a per-year loop replaces the first with the second -- more rows, the same securities, nothing in panel_ingest able to see it. Accumulating every requested period year into one write closes the intra-invocation half; _refuse_shrinking_statement_years closes the cross-invocation half, measured live: after --start 2023 --end 2024 the 2024 partition holds 9 rows and a bare --year 2024 would write 7, and is refused. _audit_written_partitions runs for both phases (year=None in the span phase), so "a key in the table with no branch" stays exit 5 rather than exit 0 with an empty partitions list, in the half of the command that builds the industry corpus as well as the half that builds prices.
entrypoint: openalpha panel build --dataset namechange;openalpha panel build --dataset index_weight;openalpha panel build --dataset index_classify;openalpha panel build --dataset index_member_all;openalpha panel build --dataset income;openalpha panel build --dataset balancesheet;openalpha panel build --dataset cashflow;openalpha panel build --dataset fina_indicator;openalpha panel build --subject
notes: P3 hard prerequisite, on top of 0e6f112. Extends OA-PANEL-015 (whose notes recorded "Five build targets, not twelve" as a scope decision of V2-P1-015, taken because wiring the rest from a transport that issue could not exercise would have been surface with no test behind it), OA-PANEL-019 and OA-PANEL-020 (the panel CLI's operability, --as-of and --resume), OA-PANEL-009 (index_weight), OA-PANEL-010/011 (the industry and statement contracts). Every number in the description is a live measurement made for this issue on 2026-08-11 with a real token, and three of them changed a decision. (1) The universe cannot be filtered by listing lifecycle in either direction: 688981.SH listed on the A-share market in 2020 and its income window for 2015 returns five rows, while 000003.SZ was delisted in 2002 and its 2024 window returns three -- so a filter that looked like an obvious saving would drop real filings, silently, since a missing security is indistinguishable from one that did not file. (2) index_weight needs a month-END as_of: a first-of-month instant fetches the right window and the point-in-time filter then empties it, because the publication lands on the month's last open session; measured across all twelve months of 2024 and 2026, one 300-row publication each at month-end and no_data at month-start. The same correction applies to namechange and the three announcement-year statement endpoints, which is why _year_end_as_of exists beside _year_as_of rather than instead of it -- trade_cal genuinely wants 1 January, because _calendar_publication_timeline dates a whole year's rows as available from its start. (3) index_classify fetches both measured vintages rather than only the one index_member_all speaks: having refused the endpoint's SW2014 default (which is not the vintage the memberships are labelled with), the remaining set is closed and two requests long, and fetching one would leave a vintage this repository has measured and can read back reporting partition_missing. Each of the eight targets was built once against the live endpoint on 2026-08-11 rather than only against a scripted transport, and tests/e2e/ is deliberately not extended to cover them (its build is already half an hour and a whole-market statement sweep is 2h55m per dataset-year): index_classify 2 requests -> 359 and 511 rows under 2014 and 2021; index_member_all 62 requests in 133s -> 41 event-year partitions; namechange 2024 1 request -> 330 rows; index_weight 2024 36 requests in 67s -> 21,600 rows, which is exactly 12 x (300 + 500 + 1000); income/balancesheet/cashflow 2024 over three named securities -> 11/16/13 rows; fina_indicator --start 2023 --end 2024 -> announcement-year partitions 2023/2024/2025, and the bare --year 2024 re-run refused with exit 1. panel doctor then read all of them back (index_classify 2021 READY 511 rows, index_member_all 2024 READY 380, namechange 2024 READY 330, index_weight 2024 READY 21,600) and data-check cleared them -- which is the state that had been reported as partition_missing for ever. Scale is the part that is stated rather than solved: a whole-market statement backfill is ~23,500 round trips per year across the four endpoints and ~282,000 for --start 2015 --end 2026, and at the rate measured on 2026-08-11 that is days rather than hours: a single request is 1.1-4.6s, and a real whole-market cashflow sweep sustained 295 requests in 529s = 1.79s each, for which the command reported an eta of 10,008s (2h47m) for that one dataset-year and which extrapolates to ~140 hours for the four endpoints over 2015-2026. The account's 500-per-minute quota (9.4 hours for the same work) is therefore not the binding constraint at that latency. Concurrency was considered and deliberately not taken: TushareProvider and UrllibTushareTransport document no thread-safety, and every test in this repository injects a scripted transport whose payload list and ordering assertions are not thread-safe either, so it is a change to the test seam rather than to this command. What is delivered instead is _echo_budget (the size of every fetch loop, on stderr, before the first request), a progress stride that scales (max(10, ceil(total/40)), so 145 sessions and even a 244-session year still report every ten and 5,881 securities report every 148), and --subject. --resume gains a second, weaker rule for index_weight and the three announcement-year statement targets: a registered partition, with no census behind it, because those datasets have none -- a security that announced nothing in a year is absent and indistinguishable from one never fetched. The residue is disclosed on the RESUMED line itself and pinned by a test that reproduces it (a --subject-narrowed partition is skipped), rather than claimed away; fina_indicator cannot be resumed at all and the reason is structural rather than unimplemented. Three pre-existing assertions changed and each is recorded: the whole-table PANEL_BUILD_TARGETS literal (five entries to thirteen, named one by one), _LIFECYCLE_YEAR_TARGETS (renamed _UNPINNED_PARTITION_YEAR_TARGETS and widened from one member to four, each with its own measured reason), and the ten-element _PANEL_WRITE_REFUSALS / _LOAD_FAILURES set, which gains IndustryClassificationError -- the tenth domain error that test anticipated, needed because index_member_all's fetch plan reads its l1_code slices through load_industry_trees and a malformed stored tree would otherwise have exited 5 with the message withheld, SuspensionError's defect in a dataset that had not been built yet when that one was found. test_cli_panel.py's mutation target moved from 'namechange' to a name nothing in the repository knows, because 'namechange' is now a real target with a real branch and the mutation would have silently stopped being one.

feature_name: Versioned factor definitions, content-addressed by the identity helper the rest of the repository already uses
feature_description: V2-P3-001's six properties plus a seventh, as fields on one frozen pydantic contract, each read by code rather than by convention: stable identity (factor_id), version, family, required fields, lookback window, direction, and max_window_sessions -- how many panel sessions the lookback window is allowed to span. The seventh is the correction of a defect the six had between them: lookback_sessions counts a security's own rows and says nothing about when they were, so a name halted for three months earned a '120-session momentum' spanning 210 calendar days, marked computed. factor_id is domain/_identity.py#stable_model_id with a fct_ prefix -- the same canonical JSON that derives ProviderRecord.record_id, SignalFrame.signal_id, DecisionLedger.decision_id and ValidationResult.validation_id -- because a sixth hash function would be a sixth thing that can disagree about key order, ensure_ascii, separators or float repr, and the failure mode of a disagreement is two IDs for one factor. family and direction are closed Literals. required_fields is a tuple of (dataset, column) references validated with the panel plane's own identifier rules. FactorBuildManifest is content-addressed in both directions: what changed must move the ID (subject_digest and universe_digest carry the sets, not just the counts) and what did not change must not (no wall clock on either side -- built_at was already out, and the input side's batch_digest moved to the unhashed FactorInputProvenance). FactorRegistry is a frozen collection that refuses an empty declaration and a repeated handle. V2-P3-014's ordering window was spent here: the report-period reach landed and `summary` left. A factor declares each axis exactly when `required_fields` puts it on that axis -- lookback_sessions/max_window_sessions for an ordinary panel dataset and lookback_periods/max_window_periods for one of PERIOD_INDEXED_DATASETS (the four statement endpoints), all four nullable and each pair refused unless the equivalence holds. A statement-only factor (V2-P3-010's ROE reads fina_indicator.roe and nothing else) therefore declares no session reach at all, and a price factor declares no period reach. Prose left all three identity contracts for FactorNote, a plain frozen dataclass the registries carry beside the specs and that no stable_model_id is ever applied to.
notes: Three judgements are recorded rather than assumed. (1) THE IDENTITY IS MEASURED FIELD BY FIELD, NOT ASSERTED TO EXIST. Roadmap section 9 is the counter-example this repository already paid for: config_digest and random_seed were stated in the PRD, in an audit document and in a task brief to feed decision_id, and a review's experiment showed they do not -- they are fields of RunManifest, and RunManifest is not one of the models stable_model_id is applied to. So the acceptance test varies each of the eight declared fields alone and asserts factor_id moves, and the manifest twin does the same for its fourteen and the input reference's five. A test that asserted an ID exists would have passed against exactly the shape section 9 describes. (2) schema_version IS HASHED AND THAT IS WANTED. Roadmap section 8 measured that schema_version is a real field rather than a computed one on four contracts, so a bump moves every ID; here that is the property rather than the hazard, because a factor-definition/v2 describes a different contract and its observations must not be indistinguishable from a v1's. The two computed handles (factor_id, qualified_key) are excluded from the payload, so neither adds a second canonicalisation that can disagree with the first. (3) A THIRD REGISTRY GUARD WAS WRITTEN AND DELETED. 'Two handles with one content address' reads like an obvious refusal and is a branch nothing can reach -- key and version are both hashed, so distinct handles imply distinct IDs, and two definitions with the same handle are refused by the duplicate-key check before the ID is consulted. Keeping it would have put an unreachable branch in the one object whose job is to make unreachable branches visible; test_two_distinct_names_can_never_share_a_content_address asserts the property the deleted guard would have. NOT REGISTERED IN domain/versioning.py OR domain/schema.py: that registry dispatches stored JSON rows back to a model and a factor definition is never stored as JSON, and CONTRACT_MODELS is the five contracts the HTTP face publishes -- a factor's public face is V2-P3-015. ColumnarPanelBatch made both choices for the same reasons. FOUR JUDGEMENTS WERE ADDED AFTER A REVIEW FALSIFIED THREE CLAIMS THIS ENTRY MADE. (A) AN IDENTITY HAS TWO HALVES AND ONLY ONE WAS MEASURED. 'Every declared field reaches the identity' is satisfiable by a model that declares the wrong fields, and this one did, in both directions. Collision: subject_count and universe_count were recorded and the sets were not, so two builds over disjoint two-name cross sections produced the same manifest_id and writing the second silently replaced the first's observations -- measured. subject_digest and universe_digest close it. Instability: FactorInputRef carried the provider's batch_digest, which hashes fetched_at, so re-fetching a partition with byte-identical rows moved every manifest_id built from it -- and because a stored build may not be dropped, the recomputed build could then never be written and the old one could no longer be re-derived. It moved to FactorInputProvenance, which is not a field of anything hashed. (B) THE IDENTITY TABLES ARE AUDITED AGAINST model_fields AT RUN TIME. The three parametrize lists are hand-written and would have kept passing while covering less than they claim; test_the_identity_audit_covers_every_declared_field_and_cannot_go_stale reads them back against the models. (C) NON-FINITE VALUES CANNOT WEAR THE computed CODE. The rule that undefined_value exists for lived only in one private engine function, so FactorObservation(value=nan, coverage='computed') constructed, wrote and read back -- measured. It is now in validate_factor_observation, a module-level function the constructor calls and the write path calls again, because a __post_init__ is a method and a frozen slots=True dataclass is still subclassable (panel/catalog.py's own argument, and a three-line subclass was measured storing an empty subject, a negative row count and a backwards window). (D) THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN. Adding a field to either model invalidates every stored factor_id and manifest_id and there is no migration path, so every field this contract will need has to land BEFORE V2-P3-014 writes the first immutable artifact -- including the report-period reach V2-P3-009..011 will want. Today no production factor partition exists and the cost is zero. WORDING CORRECTED: FactorField's check is syntactic; it refuses a name that could not be a panel dataset or an unquoted SQL identifier, not one that names no real column, and the earlier 'cannot be declared at all' claimed a check it does not make. MAX_FACTOR_KEY_LENGTH narrowed 48 -> 40 because panel_factors now builds a dataset name out of the key and MAX_IDENTIFIER_LENGTH caps it at 63; the arithmetic is asserted rather than commented. V2-P3-014-PREREQUISITE: THE REPORT-PERIOD REACH LANDED AND PROSE LEFT THE IDENTITY, IN ONE CHANGE. Both move factor_id and therefore manifest_id, transform_manifest_id and neutralization_manifest_id, and ContractVersions is deliberately not registered for these models, so there is no migration for a stored factor_id column. Doing them separately would have paid that twice; today the cost is zero because nothing in cli.py or scripts/ builds a factor partition. (1) THE SECOND AXIS IS TWO NULLABLE PAIRS, NOT FOUR FREE NUMBERS. A filing's panel row is dated at ann_date on all four clocks (providers/tushare.py#_announcement_timeline), so under a session index an annual and a Q1 disclosed on one day are two rows of one (subject, event_time) key and compute_factor refused the whole build -- measured as an A/B over one corpus written twice, in tests/integration/panel/test_factor_report_periods.py. lookback_periods counts a security's own report periods knowable at as_of (StatementHistory.periods_on's set) and max_window_periods bounds how many PANEL periods they may span; equality means 'no missed filing inside the window', which is what makes window[-5] the year-earlier period and what makes differencing two cumulative periods into a single quarter arithmetic rather than a guess. Year-on-year is therefore NOT a third dimension -- it is the same two numbers with larger values -- and single-quarter-versus-cumulative is the factor's choice while the contiguity it needs is the contract's. (2) EACH REACH IS DECLARED EXACTLY WHEN THE AXIS IS READ. A reach for an axis the factor is not on is a number inside factor_id that no branch of panel_factors can consult -- the 'field with no reader' this contract refused a report-period dimension for until it had one -- and a missing reach for an axis it IS on is an unbounded window. Both directions on both axes are refused with matched messages. (3) PROSE DECIDED NOTHING AND WAS INSIDE EVERY IDENTITY. Fixing a typo in FactorDefinition.summary moved the identity of every stored build and changed no number -- precisely the shape FactorTransformManifest's docstring rejects date_timezone for. V2-P3-003's review recorded it as an inherited convention and left it; V2-P3-004 then had to knowingly break its own 'edit only with a version bump' rule to retract three unreproducible figures, and recorded the exception with an expiry (V2-P3-014). This is the expiry. The fix is a CONTRACT SHAPE change and not a hashing change: an exclude=True field is exactly the shape roadmap section 9's config_digest had, so the prose moved to FactorNote and the three registries carry notes= beside their specs, audited by validate_notes (a note for an undeclared contract is prose about nothing; two notes for one contract make note_for arbitrary). A typo is now measured to move nothing (two registries differing only in notes have byte-identical factor_ids) and a setting change is measured to move the identity, which is the discriminating pair. (4) A SPAN BOUND BESIDE A COUNT OF ONE DECIDES NOTHING AND IS NOW REFUSED. max_window_sessions and max_window_periods are free above their own lookback, and at a lookback of 1 every setting above 1 is inert: a one-point window spans exactly one panel point, so panel_factors::_session_span and _period_span both return 1 and the bound can never bind. Measured by V2-P3-009's review, raising earnings_yield_ttm's max_window_sessions from 1 to 50 and book_to_price's max_window_periods from 1 to 8 turned only the declaration tests red and left the engine and integration suites entirely green -- two factors that compute the same number for every security on every partition, carrying two different factor_ids, which is the one thing a content address may not do. The refusal is a model validator rather than a new field, so it moves no factor_id: all twelve shipped ones were recorded before and after and are byte-identical. Requiring every declared contract to carry a note is deliberately NOT enforced on an arbitrary registry -- a probe registry has nothing to say and a forced sentence is the placeholder V2-P0B-009 deleted -- it is required of the three SHIPPED registries instead.

feature_name: The panel feature computation engine, and the visibility-filtered read that lets it answer at a mid-year as_of
feature_description: compute_factor evaluates one FactorDefinition for a declared cross section at one as_of and returns one FactorObservation per security: subject, as-of, value, coverage marker, input reference and build manifest -- V2-P3-002's six-part acceptance. The coverage marker is a closed five-code set and never a bool (computed, not_in_universe, insufficient_history, input_missing, undefined_value), because 'could not compute' is not one fact and V2-P3-005 has to exclude the four negatives from a correlation rather than treat them as zeros. Observations write the panel plane through panel_ingest.write_panel_batch as two datasets PER FACTOR -- factor_obs_<key>_v<n> (one row per security and as_of) and factor_manifest_<key>_v<n> (one row per build and input partition, keyed by manifest_id, which every observation carries). Per factor because PanelStore replaces a partition whole and one shared dataset made the unit of work a year of every factor: 22,955,032 observations at a measured 14.9 GB peak through batch, merge and to_rows. Reading the inputs goes through PanelStore.read_visible_at, which runs the identical readiness rule table and substitutes a row-level available_time <= as_of predicate only when every issue found is in ROW_FILTERABLE_ISSUE_CODES. No numpy and no pandas: the runtime dependency set is unchanged at nine. read_visible_at then re-decides the readiness checks whose pass does not survive row filtering (VISIBLE_SLICE_RECHECKS) against the rows it returns, pooled over every year requirement.years names -- the scope evaluate_readiness decides the same checks at -- and reports how far the projected partition reaches as visible_last_event_time.
notes: ROADMAP SECTION 11'S INTERFACE DECISION WAS TAKEN HERE, AND NONE OF THE THREE OPTIONS IT POSED WAS CHOSEN. The problem: evaluate_readiness compares one number per partition (max_available_time) against as_of, and a partition is a year, so a complete 2015 partition is refused at every as_of inside 2015. Measured on the fixture panel, read_if_ready at 2026-01-12 blocks the whole 2026 daily partition with exactly one issue code. What shipped is a fourth option: read_if_ready is unchanged -- same promise, same fourteen panel_ingest callers, still an all-or-nothing refusal -- and a SECOND method, PanelStore.read_visible_at, runs the same evaluate_readiness over the same PartitionStates and makes one substitution: if every issue found is in ROW_FILTERABLE_ISSUE_CODES (one member, not_yet_knowable), it scans with WHERE available_time <= as_of and counts what the predicate removed. Any other issue, alone or alongside, refuses the partition whole. Four properties make this a different trade from the one P2 declined. (1) THE SHORT ANSWER IS STATED, NOT INFERRED. P2's objection was that 'a filtered read hands back a short partition and every consumer above this plane reads shortness as missing data' -- build_index_membership refuses a gap in the month sequence, load_industry_histories' answerable_through exists because a read stopping short of an interval's closing row reassembles an interval that never ends, build_stock_universe refuses a delisting whose listing was filtered away. That objection is about a SILENTLY short answer, and all three of those readers still take the un-filtered path. PanelVisibleReadOutcome carries withheld_row_count, which a caller cannot receive rows without also receiving; on the fixture partition at 2026-01-12 that is 39 visible and 40 withheld, and visible + withheld == the partition's own row count is asserted rather than assumed. (2) IT IS A DIFFERENT TYPE, AND THE REVIEW MEASURED WHAT THAT IS WORTH: PanelVisibleReadOutcome.rows and PanelReadOutcome.rows carry the identical static type, so mypy --strict stops only the mistake of passing a whole OUTCOME where the other was expected -- stock_universe_from_panel_rows(list(filtered.rows), ...) type-checks clean, and the three rebuilders P2 named take rows. The obstacle that actually holds is the AST allowlist in (4); the claim that mypy was one of the three differences is withdrawn and pinned by test_the_two_read_outcomes_expose_rows_at_the_same_static_type. The type does refuse bool()/len()/iteration on BOTH paths (DependencyClearance's precedent: a guard that only rejects the failing case teaches nothing on the passing one). rows and withheld_row_count both raise on a blocked outcome -- 0 is the one number a caller must not be told, since a blocked read withheld everything. (3) EXACTLY ONE CODE IS COMPENSATED, AND THE OTHER TWELVE ARE ARGUED. Six say the partition is not what the catalog claims (filtering rows out of a partition you cannot trust filters nothing useful), three say required data is absent (withholding more does not supply it), stale says the newest event is too old (a predicate that removes recent rows can only make it worse), two say the requirement inspected nothing. not_yet_knowable is the only verdict that is true of some rows and not others. (4) IT IS AUDITED. tests/unit/panel/test_visible_read_callers.py pins the src/ files allowed to call it (one: panel_factors.py) in the shape test_query_callers.py established, and asserts the engine does NOT call query() -- so the point-in-time guarantee stayed in the storage plane, which is exactly what P2's technical acceptance warned would move to the factor layer with nothing auditing it. THE RESIDUE IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN ARGUED AWAY, as a third KNOWN_STORAGE_LIMITATIONS entry that therefore appears on every panel doctor report: filtering a partition written months after the sessions in it replays what the STORED rows say was knowable then, not what a fetch made at that instant would have returned. Section 7 measured the concrete case -- fina_indicator carries two rows for 81.7% of its keys with byte-identical four-clock timelines, so no available_time separates an original filing from its restatement. THE COVERAGE MARKER IS A CODE SET AND NOT A BOOL, following TradingState's three states and panel_gate's eight refusal codes, and P2's finding that is_blocked cannot distinguish an injected violation from an ordinary absence. Four of the five codes are provoked against a real partition at a real as_of; undefined_value is split in two on purpose -- the arithmetic is driven directly in tests/unit/test_factor_engine_rules.py because no writer in this repository will store a zero close (DAILY_PRICE_COLUMNS: no null and no non-positive close across 58,055 bars spanning 2001 to 2026), and the engine's non-finite handling is driven through an injected evaluator. A code with no branch behind it is what V2-P0A-001's AST validation and panel build's _audit_written_partitions were both added to close. THE BUILD MANIFEST'S IDENTITY IS DESIGNED AGAINST SECTION 9 RATHER THAN AROUND IT: every declared field enters manifest_id and each is measured to, code_commit is mandatory with no default (the placeholder V2-P0B-009 deleted was 'development'), and built_at is deliberately NOT a field -- it is recorded as the observation partition's ColumnarPanelBatch.fetched_at, hence PartitionCoverage.fetched_at, so a rebuild of an unchanged factor reproduces the manifest_id and rewrites nothing but its provenance. That is the arrangement section 9 says was wanted and not had. THE EVIDENCE-PLANE BAN IS STRUCTURAL WITH A NAMED LIMIT. FactorObservation is not an EvidenceSnapshot and has no adapter, and no panel_* module has an import edge to openalpha_cn.storage or openalpha_cn.evidence -- asserted on the live grimp graph. What it is NOT: EvidenceSnapshot.kind is a free str(min_length=1, max_length=64), so EvidenceSnapshot(kind='factor_observation') is constructible and ParquetEvidenceStore would accept it; evidence/builder.py's closed _NORMALIZERS table guards the normalisation path from a ProviderBatch, not the store's front door. So the obstacle is 'writing the conversion means adding an import a test refuses', which is structural with a review attached; 'impossible' would be the kind of overclaim domain/panel_batch.py already paid for once. TWO TABLES, BOUND AT RUN TIME: FACTOR_DEFINITIONS (data, hashable) and FACTOR_EVALUATORS (callables) must name exactly the same factors, checked at import and again at every compute_factor call, because panel build's PANEL_BUILD_TARGETS gained keys with no branch behind them and answered exit 0 with an empty partition list. THE ENGINE INVENTS NO REQUIREMENT: each input dataset's ReadinessRequirement is supplied by the caller and cross-checked (its dataset, its as_of, and that its required_fields actually include the columns the factor reads), which is panel_gate's argument -- a gate that built its own requirement could ask a dataset a different question from the one its own reader asks. A BLOCKED INPUT RAISES rather than becoming input_missing for the whole cross section, which would be V2-P1-013's 'empty success' with a coverage column on it. ONE VERIFICATION FACTOR SHIPS, reversal_1d, and it is not a V2-P3-012 deliverable: one required column so input_missing has one way to happen, a lookback of 2 (the smallest for which insufficient_history is reachable at all), and a denominator so undefined_value is a branch. Its declared direction is the family's conventional prior and this repository has measured nothing about it. NO NUMPY AND NO PANDAS, so the runtime dependency set stays at nine: the engine groups rows by (subject, session), takes the last lookback_sessions of each subject's own sessions and calls one scalar function per security -- no matrix, no broadcast, no regression. V2-P3-004's neutralisation is the first issue with a cross-sectional regression in it and is the right place to re-open the question with a real workload. Measured on the fixture panel, a whole cross section at one as_of is 24 ms end to end including the store read. RESIDUE, STATED: a partition is replaced whole and has no append, so every as_of OF ONE FACTOR belonging to a year must reach write_factor_panels in one call, at a measured 0.9 GB peak for a whole-market factor-year; different factors no longer have to, because each one has its own two datasets. _refuse_to_drop_a_stored_build reads each target MANIFEST partition's stored build list off the catalog (one row, no scan) and refuses a write that would drop any, and every guard runs before the first write so a refusal changes nothing -- an earlier version checked per partition and left the observations replaced while the manifests were not, which the round-trip test caught. FIVE FINDINGS FROM A REVIEW ARE CLOSED HERE. (1) A NO-OP REFETCH NO LONGER MOVES manifest_id, AND THERE IS NOW A RECOVERY PATH. FactorInputRef carried the provider's batch_digest, which hashes fetched_at; re-writing a partition's identical rows moved every manifest_id derived from it, and since a stored build may not be dropped the rebuild could never be written while its predecessor could no longer be re-derived. The digest moved to the unhashed FactorInputProvenance, load_factor_manifests lets a caller read what a partition holds, and write_factor_panels gained `supersedes` -- so 'a rebuild that supersedes an earlier build must name it' is now a thing a caller can actually do. (2) A BUILD WHOSE VISIBLE PANEL IS NARROWER THAN ITS OWN LOOKBACK IS REFUSED. Every security's sessions are a subset of the panel's, so insufficient_history for the entire cross section is arithmetic rather than a finding; measured before the guard, a 120-session factor at as_of 2027-01-20 with years=(2027,) read 36 rows, returned a census of three insufficient_history, raised nothing and was stored. The refusal names the years, because a window spanning a year end needs the earlier year in requirement.years. What is NOT refused is a wide-enough panel over individually young securities -- that is the answer the code exists to give. (3) THE LOOKBACK WINDOW HAS A DECLARED REACH. max_window_sessions bounds how many PANEL sessions the window may span, so a two-session return across a three-month halt is insufficient_history (with the window recorded, which is what distinguishes it from too few sessions) rather than computed. Measured: a 'one session close-to-close return' of +50% over 176 calendar days, marked computed and handed to FactorPanel.values(). (4) NON-FINITE VALUES ARE REFUSED AT THREE BOUNDARIES rather than one: the evaluator's return (unchanged), the type boundary (validate_factor_observation) and the read boundary (_stored_value, which is _coverage_code's symmetric case and was missing -- float(str(cell)) parses 'nan' and 'inf' without complaint). (5) THE BUILD CENSUS IS STORED. coverage_census() speaks only to a caller that asks and no face asks until V2-P3-014, so a build that answered nobody was indistinguishable in storage from one that scored the whole market; FACTOR_CENSUS_COLUMNS is one integer column per declared coverage code, derived from the vocabulary rather than listed. direction is stored on the manifest too, because a stored value column cannot be read at all without knowing which end of the cross section the factor calls good. THE OBSERVATION PARTITIONS ARE NOT SEPARATELY GUARDED, and that is a correction rather than an omission: their subjects are securities, which permits a write that drops a whole as_of and refuses a rebuild that legitimately narrows the cross section. The build reading has neither fault and is complete for observations, because manifest_id now covers subject_digest. THE IDENTITY AUDIT READS compute_factor's OWN SIGNATURE: every parameter is either shown to move manifest_id or carried in an exemption table with a written reason, so a tenth parameter fails until somebody classifies it.. REVIEW REMEDIATION (V2-P3-002 review): ONE DECLARED SAFETY PROPERTY WAS FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT AND IS NOW A REFUSAL CODE RATHER THAN A PARAGRAPH. Three docstrings said the substitution left the structural checks alone ('every other issue still refuses the partition whole, so nothing about the structural checks weakened'). evaluate_readiness judges partition METADATA and read_visible_at answers with a SUBSET OF ITS ROWS, so for three of the thirteen codes the check's PASS is a claim about rows the predicate then removes: stale, subject_missing and date_gap, now named by SCOPE_SENSITIVE_ISSUE_CODES with the criterion in its docstring. stale was not merely scope-wrong but arithmetically DEAD: it compares as_of against the whole partition's newest event, and not_yet_knowable fires exactly when that instant post-dates as_of, so the difference is negative. Measured on this repository's own fixture panel through daily_requirement, max_staleness of one hour, one day and two days all answered while the newest VISIBLE event was 2 days 21 hours behind as_of; end to end, a 14-row partition produced a factor stamped as_of 2026-06-30 over a visible slice ending 2026-01-09 -- 172 days under a declared bound of 7 days, every observation reading coverage=computed. THE FIX: read_visible_at re-decides VISIBLE_SLICE_RECHECKS (stale, subject_missing) against the rows it is about to return, through the same functions evaluate_readiness calls (staleness_issue, subject_gap_issue), so there is still exactly one place each verdict is computed; a slice that fails is REFUSED and the reason lands on PanelVisibleReadOutcome.visible_slice_issues. WITHHELD_ROW_COUNT DOES NOT IMPLY HOW FAR AN ANSWER REACHES and the two are uncorrelated where it matters -- the 172-day build withheld four rows out of fourteen -- so the outcome also carries visible_last_event_time, the evidence the re-decided stale check is computed from. compute_factor now refuses an input requirement that waives max_staleness, on the same footing as its existing refusal of a waived required_fields; factor_observation_requirement's waiver on the DERIVED read-back partition is unchanged and its argument still holds. date_gap is NOT re-decided: doing so means re-deriving session dates from instants in SQL, a second implementation of panel_ingest._date_census that openalpha_cn.panel cannot even import, and it would be a no-op on every path that exists today because _price_requirement is the only requirement stating required_dates and it clamps them at the same 16:30 instant the provider dates available_time at (fixture panel at 2026-01-12T04:00Z: five required, the same five returned). That residue is disclosed as a fourth KNOWN_STORAGE_LIMITATIONS entry, date_gap_clears_on_partition_rows_the_filtered_read_withholds. TWO SMALLER CORRECTIONS: a row with a NULL available_time fell out of both halves of the read (SQL three-valued logic drops it from <= and from >), so the asserted identity visible + withheld == row_count was false (measured 2 + 0 over 3 rows) and the row vanished with no code naming it -- the withheld predicate is now > ? OR IS NULL, which is fail-closed and restores the identity; and the AST detector's named residue was wrong (splatted arguments ARE caught; what escapes is a bound-method alias or getattr), now measured in both directions. The 288 s write figure is withdrawn as an absolute: four measurements of that one quantity now read 288 s, 56.7 s, 234 s (extrapolated from a fifth of the scale) and 617.9 s, a spread wider than an order of magnitude that column count and machine do not account for, so only the two-orders-of-magnitude ordering against compute_factor is claimed.. MERGE REMEDIATION (P3 A/B merge): THE RE-DECIDED BOUND WAS APPLIED AT THE WRONG SCOPE, AND ONLY A CROSS-YEAR REQUIREMENT COULD SHOW IT. max_staleness and required_subjects are fields of the ReadinessRequirement, which names a SET OF YEARS, and evaluate_readiness has always decided both over that whole set -- max(coverage.last_event_time) across the usable years and the union of their subject censuses. The visible-slice re-check above compared the same bound against ONE partition's rows, so read_visible_at refused reads read_if_ready permits on the identical requirement: measured on a two-year probe at as_of 2026-01-08 under a five-day bound, assess_readiness(years=(2025,2026)) is ready (the answer reaches 2026-01-07, 21 hours back) while read_visible_at(..., year=2025) blocked with stale quoting 7 days 21 hours -- the span of the look-back window rather than the age of the answer. EVERY TEST THAT EXISTED WHEN THE RE-CHECK LANDED NAMED A SINGLE YEAR, where pooled and per-partition coincide, so nothing saw it; it surfaced only when V2-P3-003's cross-year probe stopped waiving the bound the review had just made mandatory. The consequence lands on V2-P3-012: a 120-session momentum factor evaluated in January has to name the previous year, and at partition scope the only bound that permits that build is one wide enough to span the window -- roughly six months, which is wide enough to re-admit the 172-day build this whole remediation exists for. THE FIX IS A SCOPE FIX AND NOT A WEAKENING: read_visible_at pools the re-decided checks over requirement.years, by the same two reductions evaluate_readiness performs, taking one extra aggregate per further year on the connection already open and projecting only the year asked for. Both directions are pinned: test_the_freshness_bound_is_decided_over_every_year_the_requirement_names (a two-year read answers, and the same partitions under years=(2025,) are still refused with stale by both paths) and test_a_bound_still_refuses_a_multi_year_answer_that_is_old_in_every_partition (the 172-day shape at two-year scope, refused on every year), with the engine-level pair in test_a_declared_freshness_bound_survives_the_cross_year_window_it_has_to_allow. VISIBLE_SLICE_SCOPE was reworded from 'the rows this read returns' to 'the rows its requested years return', because the old phrase named one partition beside a reach taken from another. THE ENGINE GAINED A SECOND INDEX, AND THE MULTIPLICITY REFUSAL DID NOT WEAKEN. _read_dataset takes a dataset in PERIOD_INDEXED_DATASETS on its report_period column and every other on the session its event_time resolves to; FactorWindow carries both tuples so V2-P3-009's EP can divide a filing by a price without the two sharing an index. The selection rule on the period axis is StatementHistory.filing_for's -- keep the greatest visible announcement for a period -- stated a second time rather than called, because statement_histories_from_panel_rows requires the dataset's whole projected column set and a factor reading one column would then fetch all ten; the copy is held against the original by a TEST-TIME audit over one corpus (test_the_engines_period_selection_is_the_domains_filing_for) -- 'run-time' was the wrong word and is corrected below. WHAT STILL RAISES: two rows of one (subject, period) announced on the SAME day, which is the shape carrying 81.7% of fina_indicator's real duplication and which no column in these datasets orders. WHAT STOPPED RAISING: two DIFFERENT periods disclosed on one day, which was never a duplicate and which made an ordinary income input unreadable. NO SIXTH COVERAGE CODE: a period count shortfall and a period span overrun are both insufficient_history, distinguishable on the stored row because input_period_first/last carry the window the second was refused for and the first has none -- max_window_sessions' own precedent. The panel's period calendar was the union of the report_period values the visible read returned, by analogy with max_window_sessions' panel sessions; the contract review falsified that analogy and it is corrected below. A requirement for a period-indexed dataset must require report_period, because the engine projects it whether or not the factor names it and a partition without it would clear readiness and fail as a binder error. REVIEW REMEDIATION (factor contract review): THREE ENGINE DEFECTS, AND NO CONTRACT FIELD MOVED, SO NO SECOND IDENTITY MIGRATION -- the ordering constraint domain/factor.py states is already satisfied and every fix below is behind the fields rather than in them. (1) THE SAME-DAY MULTIPLICITY REFUSAL DEPENDED ON THE ORDER THE PARTITION RETURNED ITS ROWS. The duplicate check sat behind the restatement branch (announcement < previous continued, announcement == previous raised), so once a LATER announcement of a period had been read, both members of an earlier same-day pair were skipped silently. Measured on three rows in one partition, varying only the write order: [dup,dup,later] raised, [later,dup,dup] computed 555.0, [dup,later,dup] computed 555.0. read_visible_at scans with no ORDER BY over a partition DuckDB may read in parallel row groups, so neither the caller nor the provider decides which order a real build gets; the value the answering runs produced was RIGHT, so what was non-deterministic was not a number but whether the BUILD SUCCEEDED, which V2-P3-014's immutable artifacts cannot tolerate. The refusal is now decided on the (subject, point, announcement) triple, order-independent by construction and unchanged on the session axis, where point == announcement makes the triple exactly the old key. (2) max_window_periods == lookback_periods DID NOT MEAN 'NO MISSED FILING INSIDE THE WINDOW'. The span was measured against the panel's own period set, and a quarter no security in the cross section filed is not in that set. Measured: a security missing 2024-12-31 in a build where nobody filed 2024-12-31 was coverage=computed with value 0.5555555555555556, over a window whose [-5]-to-[-1] interval is FIFTEEN months (140/90-1 where a contiguous window gives 140/100-1); adding ONE other security that filed the quarter turned the identical build into insufficient_history. The guarantee was therefore a property of the build's composition rather than of the security, which is what V2-P3-011's whole window[-5] argument rests on. _period_span now counts on FISCAL_QUARTER_ENDS -- a PRC listed company's accounting year is the calendar year, so the quarters between two period ends are enumerable without reading a row -- and _report_period refuses a report_period that is not one of the four, because rounding one into the quarter it falls in is the second calendar the engine declines to build and would silently merge 2024-05-15 with 2024-06-30. The new measure is strictly stronger and never weaker: every panel period is a quarter end, so the panel's points between a window's ends are a subset of the grid's. The session axis keeps the panel-session measure, and the asymmetry is argued rather than tolerated: the sessions a cross section returns ARE the trading calendar, because every security is quoted on every open day. (3) THE ENGINE HAD NO ANSWERABLE_THROUGH. load_statement_histories bounds a partial-year read at the year before the first stored partition it skipped and refuses days past it (KNOWN_FINANCIAL_STATEMENT_LIMITATIONS.a_partial_year_read_answers_from_inside_its_window); compute_factor read exactly requirement.years and never consulted store.registered_years, so a build that skipped a stored announcement year reported the SUPERSEDED value as computed -- measured 110.0 where the domain over both years answers 999.0 and its answerable_through=2024 refuses the day outright. max_staleness does not stand in for it, reproduced at the 120-day bound this engine's own tests argue for with a January restatement. _refuse_a_read_that_cannot_see_what_as_of_holds is the counterpart, and it is deliberately NARROWER than the domain's rule in one direction: only a stored year at or after the earliest year the read covers can hide an announcement, because a stored year below that is history the factor chose not to reach for and costs only insufficient_history, which is honest and visible. FOUR SMALLER ITEMS. A row whose event_time resolves after as_of now raises on both axes: the visible read decides what a caller may see from available_time while this engine orders and indexes on event_time, and with the later announcement of a period made available a day before the earlier one, the engine took a restatement two months before it was announced. Nothing this repository writes can construct that -- _announcement_timeline gives every statement row the same instant on all four clocks -- which is precisely why an audit over a byte-equal corpus was structurally unable to see it. The round-trip fixtures could not tell a reach column from its own neighbour: both round trips used equal pairs (5/5 on the period axis, REVERSAL_1D's 2/2 on the session axis) and both column-swap mutants survived the entire tree, so a both-axes round trip carrying 2/3/4/5 was added. Two source docstrings cited tests that do not exist under the name given, one introduced by this contract change and one older, and tests/unit/test_source_cited_tests.py now resolves every tests/...::name citation in the package against the tree (OA-OPS-031). And SHIPPED_REGISTRIES, the hand-written table behind test_every_shipped_contract_carries_its_prose, is now held against an AST scan for module-level registry constants, so a FOURTH identity contract shipped without prose fails rather than simply never being asked.

feature_name: Versioned preprocessing transforms, stored beside the raw observations rather than over them
feature_description: Implementation Decision 8's three transforms as one content-addressed contract: winsorization (none / quantile / mad), standardization (none / zscore / centred rank) and a missing-value policy with one declared action per non-computed coverage code. FactorTransformSpec.transform_id is domain/_identity.py::stable_model_id, the same helper factor_id and manifest_id come from, so a transform is versioned by content rather than by convention; FactorTransformManifest.transform_manifest_id additionally hashes source_observation_digest, a content address of the raw (subject, coverage, value) triples the build consumed, so the identity moves when the numbers move and not only when the parameters do. THE VALUES ARE SEPARATE FROM THE RAW ONES AS A STORAGE LAYOUT, NOT AS A DISCIPLINE: a processed value is a ProcessedFactorObservation in factor_proc_<key>_v<n> with its own manifest dataset, and the raw factor_obs_<key>_v<n> partition is untouched and byte-identical across a processed write. Every processed row names the raw row it came from by (source_manifest_id, subject, as_of) -- the exact key of a row in the raw dataset, performed as a join in the integration test rather than described -- plus source_coverage, so the four reasons a security had no raw value survive into the processed plane. Two processed codes carry a value, processed and imputed, so a number the missing-value policy supplied is never indistinguishable from a measurement; validate_processed_factor_observation refuses a processed row over a non-computed source and an imputed row over a computed one.
notes: FOUR JUDGEMENTS ARE MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. (1) THE MISSING-VALUE POLICY DOES NOT TREAT THE FOUR NON-COMPUTED CODES ALIKE. not_in_universe cannot be filled at all -- refused at declaration time -- because a security the caller declared outside the cross section is not one with missing data, and imputing a cross-sectional median for it puts a name that had not listed yet, or had already delisted, into the scored cross section with a number derived from securities it was never comparable to. The other three are the caller's declared judgement, one field each, no defaults, and a sixth FactorCoverage member cannot arrive without a policy field: _refuse_a_policy_that_cannot_answer_every_missing_code runs at import against FACTOR_COVERAGE_CODES and refuses the module. (2) ONLY computed OBSERVATIONS PARTICIPATE IN THE CROSS-SECTIONAL STATISTICS, AND AN IMPUTATION NEVER RE-ENTERS THEM. If a fill fed back into the mean and deviation it was drawn from, every processed value would move with the COVERAGE RATE -- the same market on the same day would standardize differently because one security's filing was late. Measured: adding non-computed observations to a panel leaves every computed security's processed value byte-identical while moving transform_manifest_id, which it must. (3) THE SMALL-CROSS-SECTION EDGE HAS A DECLARED ANSWER AND A MEASURED CURVE. _quantile is linear interpolation between order statistics, so the q-quantile of n points sits at position (n-1)q and the interval always excludes at least one name: the fraction actually clipped is max(1/n, q), so a '1% winsorization' clips 33% of a three-name cross section, 10% of a ten-name one, and first clips what it declares at n = 1/q. FactorTransformSpec.min_cross_section is the declared floor below which a build produces insufficient_cross_section for everybody, and the shipped CROSS_SECTION_STANDARD sets it to 100 = 1/lower_quantile -- derived, not chosen, because a delivered proof hanging on a free parameter is a failure this repository has already paid for. (4) THE ZERO-DISPERSION EDGE IS DECIDED BY THE STANDARDIZER, NOT BY A min==max TEST IN THE ENGINE. zscore and rank both answer degenerate_cross_section on an all-tied cross section -- the same fact under two arithmetics -- while none passes the values through, because it makes no ordering claim. Deciding it in the method also closes a hole a min==max test leaves: [1e308, -1e308] is not constant and its variance overflows, which the zscore branch reports as degenerate rather than storing a non-finite scale.
