A separate run-time refusal covers the collapse of a SCALE ESTIMATOR on data that had dispersion (mad on [1,1,1,1,9] estimates MAD=0 and would clip every participant to the median); it fires only when the raw participants were not already tied, so an all-tied cross section stays an answer rather than becoming an error. POINT-IN-TIME: apply_factor_transform takes a FactorPanel and NO STORE -- no as_of, no universe, no requirement -- so the securities in a cross-sectional statistic are exactly the observations compute_factor produced at that as_of through read_visible_at. Audited by signature and measured by deriving every expected z-score at a mid-year as_of from the closes the availability filter left. ONE RESIDUE IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN CLAIMED CLOSED: KNOWN_STORAGE_LIMITATIONS.a_derived_partition_may_outlive_the_build_its_rows_point_at -- this plane has no cross-dataset referential integrity, and write_factor_panels' supersedes can drop a raw build that processed rows point at. Measured on the fixture panel: 8 of 8 processed rows left resolving to nothing, no refusal. THE BOUND FIRST WRITTEN HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED: it said supersedes is the only path, and it is not -- nothing requires the raw partition to have been written at all, so a processed write that simply precedes its raw one stores the same dangling pointer with no deliberate act anywhere. Measured and asserted by test_a_processed_partition_can_be_written_when_the_raw_one_never_was. What still bounds it is narrower: a raw partition that EXISTS cannot lose a build by accident, because a rebuild reproduces its manifest_id and _refuse_to_drop_a_stored_build refuses every other write that would remove one. NO NUMPY OR PANDAS: apply_factor_transform over 5,534 participants takes 36.7 ms, which is 1.6% of the compute_factor that must precede it and 0.06% of the write that follows; ADR-0003's 2026-08-12 update carries the table. Runtime dependencies remain nine. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY INDEPENDENT REVIEW ARE FIXED HERE. (A) THE WRITE BOUNDARY DID NOT CHECK THAT A ProcessedFactorPanel'S SPEC IS THE ONE THAT PRODUCED ITS ROWS. transform_manifest_batch takes its ten head columns off panel.manifest and its nine policy columns off panel.spec, so dataclasses.replace(result, spec=other) stored a manifest row whose transform_id was one transform's and whose standardization_method was another's, over a partition of the first transform's numbers -- falsifying this row's own claim that the stored policy is a projection of transform_id, and invisible to _transform_manifest_from_row's identity self-check, which reassembles only the head columns. The same root cause let two panels sharing one manifest and wearing two spec labels be written together: measured, two manifest rows under one transform_manifest_id and sixteen processed rows for an eight-name cross section. _refuse_a_processed_panel_that_does_not_own_its_rows now refuses both at the batch builders -- the output-side mirror of the input-side guard the engine already had -- and _refuse_two_applications_of_one_transform_at_one_as_of keys off the manifest rather than off the spec. (B) THE TWENTY-THREE STORED COLUMNS NO LOADER REASSEMBLES -- the census, the declared policy and the statistics -- HAD THEIR NAMES ASSERTED AND THEIR VALUES NEVER READ. Measured: every census column written as 0 and every missing-value column written as 'exclude' left the four covering test files at 233 passed. Four round-trip tests now read the manifest row off the partition and hold all twenty-three to values, with the census recounted against the processed rows in the other partition, so the two datasets have to agree; a per-column falsifier confirms each of the twenty-three now goes red. SUMMARY LEFT THIS CONTRACT. FactorTransformSpec.summary was inside transform_id and therefore inside every stored transform_manifest_id, so a typo fix moved builds whose numbers were unchanged -- the defect this issue's review disclosed and declined to fix alone, because taking it out of one of the three identity contracts would have left them disagreeing. All three dropped it together in the V2-P3-014 prerequisite change; the prose is CROSS_SECTION_STANDARD_NOTE, carried by FACTOR_TRANSFORMS.notes and resolvable through note_for. test_a_prose_only_edit_moves_the_identity_and_changes_no_number became test_prose_cannot_reach_this_identity_because_it_cannot_enter_this_contract, which is a structural claim rather than a convention: extra='forbid' means there is no summary= to pass.

feature_name: Cross-sectional neutralisation against industry and size, stored as a third tier beside the raw and processed ones
feature_description: Implementation Decision 8's fourth transform -- the one V2-P3-003 deliberately left -- as its own content-addressed contract rather than as a stage of the preprocessing one. A neutralisation regresses one as_of's PROCESSED factor cross section on a complete set of SW industry dummies plus one market-cap regressor and stores the RESIDUAL, so D8's raw / processed / neutralized is three record types in three pairs of datasets and none is written over another: a residual is a NeutralizedFactorObservation in factor_neut_<key>_v<n> with its own manifest dataset, and both partitions below it are byte-identical across a neutralised write. FactorNeutralizationSpec.neutralization_id is domain/_identity.py::stable_model_id, the same helper factor_id, transform_id and manifest_id come from; FactorNeutralizationManifest additionally hashes source_processed_digest (the processed (subject, coverage, value) triples consumed) AND characteristic_digest (the taxonomy, level, measure, every (subject, industry, cap, backfilled) tuple and both residue lists), so the identity moves when either input's numbers move and not only when the parameters do. THE PROVENANCE CHAIN IS TWO HOPS AND BOTH ARE PERFORMED AS JOINS: a neutralised row's (source_transform_manifest_id, subject, as_of) is the exact key of a processed row, and that row's (source_manifest_id, subject, as_of) is the exact key of a raw one. industry_code is stored on every residual because a residual is a deviation from a group and a reader who cannot see the group holds a number whose meaning is a join away.
notes: SIX QUESTIONS THIS ISSUE HAD TO ANSWER, EACH WITH A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. (1) HOW MARKET CAP ENTERS IS DECLARED IN TWO FIELDS AND ONE APPARENT CHOICE IS PROVABLY NOT ONE. market_cap_measure (total_mv / circ_mv) and market_cap_scale (level / log) each change every residual, and the SIZE of that change is asserted as a FLOOR rather than quoted as a figure. This is a correction: earlier text here and in five places in src/ carried 0.0196, 0.195 and 'residual rms 0.995' as if measured on the market. They came from one seed of the synthetic probe in tests/unit/test_factor_neutralization_rules.py -- whose circulating capitalisation is a Normal(0.7, 0.25) float ratio the test invents, so no stored circ_mv has ever been through it -- and the quantity is not stable enough to quote: over the eight seeds that test now sweeps the measure gap spans 0.0067..0.0591 and the scale gap 0.0210..1.2221, a 58x spread across an arbitrary parameter, against residuals whose deviation is 1 by construction. So what is asserted is that every seed clears MEASURE_GAP_FLOOR and SCALE_GAP_FLOOR, plus the spread itself (max > 10x min), which falsifies 'these are formalities' and claims nothing further. Re-SCALING the regressor changes no ANSWER -- z-scoring log(total_mv) and 1000*log+7 each move a residual by 4.44e-16 -- because a complete dummy set already spans the constant, so a field for it would reach the identity and decide nothing, which is the defect FactorTransformManifest rejected date_timezone for. That figure is NOT a uniform bound over affine maps: 1e-6*x-3 measures 8.4e-12 on the same probe, pinned by EXTREME_RESCALING_BOUND, because shrinking the demeaned regressor by six orders costs six orders of relative precision. (2) THE RANK OF THE DESIGN IS SETTLED BY DROPPING THE GLOBAL INTERCEPT AND KEEPING ALL 31 INDUSTRIES, and the choice changes the COEFFICIENTS' interpretation and NOT the residuals: a dense least-squares solve of 'intercept + 30 dummies + cap' and one of '31 dummies + cap' agree on every residual to 8.88e-16, because the two span the same column space. That reading needs no arbitrary reference industry. (3) WHICH INDUSTRY A SECURITY IS IN ON as_of IS A POINT-IN-TIME QUESTION AND THERE IS ONLY ONE VINTAGE TO CHOOSE FROM: index_member_all takes no src and every one of its 7,893 rows uses SW2021's 31 L1 codes (domain/industry_classification.py), so the vintage is a property of the corpus rather than a parameter; index_classify's two vintages are the TREE, which nothing here consults. The assignment is resolved by IndustryAnswer for the session asked about -- the fixture's session-adjacent hand-over is driven end to end, so a builder resolving by 'the last assignment that started' instead of 'the one covering the day' produces a different group for one name and different residuals for the other seven. IndustryAnswer.is_backfilled is carried per security, hashed into characteristic_digest and stored as the manifest's backfilled_industry_count. (4) A SECURITY WITH NO INDUSTRY GETS ITS OWN CODE IN A NEW VOCABULARY, NOT ONE OF ProcessedCoverage'S FIVE. NeutralizedCoverage is a fresh closed set of seven, so neither of V2-P3-003's import-time audits is touched -- adding to ProcessedCoverage would have added census columns to factor_procmn_* for codes no processed row can carry. industry_missing is separate from market_cap_missing because they point at different datasets and the first is permanent: 2,694 of 2,776 listed names classified on 2015-06-30, a 2.95% hole. An equivalent import-time audit IS installed in the new direction: _refuse_a_participation_table_that_cannot_answer_every_valued_processed_code refuses the module if a sixth PROCESSED code carrying a value has no participation rule admitting it, because such a code would be dropped from every regression silently. (5) THE ONE-MEMBER INDUSTRY IS MADE UNDECLARABLE RATHER THAN CODED AFTER THE FACT. Its residual is EXACTLY 0.0 for every factor and every slope -- it is its own group mean in both variables -- so min_industry_members has a lower bound of 2, which is the only bound in this contract that refuses a declarable configuration (min_cross_section deliberately admits 1). Excluding such a name costs the rest nothing: measured, the slope is BIT-IDENTICAL with and without it and every other residual moves by exactly 0. A group below a declared floor above 2 gets thin_industry, and the members are removed BEFORE min_cross_section is counted -- the opposite order would clear a floor on names it was about to code. (6) NUMERICAL STABILITY IS BOUGHT BY NOT FORMING THE MATRIX. The residual has a closed form (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell: group-demean y and x, one slope through the origin), which is O(n) in three fsum passes and agrees with a dense pivoted solve to 8.88e-16. The Gram matrix that solve forms has a diagonal spanning 151 to 3.55e17 on the level-cap design of the _panel(7) probe the comparison test drives, a ratio of 2.35e15 (the 1.37e15 quoted earlier is _panel(19)'s, and the seed is now named because the ratio is a property of the draw) -- but the dense solve still agreed to 4.44e-16, so the closed form is claimed for its cost and its absent matrix and NOT for a numerical failure it was observed to avoid. POINT-IN-TIME: apply_factor_neutralization takes a ProcessedFactorPanel, a spec, an IndustryMarketCapCrossSection and NO STORE -- no as_of, no universe, no requirement, audited by signature. The second cross section is a VALUE stamped with the instant it was read at, the engine refuses one whose as_of is not the panel's, and it refuses one that does not place every participant in exactly one of its three collections -- which is the guard with no other detector, since a name the cross section never heard of is otherwise indistinguishable from one it has no industry for. NO NEW VISIBILITY DOOR IS OPENED: the two foreign datasets are read through panel_ingest's load_industry_histories and load_daily_valuations, which take PanelStore.read_if_ready -- the UN-filtered door -- so they are read more strictly than the factor's own inputs were, and this module's FILTERED_READ_CALLERS entry is spent entirely on reading its own output partitions back. THE RESIDUE IS DISCLOSED AND DRIVEN RATHER THAN CLAIMED CLOSED: KNOWN_NEUTRALIZATION_LIMITATIONS.the_two_foreign_inputs_are_read_whole_partition_so_a_mid_year_as_of_is_refused -- read_if_ready decides not_yet_knowable on a partition's MAX available_time, so a daily_basic year partition is unreadable at every as_of inside its own year and a neutralised series is a year-end operation. Measured on the fixture at as_of 2026-01-12T04:00Z, where the year's last session becomes available 2026-01-16T08:30Z. THAT LIMITATION HAS A SECOND HOP AND IT IS THE ONE THAT REACHES A READER: neutralized_observation_batch stamps all four of a stored row's clocks with the BUILD's as_of, and that as_of cannot precede the daily_basic partition's max available_time -- so a residual about ANY day of year Y is only visible at an as_of after Y's last session, and because load_neutralized_factor_observations filters rows rather than refusing partitions, an in-year read returns EMPTY rather than an error. The residuals' CONTENT is point-in-time correct (each uses its own day's industry and capitalisation); the TIMESTAMP is not honest. V2-P3-005 is not blocked but must disclose that it reads a year-end snapshot; V2-P4-013's walk-forward IS blocked below annual granularity, and the prerequisite is filed as V2-P4-026 in roadmap section 11 rather than solved here, because both fixes (a finer daily_basic partition, or a day-bounded read in load_daily_valuations) change a V2-P1 storage contract. Four more are declared: no cross section before 2021-12-13 is neutralisable at all (the SW2021 availability floor blocks the whole read); an answer inside the era can still be backfilled and is counted rather than refused; a residual is orthogonal to the DECLARED regressor and not to size in general; a thin industry is coded rather than pooled up the taxonomy. MODULE SPLIT: this is a new top-level panel_neutralization.py rather than 1,000 more lines in panel_factors.py (3,912 and already the largest in src/), and the deciding argument is new rather than size -- it is the first thing on this plane that reads a FOREIGN dataset, and PANEL_MODULE_DEPENDENCIES records dependencies at package granularity, so keeping it in panel_factors would have widened the factor engine's reach to two datasets invisibly to the audit that exists to see widenings. NO NUMPY OR PANDAS: the closed form is 1.6 ms at 5,534 x 31 against a 143.5 ms dense solve, 0.8% of the compute_factor before it and 0.03% of the write after it; ADR-0003's 2026-08-12 V2-P3-004 update carries the table and the honest bound (a k-regressor risk model has no such closed form and would re-open the question). Runtime dependencies remain nine. TWO PERFORMANCE DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY PROFILING AND BOTH ARE SHAPES THIS REPOSITORY HAS RECORDED BEFORE: a pydantic computed_field read per security (5,534 stable_model_id calls, 31 ms) for the THIRD time in this tree, fixed by giving _neutralized_row a signature with no object to read one off; and a linear cross-section lookup inside the participant loop (322 ms of a 394 ms profiled build, 82%), fixed by indexing once. 148.5 ms became 17.4 ms with a byte-identical manifest identity. EVERY STORED COLUMN IS READ BACK AND HELD TO A VALUE -- eleven observation columns and all 34 manifest columns, with the census RECOUNTED against the observation partition so the two datasets have to agree with each other, which is the instrument V2-P3-003's review installed after measuring that 23 rendered-but-unasserted columns could all be written as constants with 233 tests staying green. TWO ASSERTIONS THAT COULD NOT SEPARATE TWO ANSWERS WERE FOUND BY REVIEW AND BOTH HAD ONE ROOT CAUSE: no test drove apply_factor_neutralization over more than ONE admitted industry group, because the integration fixture put seven names in one industry and coded the eighth thin_industry. On a single group, demeaning by group and demeaning the whole cross section are the same arithmetic -- so _neutralize(subjects, ['_ONE_'] * n, regressor, values), an engine that discards the classification entirely and stores a pure size residual, left all 146 tests green, and swapping min/max in smallest_industry_size / largest_industry_size did too (both were 7, and FactorNeutralizationStatistics' 'the two run backwards' guard therefore had no reachable driver). The fix is a second integration fixture, WIDE_SHAPES, whose session carries two admitted industries of 2 and 6 names with mean capitalisations of 2,375,000 and 5,375,000; test_the_residuals_are_the_two_group_regression_the_stored_inputs_imply holds every residual to a hand-computed per-group number and asserts the discarding engine's answer differs by more than the residuals' own dispersion, and test_the_two_industry_size_columns_are_two_answers_and_not_one_on_a_two_group_market reads 2 and 6 back off the stored manifest partition. NOT YET WIRED: nothing in cli.py or scripts/ imports panel_neutralization, so this ships as a library and has never produced a partition from real data -- V2-P3-014 owns the wiring. SUMMARY LEFT THIS CONTRACT AND THE EXCEPTION IT NEEDED IS SPENT. FactorNeutralizationSpec.summary carried a documented exception to its own 'edit only with a version bump' rule -- this issue's review edited INDUSTRY_AND_SIZE.summary without a bump to retract three unreproducible figures -- together with an expiry at V2-P3-014. The V2-P3-014 prerequisite change spent it by removing the field from all three identity contracts rather than by waiving the rule again. The prose is INDUSTRY_AND_SIZE_NOTE, word for word including the retraction, carried by FACTOR_NEUTRALIZATIONS.notes and outside neutralization_id.

feature_name: Information coefficient, rank IC, IC decay and stability, over all three factor tiers and signed by the factor's own declared direction
feature_description: V2-P3-005's information coefficient as a standard-library leaf module over the three stored factor tiers, with the four questions a correlation cannot answer for itself made into declared fields. WHERE THE FORWARD RETURN COMES FROM IS STRUCTURAL, NOT DOCUMENTARY. ic_cross_section takes OutcomeLabel and never a float, so V2-P1-017's chain (prediction_day -> next_trading_day -> shift(horizon.sessions) -> exit_day, eight closed refusal codes) is the only path a number can arrive by; domain/daily_prices.py measured the path this rules out at -0.530973% where the truth is +2.742230%, sign reversed, on 000001.SZ's 2026-06-12 ex-dividend session. A refused label is COUNTED (ICCensus.unlabelled_count) rather than read as a flat 0.0. WHICH OBSERVATIONS ENTER IS A TABLE RECONCILED AT IMPORT. raw admits {computed}, processed admits {processed} and NOT {imputed}, neutralized admits {neutralized}; TIER_VALUE_CODES and TIER_ADMITTED_CODES differ in exactly that one cell, and _refuse_a_tier_table_that_disagrees_with_its_own_contract refuses the module's IMPORT if either table stops matching domain/factor.py, domain/factor_transform.py or domain/factor_neutralization.py. THE DIRECTION DECIDES THE SIGN AND ARRIVES AS A DEFINITION. FactorICSpec carries a FactorDefinition, not a FactorDirection, so the wrong sign convention is unreachable rather than discouraged; ICPoint stores raw_ic beside the oriented ic and its validator refuses a point whose orientation contradicts its declared direction. This is FactorDefinition.direction's first consumer -- V2-P3-001's review recorded that it had none.
notes: SIX QUESTIONS THIS ISSUE HAD TO ANSWER EXPLICITLY. (1) WHAT AN IC IS. pearson is the product-moment correlation; spearman (the rank IC) is the same correlation on AVERAGE RANKS, ties sharing their average rank -- the identical rule panel_factors._standardize_rank applies, ALIGNED rather than divergent, and pinned element-wise over 300 tie-dense random vectors by test_the_rank_this_module_assigns_is_the_rank_the_transform_plane_assigns because they are two implementations (a backtest/ leaf may not import a module that reaches DuckDB). The all-tied degeneracy is aligned too but SPLIT IN TWO: degenerate_scores is a defect in the factor, degenerate_returns is a fact about the day, and one code would make them indistinguishable on a stored report. (2) THE DECAY AXIS IS horizon_sessions AND ITS BOUNDARY IS domain/horizon.py's. ResearchHorizon.sessions is defined for d horizons and refuses a calendar one, so a 3m rung is not constructible; the return at each rung is CUMULATIVE from one entry rather than the marginal return of session h, because WindowReturn is entry-to-exit and a marginal reading would need a label contract that does not exist (KNOWN_IC_LIMITATIONS records this). Every rung is held to the SAME offered as_ofs, or a curve falling from 0.05 to 0.01 could be decay or could be a sample that shrank underneath it; per-rung measured_count reports the attrition instead. (3) STABILITY IS FOUR DEFINED NUMBERS. mean_ic = fmean of the oriented measured ICs; stdev_ic = SAMPLE (n-1) standard deviation; icir = mean/stdev and None when the dispersion is zero; sign_consistency = positive_count / measured_count on the ORIENTED IC, with a zero IC in the denominator and in neither numerator bucket. The icir None is a DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from backtest/event_study.py's math.inf: inf discards the sign of a constant negative series and is a non-finite number the three observation contracts all refuse one plane over. No t-statistic and no confidence interval are published, because at horizon h two prediction days one session apart share h of h+1 sessions (five of six at 5d) so the series is autocorrelated by construction and an independence claim would be false. (4) AND (5) BOTH FLOORS ARE DECLARED FIELDS WITH NO DEFAULT, EACH BOUNDED BELOW BY ARITHMETIC. min_securities >= MINIMUM_IC_SECURITIES = 3 because two points lie on one line, so |r| = 1 for ANY pair -- measured over 200 random pairs, and the assertion is round(abs(r), 15) == 1.0 and not an identity, because eight of ten come out 0.9999999999999998. min_as_ofs >= MINIMUM_IC_AS_OFS = 2 because a sample standard deviation of one number does not exist. Three is a FLOOR and not a recommendation: min_securities=3 is declarable and KNOWN_IC_LIMITATIONS records that it is almost all noise, which is the shape the eight narrow-sample Criticals took. (6) THE SIGN IS ORIENTED ONCE, AT THE ONLY PLACE HOLDING THE DECLARATION, rather than at each consumer: V2-P3-008 groups by family and V2-P3-014 reports three tiers per family, and averaging a higher_is_better factor's +0.03 with a lower_is_better factor's -0.03 gives zero for two factors that both worked. raw_ic is kept beside ic so the choice is auditable. THE PRODUCT CONSTRAINT THIS ISSUE IS REQUIRED TO DISCLOSE: a neutralised IC reads a YEAR-END SNAPSHOT. neutralized_observation_batch stamps all four clocks with the build's as_of, which is at or after the year's daily_basic max_available_time, and reads go through read_visible_at -- so a mid-year as_of returns nothing rather than raising. V2-P3-004's review judged this non-blocking here because the residuals' CONTENT is clean (industry, market cap and processed value all of the row's own day), so neither the IC nor the decay curve is forward-contaminated; what is lost is the honesty of the timestamps. V2-P4-026 is the fix and is a hard precondition of V2-P4-013. NUMERICAL STACK: still the nine runtime dependencies. spearman at ADR-0002's 5,534-name cross section is 3.56 ms, 630x smaller than the 2.24 s compute_factor read that feeds it; a whole year of daily as_ofs is 0.90 s. ADR-0003's 2026-08-12 update carries the table and the n log n scaling measurement, and closes the second of the two workloads its Context named.

feature_name: Momentum and reversal factors, and industry-relative momentum as a composition
feature_description: V2-P3-012's momentum and reversal family: four versioned FactorDefinitions -- a 20-, 60- and 120-session momentum and a 5-session reversal -- each computed as the product of the published session return close / pre_close over the sessions it declares, plus industry-relative momentum delivered as a composition of V2-P3-003's transform and V2-P3-004's neutralisation rather than as a fifth definition.
notes: THE RETURN PATH IS THE ONE THING THIS FAMILY COULD NOT GET WRONG AND IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. domain/daily_prices.py measured three ways to compute one session's return across 000001.SZ's 2026-06-12 ex-dividend date: close/pre_close-1 (Tushare's own pct_chg) reads +2.742230%, the adj_factor path +2.742251%, and the naive close[t]/close[t-1]-1 reads -0.530973% -- the SIGN is wrong. A momentum is that quantity compounded, so the third path compounds the error, and the engine's own verification factor reversal_1d is built on exactly that third path (its note already says V2-P3-012 will not be built on top of it). Every factor here therefore declares BOTH daily.close and daily.pre_close and multiplies close/pre_close over its window: pre_close is the previous close already restated for that morning's corporate action, so the product is corporate-action-correct by construction and telescopes across a halt as well, since the pre_close of a resumption session is the pre-halt close restated. adj_factor is not read -- equally correct, but it would make every momentum a two-dataset factor and turn a missing factor row into input_missing on a security whose prices are all there (49 such names on 2024-06-28). pct_chg is not read either, though it is in the same rows: it is the third WITNESS session_returns reconciles the price path against, and it is published on two grids whose coarse tick is 1e-4 of return, which compounded over 120 sessions is a quantity nobody has bounded. WINDOW ENDPOINTS ARE A DECLARATION PLUS A SLICE, NOT A CONTRACT FIELD. Each momentum declares five sessions MORE than it compounds (25/65/125 for 20/60/120) and its evaluator drops the newest five. There is no gap field on FactorDefinition and one was not added: it would move factor_id for every factor in the repository and be read by three of them. The skip is SHORT_REVERSAL_SESSIONS, the same constant reversal_5_sessions declares as its reach, so the sessions a momentum multiplies and the sessions the reversal multiplies are DISJOINT. That is the half of the reason this repository can prove: with no skip a 20-session momentum's window contains the reversal's and the two are bound by the exact identity 1+m20 == (1+m15)*(1+r5), which V2-P3-008's redundancy analysis would report as a finding about arithmetic. The conventional reason -- a momentum stated over a period ending before the short-reversal window is not measuring it -- is named as the family's prior and nothing here has measured it. NOTE WHAT THE STORED WINDOW COLUMNS CANNOT SHOW: input_session_first/last record the DECLARED 25-session window, whose newest session is the reversal's newest session too, so the disjointness is measured against two stores differing only in the newest five sessions' returns. MAX_WINDOW_SESSIONS IS ONE JUDGEMENT APPLIED FOUR TIMES AND THE NUMBERS ARE NOT FIXTURE-FITTED. The reversal is at EQUALITY (5/5), reversal_1d's setting, because the whole content of a short-horizon reversal is that the interval is recent and unbroken; a name halted for one session in the last five gets insufficient_history. The three momenta tolerate one halted session in five of their own reach (MAX_HALTED_SESSIONS_IN_FIVE), giving 30/78/150. Equality is wrong for them and the measurement is this repository's own: MIN_SESSION_ROW_SHARE records 2015-07-09 serving 1,363 bars against a year median of 2,359 -- 42% of the market with no row -- and under equality every one of those names would carry insufficient_history for the next 125 sessions. One in five rather than one in two because at one in two a 120-session momentum may span 250 panel sessions, which is a YEAR on the 242/243/244-session years daily_prices.py measured. What makes the number auditable rather than free is a ladder that is asserted: 30 < 65 and 78 < 125, so no momentum's worst-case span reaches the nominal reach of the next factor up, and 150 < 242. Widening the tolerance fails test_no_momentum_windows_worst_case_span_reaches_the_next_rungs_own_reach before it changes a single value. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: there is no measured distribution of A-share halt DURATIONS in this repository, so the tolerance is a declared judgement with a stated cost and not a calibration. HALTS AND LIMIT MOVES SPEND NO COVERAGE CODE. A whole-day halt is simply a session the security does not own, so the product spans it correctly and the only price is span, which max_window_sessions charges. A timed halt leaves a bar (2015-07-08 measured 31 of 31 with one), and a limit-up or limit-down session is an ordinary bar whose close/pre_close is the real limited return. No factor here reads suspend_d or stk_limit, and the two absences have different reasons. suspend_d's own columns are text (suspend_type, suspend_timing) and _numeric refuses a non-numeric cell, so a halt state is not declarable as a factor input at all. stk_limit's two columns ARE floats and could be declared, and are not: masking a limit session would be a judgement about the market that nothing here has measured, it would make every value depend on a second dataset's coverage, and that dataset carries the Beijing-board encoding where down_limit is a fixed 0.0 (domain/price_limits.py: every row with down_limit <= 0 across 235 sessions is a .BJ code with a sentinel up_limit) -- a sentinel a factor window that silently dropped sessions on it would not understand. DIRECTION IS A PRIOR AND SAYS SO. Momentum is higher_is_better and the reversal lower_is_better; both notes carry reversal_1d's own disclaimer in substance -- this repository has measured nothing about either, and V2-P3-005 is where an information coefficient would say anything. INDUSTRY-RELATIVE MOMENTUM IS A COMPOSITION, NOT A FIFTH FACTOR. compute_factor hands an evaluator ONE security's window, so a statistic over industry peers is unreachable by type -- not merely because the engine cannot reach the industry table. And an industry code could not be an input even if that helped: FactorField's validation is syntactic, so FactorField(dataset='index_member_all', column='l1_code') constructs, and _numeric then refuses the string at the read -- driven in test_an_industry_code_is_declarable_as_a_factor_input_and_refused_at_the_read. What produces the quantity is the chain compute_factor -> apply_factor_transform(CROSS_SECTION_STANDARD) -> apply_factor_neutralization(INDUSTRY_AND_SIZE), whose residual is by Frisch-Waugh-Lovell (y - mean_y_g) - beta*(x - mean_x_g); the first term IS industry-relative momentum. THE DIFFERENCE FROM A PURE INDUSTRY DEMEANING IS STATED RATHER THAN ELIDED: the shipped neutralisation removes industry AND size, no declarable FactorNeutralizationSpec removes industry alone (market_cap_scale has two members and neither is 'none'), and the gap is beta*(x - mean_x_g), asserted as a floor against the residuals' own dispersion rather than as a figure -- which is the form V2-P3-004's review had to retreat to after three point estimates could not be reproduced. NOT WIRED INTO A SCHEDULE OR A READ PATH, DELIBERATELY: roadmap section 11 records that a neutralised row's four clocks are all the build as_of and that residuals for any day of year Y are invisible to every read before Y ends (V2-P4-026, V2-P4-013's hard prerequisite), with an instruction to V2-P3-009..013 to stack no further code on day-by-day visibility. The composition is three in-memory calls and reads back no stored residual. THE FIXTURE DEFECT THIS REPOSITORY KEEPS MEETING WAS MET TWICE MORE HERE, AND BOTH TIMES BY AN INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN BY A READER. (1) The first corpus used a pure oscillation whose period divides its own sum to zero, so the 20- and 60-session products sat 0.0005 apart and test_no_two_factors_answer_with_the_same_number_for_any_security failed two orders below its floor; a per-security drift term fixed it and the worst gap between any two of one security's four answers is now 0.0173 against a floor of 0.01. (2) A mutation widening momentum_120_sessions' span bound from 150 to 151 SURVIVED every assertion in the integration file, because at 144 sessions the corpus could not hold a security whose 125-session window spans 151 -- the widest factor's bound was asserted and not separable, which is exactly the shape V2-P3-004's review named. The corpus is 165 sessions now and carries two securities differing in one halted session, spanning exactly 150 and 151, so the bound has a driver on each side. The composition fixture likewise carries TWO industry groups of DIFFERENT sizes (4 and 9 of the 13 participants), because on one group demeaning by group and demeaning the cross section are the same arithmetic and smallest_industry_size equals largest_industry_size. NO NUMPY OR PANDAS, RE-DECIDED ON THIS FAMILY'S OWN WORKLOAD RATHER THAN INHERITED. A momentum is one running product per security, O(n) in the window, with no matrix anywhere -- but it is the first factor whose per-security work is proportional to the reach rather than constant, so the question was re-measured at ADR-0002's stated panel scale: a synthetic daily partition of 5,534 securities x 130 sessions (719,420 rows, both price columns) written through the real store. compute_factor over the whole cross section takes 2.93 s cold / 2.84 s warm for momentum_120_sessions and 2.50 s / 2.48 s for reversal_5_sessions -- so the 115 extra multiplications per security that separate a 120-session window from a 5-session one cost 0.43 s in total, about 0.7 microseconds each. Writing that same partition took 507.74 s, 173x the whole 120-session build. A numpy implementation could at best remove part of a 0.43 s term that sits three orders of magnitude below the write that follows it, in exchange for two runtime dependencies and every consequence ADR-0003 lists. Runtime dependencies remain nine.

feature_name: Factor family five, volatility and liquidity, and the residual it could not build
feature_description: V2-P3-013's four definitions and their evaluators: return_vol_60 (the sample standard deviation of 60 daily close/pre_close returns), downside_vol_60 (the same window's downside semi-deviation, divided by the window rather than by its own negative count), turnover_60 (mean daily_basic.turnover_rate, in percent) and amihud_60 (Amihud 2002's illiquidity ratio, in 1/CNY, with daily.amount carried from thousands of yuan into yuan). All four declare family volatility_liquidity, a 60-session reach, an 80-session span bound and no report-period reach; the two liquidity directions are opposite in sign and identical in economics. Every direction is the family's conventional prior and this repository has measured nothing about any of them -- REVERSAL_1D's standard, applied to four more. The roadmap's residual and idiosyncratic volatility are NOT shipped under those names and the notes say why.
notes: SIX JUDGEMENTS, EACH MEASURED RATHER THAN PREFERRED. (1) NEITHER FACTOR IN THE VOLATILITY HALF IS NAMED FOR A RESIDUAL, BECAUSE NEITHER IS ONE. The roadmap line asks for residual volatility and idiosyncratic volatility, which are one construct in the literature -- the dispersion of the part of a return a market or factor model does not explain. Computing either needs a market return series aligned to the security's own sessions, and the panel holds no index or market price series at all: the fifteen datasets providers/tushare.py declares are prices, valuations, adjustment factors, four statement endpoints, calendar, universe, industry tree and membership, index WEIGHTS, suspensions, price limits and name history. The gap is not one fetch away either -- FactorWindow carries one security's own rows and _classify is called once per subject, so an evaluator could not read a stored 000300.SH series if one existed. This is a DATA and ENGINE-SHAPE blocker and explicitly not the numerical-stack one ADR-0003 warns about: a single-factor time-series regression is univariate, b = cov(r, r_m) / var(r_m), O(n) in pure Python and needing neither numpy nor a new machine. What is missing is the regressor. return_vol_60 is the total volatility such a residual reduces to when b*r_m cannot be subtracted and downside_vol_60 adds asymmetry, and both say so in their own FactorNote. (2) THE RETURN PATH IS close / pre_close - 1 AND THE WRONG ONE IS DRIVEN TO SHOW IT IS WRONG. domain/daily_prices.py measures three paths and one is wrong by up to 118.30 over 37,602 rows and reverses the sign across an ex-rights morning. Three of these four factors are built on returns, so that defect would have reached all three at once. The fixture carries one ex-rights session inside every window precisely so that a close-to-close implementation is separable on it; without one, both paths agree on every session and the assertion measures nothing. A second consequence decided the path as much as correctness did: each return is computed inside its own row, so a window of N sessions yields exactly N returns and the sample size behind a value is the count the definition declares -- a close-to-close path would yield N-1. (3) turnover_rate AND NOT turnover_rate_f, WHICH IS FAIL-CLOSED WITH A MEASURED COST. daily_prices.py records turnover_rate populated on every one of 51,708 rows across eighteen sessions spanning 2001 to 2026, while turnover_rate_f is in DAILY_BASIC_NULLABLE_COLUMNS (17 nulls over four sessions 2001-2008) and its sibling free_share carries 74 CONSECUTIVE null trading days on 300290.SZ. Because the engine hands an evaluator only complete windows, one null session is input_missing for all 60 as_ofs whose window contains it. Reading the free-float column would also falsify that module's own stated reason for the split. The cost is stated rather than hidden: float-share turnover understates trading intensity where the float carries a strategic holding, and the two columns are not interchangeable -- 1.0473 against 2.4905 for 000001.SZ and 0.4039 against 0.9334 for 600519.SH. (4) daily.amount IS IN THOUSANDS OF YUAN, MEASURED AGAINST AN INDEPENDENT WITNESS. Across eleven real stored rows spanning 2001-01-02 to 2026-06-15, amount * 1000 / (vol * 100) is the only reading of that column pair whose implied VWAP falls inside the session's own low-high range, on all eleven, and each of the other three readings falls outside it on all eleven. The unit is load-bearing and invisible downstream: a rank IC and a z-score are both scale-free, so a denominator wrong by 1,000 would reach every report and no test that only ranks. A zero or negative amount makes the whole observation undefined_value rather than being skipped, because a mean over whichever sessions happened to trade is a value whose sample size is a function of the data. (5) THE WINDOW IS 60 SESSIONS FOR ALL FOUR AND WAS NOT CALIBRATED ON A FIXTURE. Three facts decide it and none needs data of ours: it is one A-share quarter (2024 held 242 sessions); the relative standard error of a sample standard deviation is 1/sqrt(2(N-1)) under normality, which is 16.4% at 20, 9.2% at 60 and 6.5% at 120; and one horizon across the family makes V2-P3-008's redundancy analysis a comparison of content rather than of horizon. max_window_sessions is 80 -- 20 sessions of slack, one A-share trading month. Not zero, because 26 listed-and-halted names on the ordinary session 2024-06-28 is half a percent of the market and a zero-slack quarterly factor would refuse every name that took one announcement halt; not more, because 80 panel sessions already reach across four calendar months. BOTH BOUNDS ARE SEPARABLE ON THEIR OWN BOUNDARIES rather than merely rendered, which is the V2-P3-004 review's lesson: three securities holding sixty of their own sessions each and spanning 79, 80 and 81 panel sessions answer computed, computed, insufficient_history, and two holding 60 and 59 contiguous sessions answer computed and insufficient_history with identical spans. (6) undefined_value IS NOW REACHABLE THROUGH THE WHOLE ENGINE ON DISK. test_factor_engine.py records that it is not, for reversal_1d, because DAILY_PRICE_COLUMNS' five guarded columns admit no zero -- so its two halves are split across two files. amihud_60's denominator is daily.amount, which is not one of those five, so a zero in it is storable and the code is provoked end to end here for the first time; the same security is computed for the three factors that do not read amount, so the code separates the two faults rather than merging them. Ten mutations of the implementation were each confirmed to turn these tests red, including the naive close-to-close path, a population deviation, a downside deviation divided by its own negative count, an Amihud without the currency unit, an Amihud that skipped its zero denominators, a reader pointed at turnover_rate_f, either bound moved by one, and a flipped direction.

feature_name: Factor family one, value: EP / BP / SP on two axes, and the deducted-profit yield it cannot build
feature_description: V2-P3-009's three definitions and their evaluators: earnings_yield_ttm (EP -- the trailing twelve months of income.n_income_attr_p over market capitalisation), book_to_price (BP -- balancesheet.total_hldr_eqy_exc_min_int at the latest knowable report period over the same denominator) and sales_yield_ttm (SP -- the trailing twelve months of income.total_revenue). All three declare family value, direction higher_is_better, a one-session reach on daily_basic.total_mv and a report-period reach on a statement dataset -- 5/5 for the two flow factors and 1/1 for the stock one. They are the FIRST factors this build ships on both axes at once and the first that read a filing at all: the report-period reach fields shipped with no production reader and these are it. EPcut is NOT shipped -- no stored statement projection carries a deducted-profit column -- and earnings_yield_ttm occupies that slot on return_vol_60's terms, disclosing what it is not.
notes: SEVEN JUDGEMENTS, EACH MEASURED OR DECLARED WITH ITS COST. (1) A VALUE FACTOR IS ON BOTH AXES AND THE ENGINE ALREADY SUPPORTED THAT. FactorDefinition declares each reach exactly when required_fields puts the factor on that axis, FactorWindow carries a sessions tuple and a periods tuple with series() aligned to whichever its dataset is on, FactorObservation carries a window pair per axis, and _classify forms and bounds both independently. All of it shipped with the report-period axis and was exercised only by test-local definitions; these three are the first shipped users. So the time-point mismatch -- a daily denominator and a quarterly numerator -- is not resolved by aligning one to the other: each side is read on its own index and the evaluator divides [-1] by [-1]. (2) daily_basic.total_mv IS IN UNITS OF 10,000 YUAN, MEASURED ON STORED ROWS. The chain needs no upstream field list: vol * 100 / (float_share * 10,000) reproduces the stored turnover_rate, so the share counts are ten-thousands; and total_mv * u / (total_share * 10,000) reproduces the session's own close for exactly one of the four multipliers Chinese financial reporting uses (1, 100, 10,000, 100,000,000), on all four real rows spanning 2005 to 2026. The unit is load-bearing and invisible downstream -- a rank IC and a z-score are scale-free, so a denominator wrong by 10,000 reaches every report and no test that only ranks. total_mv and not circ_mv, because a filing describes the whole company. (3) NOT THE PUBLISHED RATIOS INVERTED, WHICH IS THE CHOICE WITH THE SHARPER ARGUMENT. daily_basic carries pe, pe_ttm, pb, ps and ps_ttm, all five in DAILY_BASIC_NULLABLE_COLUMNS, and their null rate is the point: 1,102 null pe and 1,214 null pe_ttm of 5,338 rows on 2024-06-28, because a published multiple has no value for a loss-maker. An inverted multiple would answer input_missing for about a fifth of the market -- precisely the fifth a SIGNED yield scores correctly -- and it would score the upstream's own trailing-window arithmetic rather than the filings, which is the reason _compounded_session_return refuses pct_chg. (4) THE FLOW NUMERATORS ARE TRAILING TWELVE MONTHS AND NOT THE LATEST CUMULATIVE. A-share statements accumulate inside the calendar fiscal year, so the latest cumulative figure is 3, 6, 9 or 12 months of profit and a cross section read at one as_of mixes those as soon as two issuers file on different schedules. TTM(P) = cumulative[P] + cumulative[the December before P] - cumulative[P - 4 quarters], and a five-period window ending at P holds all three by construction, because window[:-1] is four consecutive quarters and therefore exactly one December. What makes that index arithmetic legitimate is max_window_periods == lookback_periods, which _period_span makes true against the fiscal-quarter grid rather than against the periods the build happened to read. The cost is a coverage difference INSIDE the family -- five contiguous filings for EP and SP, one for BP -- and both bounds are separable on one partition: 600000.SH is short on the count at an unbroken span and 000063.SZ is whole on the count at a six-quarter span, and both answer insufficient_history. (5) A NEGATIVE NUMERATOR IS computed AND NEGATIVE. A loss-making issuer has a negative earnings yield and an insolvent one a negative book-to-price; the arithmetic has an answer, and undefined_value is documented for the case where it does not. This is the whole reason the family is stated as yields rather than as multiples: E/P is monotone through zero and P/E is not. undefined_value is reserved for a non-positive capitalisation, which is REACHABLE on a partition this repository's own reader accepts -- domain/daily_prices.py requires total_mv to be finite and not to be positive, since only DAILY_PRICE_COLUMNS' five get the positivity check -- so a stored 0.0 provokes it end to end, on AMIHUD_60's precedent. (6) THE COLUMNS ARE CHOSEN AGAINST THE MEASURED CONCENTRATION OF THE REFUSALS. domain/financial_statements.py records that the refusals pool rather than spread: ebit is 258 of income's 288, total_share 34 of balancesheet's 43, free_cashflow ALL 450 of cashflow's and fcff 441 of fina_indicator's 507. This family reads none of them, nor bps, whose two versions of one 603049.SH filing differ by a factor of ten. The three columns' OWN refusal rates are measured rather than derived, over two disjoint 91-security samples: total_revenue 13 of 10,567 filings (0.123%), n_income_attr_p 20 of 10,567 (0.189%) and total_hldr_eqy_exc_min_int 21 of 10,369 (0.203%). That replaces a derived budget whose middle term was itself a sample property: 'at most 30 non-ebit income reads over 3,201 filings and at most 9 non-total_share balancesheet reads over 3,170' implied 0.94% and 0.28%, while the same two samples put those residues at 55 / 5,210 and 92 / 5,357 (1.72%) and at 60 / 5,120 (1.17%) and 32 / 5,249 (0.61%), two to four times the recorded figures. The three target columns come in under the old bounds and the quantity the bounds were derived from does not, which is domain/financial_statements.py's own 'how little is a property of the sample and not of the dataset'. It buys no immunity either way: 002538.SZ's 2022 annual carries three versions of total_hldr_eqy_exc_min_int spanning 3.8%. BP is NOT fina_indicator.bps times a share count and NOT total_assets minus total_liab, and both refusals are argued with real numbers. SP READS total_revenue AND NOT revenue, AND THAT REASON WAS CORRECTED AFTER REVIEW. The delivered argument was that the two columns are equal on an ordinary industrial and part only for the company types whose top line is not one number, so no fixture could decide it. Measured by comp_type, every half of that is false: over the whole history of 14 banks, insurers and brokers the two carry the same number on all 1,350 rows (comp_type 2 / 3 / 4, zero differences), the only place this endpoint separates them is comp_type=1 at 37 of 1,468 rows in a 47-name sample, and 600519.SH separates them on ALL 42 of its stored periods -- 123,122,542,625 of total_revenue against 120,776,131,875 of revenue at 2024Q3, 1.94% of revenue. The 000001.SZ 2018H1 row that was quoted as the 'ordinary industrial' carrying both is comp_type='2', a bank. total_revenue remains the right column, as the topmost and inclusive line, and the argument for it is now a real row rather than a reading of the statement: test_the_top_line_and_revenue_are_two_different_numbers_on_a_real_industrial_row. (7) THE ENGINE NOW COLLAPSES DUPLICATE FILING ROWS THAT AGREE, WHICH IS THE DOMAIN'S OWN RULE. _read_dataset refused on multiplicity alone, so it refused 372 of income's 633 duplicate keys, 1,166 of balancesheet's 1,244 and 2,194 of fina_indicator's 2,671 that say exactly the same thing twice, where ReportFiling.value_of answers every one of them. The engine is a second statement of that rule and the audit that exists to hold the two together could not see the gap, because its corpus has no key whose duplicate rows agree. Collapsing on the PROJECTED cells makes the two answers identical rather than approximate. Driven on the two rows 600739.SH's 2024 annual really arrives as -- both update_flag='1', disagreeing about total_revenue by 4.6% and agreeing exactly about n_income_attr_p -- where earnings_yield_ttm computes off the same partition sales_yield_ttm refuses, and the refusal names the column. The session axis keeps the strict rule, because no session-indexed dataset here has versions. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY IS A WHOLE-MARKET BUILD: 261 of income's 3,201 filings genuinely disagree, and one of them anywhere in the cross section still refuses the build rather than that one security, because a per-security answer would need a sixth FactorCoverage member and FACTOR_CENSUS_COLUMNS is derived from that vocabulary into the stored manifest schema, whose width is pinned; reusing one of the five would be wrong on the meaning, since input_missing says the row is not there and undefined_value says the arithmetic has no answer, where this says the publisher stated the number twice and disagreed with itself. THAT IS NOW V2-P3-018 rather than a paragraph: the review measured income's ambiguous filings at 8.2% and 8.7% on two independent samples against the 8.15% recorded, fina_indicator's recorded rate is 13.7%, and V2-P3-010's ROE reads fina_indicator.roe -- already recorded losing 5 reads in a 53-security corpus and 33 in a 76-security one -- so the next two families meet this wall sooner and harder than the value family does. EPcut IS NOT SHIPPED AND THE REASON IS FALSIFIABLE. Deducted net profit is in none of the 10 / 7 / 5 / 11 stored columns; the endpoint serves profit_dedt ITSELF, read back by adding that column to fina_indicator's projection over 101 securities, which is a stronger witness than the dt_netprofit_yoy named in KNOWN_FINANCIAL_STATEMENT_LIMITATIONS.the_merge_rule_is_agreement_in_the_projection -- so this is a projection boundary and not an upstream absence, and V2-P3-017's premise is a measurement rather than an expectation. Widening the projection is a V2-P1-011 contract change whose price is every stored partition's schema and the contract tests pinned to the field list, and NOT a re-pricing of the collapse: over one batch of rows read twice (101 securities, 4,423 filings) the folded rows (2,566), the ambiguous filings (697) and every existing column's refusals came back identical, and the 41 new refusals were profit_dedt's own. The delivered claim that adding a column would change every recorded dataset's refusal rate was a conditional read as a certainty. earnings_yield_ttm occupies the slot on RETURN_VOL_60's terms -- what EPcut reduces to when the non-recurring part cannot be subtracted -- and test_no_stored_statement_projection_carries_a_deducted_profit_column goes red the day a stored projection gains one. WHAT THIS ENTRY FIRST QUOTED WAS ARITHMETIC ON ALREADY-RECORDED TOTALS AND IS NOW MEASUREMENT: V2-P3-009's independent review re-probed the endpoint, and the three read columns' refusal rates, the comp_type split of the two revenue columns, the widened-projection A/B and the ambiguity rates above are its numbers rather than derivations from another sample's. A NON-FINITE STORED CELL NOW REFUSES THE BUILD ON BOTH AXES AND ONLY ONE AXIS FORCES IT. The period axis's collapse is built on == and nan != nan, so a byte-identical pair carrying nan would be reported as a disagreement the publisher never stated; the session axis has no collapse, so there the argument is a judgement, and the cost of being wrong is that one security's nan refuses the whole cross section where it used to cost that security alone. The two rules point opposite ways on purpose: FactorEvaluator turns a non-finite RETURN into undefined_value and _numeric refuses a non-finite CELL. A COUNT OF ONE NOW PINS ITS SPAN BOUND: FactorDefinition refuses max_window_sessions or max_window_periods above 1 beside a lookback of 1, because a one-point window spans exactly one panel point and the bound can never bind -- measured, raising earnings_yield_ttm's max_window_sessions from 1 to 50 and book_to_price's max_window_periods from 1 to 8 turned only the declaration tests red and left the engine and integration suites green, so two behaviourally identical factors carried two different factor_ids. It is a validator and not a field, so no stored factor_id moves and none of the twelve shipped ones did. MUTATIONS: the delivered implementation's were confirmed red at delivery, and this correction adds four of its own, each confirmed to turn a test red -- sales_yield_ttm's column pointed at revenue, and the count-of-one span rule removed, weakened to 'above 8' and over-tightened to 'at or above 1'.

feature_name: Factor family two, quality: ROE / ROIC / gross-margin stability / accruals, on the report-period axis alone
feature_description: Four quality factors on the report-period axis ALONE -- the first shipped factors whose lookback_sessions is None, so compute_factor forms an empty session window and every reach question is decided on the fiscal-quarter grid. return_on_equity_ttm is trailing income.n_income_attr_p over balancesheet.total_hldr_eqy_exc_min_int at the window's last period; return_on_capital_ttm is trailing income.n_income over capital employed (total_assets less total_cur_liab); gross_margin_stability is the sample standard deviation of four trailing-twelve-month gross margins off eight contiguous filings; accruals_ttm is trailing n_income less trailing cashflow.n_cashflow_act over total_assets. The window a factor sees is the UNION of the report periods of every statement dataset it reads, so a security whose income history is whole and whose balance sheet is one period short is input_missing rather than silently short a term. ROE is COMPUTED and deliberately NOT fina_indicator.roe; ROIC and the margin stability are input_missing for banks, insurers and brokers by construction.
notes: ROE IS COMPUTED RATHER THAN READ, AND THE DECIDING REASON IS NOT V2-P3-009's. That issue refused the published pe / pb / ps because inverting a multiple scores the upstream's arithmetic; that applies here too and is not decisive. What is: a published ROE is a CUMULATIVE-PERIOD return -- three months of profit over equity at Q1, nine at Q3 -- and no arithmetic converts it to a trailing one, because the cumulative-to-TTM identity is an identity about SUMS and a ratio is not a sum. roe[P] + roe[December] - roe[P-4] has three different denominators and is the trailing return on equity of nothing. Measured on the live endpoint 2026-08-13: 600519.SH's roe reads 10.5688 / 19.2038 / 26.8330 / 38.4283 at its four 2024 periods, and each quarter's share of the annual (0.275 / 0.500 / 0.698) tracks the cumulative profit's share (0.279 / 0.484 / 0.705) to within 0.02. SECOND REASON: the formula behind the served number is unstated and unreproducible from this projection -- against the closing-equity computation n_income_attr_p / total_hldr_eqy_exc_min_int the published annual figure is out by 2.0-9.5% over 600519.SH's eight most recent annuals, 2.3-11.7% over 000001.SZ's and 1.4-36.7% over 000002.SZ's, whose 2025 annual is -55.4220 published against -75.7507 computed; and fina_indicator carries NEITHER a profit column NOR an equity column, so a reader holding only that endpoint has nothing to reconcile against. THIRD: fina_indicator has no update_flag, no f_ann_date and no report_type, 81.7% of its keys carry more than one row, and the two versions of 603049.SH's 2024 annual give roe as 23.9249 and as 176.0751. A FOURTH ARGUMENT WAS WRITTEN, MEASURED AND FALSIFIED IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS, AND IS KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED: the refusal exposure of the computed route is WORSE. Over two disjoint live samples (93 + 92 = 185 securities, all four endpoints paged to exhaustion, collapsed on the stored projection) fina_indicator.roe's versions disagree on 29 of 10,865 filings (0.267%) against 24 of 10,595 (0.227%) for income.n_income_attr_p and 35 of 10,393 (0.337%) for balancesheet.total_hldr_eqy_exc_min_int -- and this factor reads BOTH of the latter over FIVE contiguous periods where the served column is one read at one period. That cost is paid for the first three reasons and is stated rather than hidden. THE PROBE FALSIFIED BOTH RECORDED ZEROS THIS FAMILY DEPENDS ON. domain/financial_statements.py records balancesheet.total_assets losing 0 reads in a 53-security corpus and cashflow.n_cashflow_act losing 0 over 14,245 field reads, and says in its own voice that 'the 0 is the one to distrust'. Measured: total_assets 35 of 10,393 (0.337%), n_cashflow_act 5 of 9,602 (0.052%) -- the fourth and fifth time this repository has watched a 0 move. The endpoint rates came back income 8.51% / balancesheet 0.95% / cashflow 17.11% / fina_indicator 11.80% against a recorded 8.15 / 1.29 / 15.80 / 13.70, so cashflow is WORSE than recorded and accruals_ttm is the factor that reads it. Every one of V2-P3-009's review's three measured columns also came back higher here, so that set is a sample property in the same way the derived bounds it replaced were. ROIC'S TWO MISSING TERMS ARE PRICED RATHER THAN ELIDED. The textbook numerator is EBIT * (1 - t) and income.ebit is unusable at 888 of 10,595 filings (8.38%, and 258 of income's 288 refused reads on the recorded corpus), with a worst case of -7,579,086 against +3,427,524 for one 603333.SH filing; no stored column carries interest expense, so the add-back cannot be reconstructed. n_income is total_profit less income_tax -- MEASURED, not read off the statement's shape: over six securities the identity holds on every period from 2007 onward (446 rows, worst relative residual 8.9e-7, five of the six at machine precision) and fails before it (000001.SZ 2005H1 by 31.5%, 000002.SZ 1996H1 by 5.9%, which is the pre-2007 CAS under which net profit was already net of minority interest). So the missing term is exactly the after-tax net interest, this factor understates a NOPAT-based ROIC by it, and the understatement is largest for the most leveraged names. The denominator should be total assets less the NON-interest-bearing current liabilities and this projection carries no such split, so capital employed is the widest base it can state exactly -- which is why the numerator is the CONSOLIDATED n_income and not n_income_attr_p. THE EIGHT-PERIOD WINDOW IS WHERE V2-P3-009's TTM HELPER STOPS APPLYING, AND ITS FAILURE MODE THERE IS NOT FAIL-CLOSED. The identity finds the fiscal year end inside periods[:-1] and refuses unless there is exactly one; periods[:-1] of a contiguous eight is SEVEN consecutive quarters, which holds two year ends when the window ends at Q1, Q2 or Q3 (refused) and exactly ONE when it ends at Q4, where it returns the true trailing twelve months PLUS a whole extra fiscal year less that year's first quarter. So the identity is applied to five-period SLICES of the eight -- four of them at four consecutive quarter ends -- and each slice's own periods[:-1] is four CONSECUTIVE quarters, of which exactly one ends a year at every alignment. All four alignments are enumerated, including the wrong number. THE MARGIN IS TRAILING AND THE STATISTIC IS A STANDARD DEVIATION, both against named alternatives: a cumulative-as-filed margin mixes a three-month with a nine-month horizon, a single-quarter series is dominated by seasonality by construction, and a coefficient of variation would divide by a mean that can be near zero or negative and rank the most erratic loss-maker below every stable name. Four observations is the fewest at which a Bessel-corrected estimator is doing what its name says, and each further one costs a contiguous filing whose ambiguity refuses the whole build (V2-P3-018). ACCRUALS TAKE THE CASH-FLOW CONSTRUCTION because the balance-sheet one is provably contaminated here: the change in non-cash working capital would need total_cur_liab with its short-term borrowings removed and no stored column removes them, while the depreciation add-back is in none of them either. free_cashflow is refused on the census alone -- every one of the 1,643 ambiguous cashflow filings in 185 securities disagrees about it. A DENOMINATOR GETS THE SIGN RULE A NUMERATOR DOES NOT, ON THE SAME COLUMN: book_to_price reports an insolvent issuer's negative equity as computed and negative, return_on_equity_ttm reports the same equity as undefined_value, because a negative denominator turns a profit into a negative return and a loss into a positive one and inverts the ordering the cross section is built on. TWO OF THE FOUR ARE BLIND TO FINANCIAL ISSUERS, MEASURED: over every stored period since 2015, total_cur_liab is null on 68 of 68 of 000001.SZ's balance sheets, 67 of 67 of 601318.SH's and 64 of 64 of 600030.SH's, and oper_cost on 59 of 59, 57 of 57 and 56 of 56 of their income rows, while two comp_type=1 industrials carry both populated on 0 of 62 and 0 of 63 null. So return_on_capital_ttm and gross_margin_stability answer input_missing for banks, insurers and brokers -- the right answer for a company type whose capital employed and gross margin are not defined quantities -- and the other two compute for the same security in the same build. ONE IDENTITY TIES THIS FAMILY TO V2-P3-009's: earnings_yield_ttm / book_to_price IS return_on_equity_ttm, because the market capitalisation cancels, and that is why the denominator is the window's closing equity rather than the average of its ends -- an averaged denominator would put two incompatible statements of what a book value is inside one build. The bias it buys has a direction and is disclosed: closing equity exceeds average equity for an issuer that raised capital during the year, so this ROE reads lower than the textbook one for the names that grew equity fastest. The identity is held through the real engine over three windows of three different reaches. MUTATIONS: eighteen of the implementation, each confirmed to turn a test red -- see the commit message.

feature_name: Factor family three, growth: revenue and net-profit year-on-year and revenue acceleration, on the report-period axis alone
feature_description: V2-P3-011's three definitions and their evaluators: revenue_yoy (income.total_revenue at the newest report period knowable at as_of over the same column four quarters earlier, less one), net_profit_yoy (the same on income.n_income_attr_p) and revenue_yoy_acceleration (the newest revenue year-on-year less the same rate four quarters earlier). All three declare family growth, direction higher_is_better, NO session reach at all and a report-period reach of 5/5 for the two plain rates and 9/9 for the acceleration. They are the FIRST factors this build ships that read a filing and nothing else: V2-P3-009's value family opened the report-period axis alongside a price, and lookback_sessions=None had no production reader until these. A cumulative A-share figure four quarters back is the same span of the same fiscal year, so the ratio is a year-on-year with no accumulation and this family calls _trailing_twelve_months nowhere.
notes: SEVEN JUDGEMENTS, EACH MEASURED OR DECLARED WITH ITS COST. (1) THE YEAR-ON-YEAR IS CUMULATIVE OVER CUMULATIVE AND NOT TTM OVER TTM. A-share statements accumulate inside the calendar fiscal year, so cumulative[P] and cumulative[P - 4 quarters] cover the SAME span of the same fiscal year -- nine months against nine at Q3, twelve against twelve at the annual -- and the seasonality V2-P3-009's trailing sum exists to remove is already cancelled by the two sides covering the same months. What that does NOT buy is one horizon across the cross section, and the two are deliberately not run together: EARNINGS_YIELD_TTM accumulates because a LEVEL read at one as_of mixes three months of one issuer's profit with twelve of another's, which is not a comparison at all, while a ratio of two same-span figures is a comparison whichever span it is. A TTM-over-TTM year-on-year would make every security's horizon twelve months at the cost of a nine-period reach for the plain rate and a thirteen-period one for the acceleration; the trade is taken the other way and the residual heterogeneity is disclosed in every one of the three shipped notes and driven on a partition where one security's newest filing is a Q1 and another's is the annual. (2) THIS FAMILY CALLS _trailing_twelve_months NOWHERE, AND THAT IS A CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN A SIMPLIFICATION. That helper finds its December by searching window.periods[:-1], and how many year ends the slice holds is a function of the reach AND of where the window ends: [:-1] is N-1 consecutive quarters, and K consecutive quarters hold K//4 or K//4+1 year ends depending on the alignment. At N=5 it is four quarters and therefore exactly one in all four alignments, which is what V2-P3-009's identity rests on. At N=8 it is seven, which is ONE OR TWO -- so a reader who reuses it there gets None for three alignments and a confident WRONG NUMBER for the fourth, built from the previous year's December: the true trailing twelve months plus a whole fiscal year less that year's Q1. On this repository's own fixture that is 1,212 + 1,134 - 131 = 2,215 against a true 1,212, and it is asserted as the literal EIGHT_PERIOD_WRONG_TRAILING_SUM with all four alignments driven, because 'not equal to the right answer' is the assertion shape this repository has been caught by five times. At N=9 the slice is eight quarters, exactly two calendar years, so the helper answers None in every alignment -- but that is nine being odd about a four-cycle rather than a guard anybody wrote, and a family relying on it would be relying on an arithmetic coincidence. _year_on_year reads two cells at a FIXED index offset and searches for nothing, so it has no alignment behaviour at all, and every assertion about its arithmetic is parametrised over the four alignments. (3) THE ONLY THING BETWEEN THIS FACTOR AND A WRONG NUMBER IS max_window_periods == lookback_periods, AND THE NUMBER IS PINNED. The evaluator cannot see the periods, so on a gapped window it compares three months of one year against twelve of another and answers rather than refusing. Handed the 000063.SZ shape directly -- five filings spanning six quarters, the December missing -- it reports -84.7% where the true 2025Q1-over-2024Q1 growth is +14.6%: not a blur but a reversed sign at five times the magnitude. Both numbers are asserted by value, and the engine's refusal of that window is driven end to end beside a security that is short on the COUNT at an unbroken span, so the two bounds are separable on one partition. (4) A YEAR-EARLIER BASE THAT IS NOT STRICTLY POSITIVE IS undefined_value, AND THE ARGUMENT IS AN ORDERING RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. The derivative of num/base - 1 in num is 1/base, so at a negative base the ratio is monotonically DECREASING in this year's outcome. On three real securities from the live probe the refused arithmetic produces exactly the reverse of the ranking a growth factor exists to produce: 002714.SZ swung from a 2,779,217,657.24 loss to an 829,288,208.44 profit and scores -129.8%, 000506.SZ narrowed its loss and scores -32.7%, and 002921.SZ deepened its loss by a factor of 10.8 and scores +976.6%, which would put it at the TOP of a higher_is_better cross section. Dividing by abs(base) instead is refused rather than adopted: it scores a swing from -1 to +1 at +2.0, the same as a rise from 100 to 300, and nothing measured here says those belong at one rank. _market_capitalisation refuses a non-positive denominator in the same module on the same stated argument. (5) n_income_attr_p AND NOT n_income, ARGUED AGAIN RATHER THAN INHERITED. earnings_yield_ttm chooses the attributable column because total_mv prices the parent's shares -- a PAIRING argument -- and this factor has no price in it at all, so that argument is silent and the choice has to be remade. Consolidation is what the two columns are defined by: a newly bought 51% subsidiary contributes ALL of its profit to n_income and 51% to n_income_attr_p, so a growth rate on the consolidated column reads an ownership event as operating growth at about twice the size a holder of one listed share experienced. Which of consolidation and buying out a minority is commoner in this market is NOT measured and no claim is made about it. What IS measured is the thing a fixture cannot decide: a growth rate divides a CONSTANT scale out, so 600739.SH's 2024 annual carrying n_income 664,195,391.66 against n_income_attr_p 209,556,865.25 -- a factor of 3.169 -- settles nothing about the RATES, and the live probe puts the two columns' rates apart on 139 of the 181 (security, as_of) pairs that have a comparable pair, 76.8%. Three are asserted by magnitude: 002023.SZ's consolidated growth is 2.09 times its attributable one, 000931.SZ's runs the other way at 6.6% against 2.5%, and 002314.SZ's are -563.8% against -128.1%. The integration partition therefore moves every neighbouring column by a DRIFTING ratio, because V2-P3-009's own partition -- revenue at a flat half of total_revenue, n_income at a flat 1.7 of n_income_attr_p -- would have given a mis-wired growth factor the identical number. (6) THE ACCELERATION IS A DIFFERENCE OF TWO RATES A YEAR APART, ON REVENUE, AT NINE PERIODS. Not a year-on-year of a year-on-year: the quotient reading (1+g_now)/(1+g_then)-1 has 1+g_then in its denominator, which crosses zero at a 100% contraction and is sign-inverted past it, while a difference is defined wherever both rates are and is in the units both are in. The two rates are a YEAR apart and not a quarter apart, which is what makes the reach nine rather than six: on cumulative figures YoY(Q3) is a nine-month growth and YoY(H1) a six-month one, so differencing adjacent periods mixes acceleration with a change of horizon. Revenue and not net profit because this construction needs TWO positive bases where a plain rate needs one -- measured at 61 of 220 nine-period windows undefined on n_income_attr_p (27.7%) against 0 of 220 on total_revenue. The degeneracy that would make it its own first term (a zero earlier rate) is asserted absent, and 0 of 220 real windows produced it. (7) DIRECTION IS THE CONVENTIONAL PRIOR AND NOTHING HERE HAS MEASURED IT. All three declare higher_is_better; the shared sentence says a negative IC would be a result rather than a bug and declines to characterise the prior's strength at all, because a sentence about what the literature finds for growth would be prose this repository cannot falsify. THE LIVE PROBE, AND WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT QUOTED RATES. Two DISJOINT 60-security stride samples of the 5,543 listed securities (step 92, offsets 0 and 45, zero overlap), every income filing announced 2016-2026 (4,359 filings) resolved under this engine's own rules -- later announcement wins, same-day rows collapse when the projected cells agree and refuse per column when they do not -- evaluated at 2024-06-30 and 2025-06-30 for 240 (security, as_of) pairs. Reach: 240/240 form a one-period window, 230/240 a five-period one, 220/240 a nine-period one, so 9/9 costs 10 of the 230 the plain rate scores, 4.3% -- 2 of 116 at the later as_of and 8 of 114 at the earlier, which is what a reach measured against listing dates rather than against gaps looks like, and smaller than the shape of 'two years and a quarter with no gap' suggests because an A-share issuer that files at all files every quarter. Non-positive year-earlier base: 49/230 on n_income_attr_p (21.3%) against 0/230 on total_revenue. AND THE TWO COLUMNS' RECORDED REFUSAL RATES ARE BOTH HIGHER ON THE WIDER SAMPLE: total_revenue refused 17 of 4,359 filings (0.390%) against the 0.123% V2-P3-009's review recorded, 3.2x, and n_income_attr_p 20 of 4,359 (0.459%) against 0.189%, 2.4x. Neither changes a decision here and both remain small; what they change is the standing of any QUOTED refusal rate, which is domain/financial_statements.py's own 'how little is a property of the sample and not of the dataset' landing a second time. The concentration is confirmed rather than disturbed: ebit alone refuses 595 of the 599 ambiguous filings in the same corpus, 13.65% of it, and this family reads none of the pooled columns. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY IS A WHOLE-MARKET BUILD, for V2-P3-009's reason unchanged: an income filing whose duplicate rows genuinely disagree still refuses the entire cross section rather than that one security, which is V2-P3-018. MUTATIONS: sixteen mutations of the implementation were each confirmed to turn the new tests red -- the year-on-year offset moved from four quarters to one, the base guard narrowed to zero only, the base guard replaced by abs(base), the ratio returned without subtracting one, the acceleration differencing adjacent periods, its difference reversed, its earlier term pointed at the newest period, its refusal weakened to answer the recent rate alone, each numerator pointed at its neighbouring column, either reach moved, either span bound relaxed above its count, QUARTERS_PER_YEAR set to two, a flipped direction and a mis-declared family. Nine of them were re-run against the INTEGRATION file alone; eight were caught there too and one survived -- the acceleration answering its recent rate when the earlier one is undefined -- because no security on the partition had a non-positive base at window[-9] alone. A security with exactly that shape was added and the mutant is now caught end to end.

feature_name: Quantile portfolio returns with real A-share round-trip costs, joined from the label contract's return and the execution policy's fees
feature_description: V2-P3-006's grouped portfolio returns as a standard-library leaf module over V2-P3-005's own ICCrossSection, so an IC and a spread are measured on exactly the same admitted set and cannot be reconciled by pointing at different samples. THE JOIN IS A DIVISION OF AUTHORITY AND NOT AN AVERAGING TRICK: the gross return of a position is OutcomeLabel.realized_return (WindowReturn.adjusted) and is never recomputed from the two fills, because a fill is at MarketBar.close and a round trip priced from two published closes is close_exit/close_entry -- the path domain/daily_prices.py measured at -0.530973% where the truth is +2.742251%, sign reversed; the fees are two ExecutionResults from AShareExecutionPolicy at a declared position capital, so the board lot, the STAR 200-share floor and the 5-yuan minimum commission are live rather than assumed away; and whether a position exists at all is decided by BOTH contracts, label first, because domain/labels.py refuses halts, limit locks, unpublished bands, missing bars and all three registry verdicts across every session of the window while the policy sees one bar. A refused order NEVER becomes a zero return: it leaves its group and is counted under its own HoldingOutcome, and PortfolioCensus requires held + every excluded cell + unattempted to total the securities the cross section offered. The cut is by average rank so tied values share a group whatever order they arrived in, group_count and min_securities_per_group are declared with no default, and an empty group is one of three coverage codes rather than a repair -- degenerate_scores (the factor), unfillable_groups (its ties against the declared cut) and unfillable_after_execution (the market). Group indices stay ascending in the RAW factor value and direction decides only which group is long, so long_short_spread is the exact negation of raw_spread under lower_is_better. The spread is published and is NOT a portfolio: there is no short side in AShareExecutionPolicy, no borrow cost anywhere in this repository, and a short round trip is exactly the pair of verdicts KNOWN_EXECUTION_LIMITATIONS already measures the policy and the label as disagreeing on. No cumulative curve and no annualisation are published, for the reason V2-P3-005 publishes no t-statistic: overlapping windows make compounding count one session's move several times.
notes: SIX QUESTIONS THIS ISSUE HAD TO ANSWER EXPLICITLY. (1) HOW THE GROUPS ARE CUT. By quantile of factor value, through factor_ic.average_ranks, so two securities with the same value share a rank and therefore a group whatever order the caller passed them in -- a sort-and-slice implementation makes the boundary a function of the sort's tie-break, and a discretised factor ties constantly. group_count is DECLARED with no default and a floor of 2 (a spread over one group is identically zero for every factor), and so is min_securities_per_group. Ten deciles of seven securities is insufficient_sample, reported with the counts, not three empty groups: this repository has taken eight Critical findings on narrow-sample calibration. (2) HOW THE PORTFOLIO IS BUILT. Equal declared budget per position, lot-rounded (100 shares off STAR, any count from 200 on it), and the group return is sum(net_proceeds)/sum(entry_outlay) - 1 -- what the group actually returned on the money it actually spent, which is the only reading under which A-share lot rounding is visible rather than assumed away. Equal NOTIONAL is not constructible: a 300-yuan security's smallest position is 30,000 yuan and a 3-yuan one's is 300. There is no rebalancing: one as_of is one round trip over the label's own window, so the rebalance frequency is entirely the caller's choice of as_of spacing and horizon and turnover is 100% per period by construction, which makes the reported fees an upper bound relative to V2-P3-007's rolling portfolio. (3) HOW THE COSTS GET IN. AShareExecutionPolicy is per-order and a group return is per-portfolio, and the join is that the policy supplies the MONEY (two ExecutionResults per position, a buy at the entry bar and a sell at the exit bar) while domain/labels.py supplies the MOVE. entry_outlay = notional + buy fees; gross_value = notional * (1 + realized_return); net_proceeds = gross_value - sell fees. With a constant adjustment factor gross_value and the sell leg's notional are the same number TO THE CENT, and they part on an ex-rights window in the correct direction -- a cash dividend arrives as cash and pays no stamp duty.
